jobs.title: Director, Business Analytics and Insights
jobs.description:
At CI, we see a great place to work as one that is a safe place for everyone to have a voice, where people are empowered to take ownership over meaningful work, where there is an opportunity to grow through stretching themselves, where they can work on innovative products and projects, and where employees are supported and engaged in doing so.  

CI Financial is seeking a dynamic and visionary leader to join our D&A team as the Director of Business Analytics and Insights. In this pivotal role, you will drive strategic initiatives that enhance business performance and stakeholder engagement by combining strong business partnership, data-driven insights, and practical application of AI-enabled analytics. You will lead a talented analytics team to deliver impactful solutions, identify opportunities to automate and scale insight generation, and ensure analytics capabilities align with our company's goals and values. 

 Director of Business Analytics & Insights 

 CI Financial is seeking a dynamic and visionary leader to join our D&A team as the Director of Business Analytics and Insights. In this pivotal role, you will drive strategic initiatives that enhance business performance and stakeholder engagement by combining strong business partnership, data-driven insights, and practical application of AI-enabled analytics. You will lead a talented analytics team to deliver impactful solutions, identify opportunities to automate and scale insight generation, and ensure analytics capabilities align with our company's goals and values.

 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: 

 Team Leadership: Lead and manage a team of business analytics professionals to deliver high-quality insights and actionable recommendations to business stakeholders and partners.
 Strategic leadership: Collaborate with business leaders and partners to understand priorities, challenges, and opportunities, using data to guide strategies that improve effectiveness, engagement, and outcomes. Develop and manage analytics strategies that provide actionable insights for key stakeholders, focusing on performance tracking, engagement, and growth opportunities.
 Stakeholder Management: Develop and maintain strong relationships with key stakeholders within the organization to ensure alignment and collaboration on business objectives.
 Communication skills: Present findings, insights, and recommendations to senior leadership and other key stakeholders in a clear and compelling manner, translating complex data into actionable reports and strategic plans.
 Performance Management: Establish and track key performance indicators (KPIs) and relevant metrics to measure business performance, engagement, and operational activities. Continuously monitor, create dashboards, and report on these metrics, providing actionable insights to optimize outcomes.
 D&A and AI Transformation: Drive the adoption of analytics, automation, and AI-enabled tools that enhance data accessibility, visualization, reporting, and decision support. Work closely with IT and D&A functions (i.e. data engineering, data governance, data operations) to ensure high data quality, appropriate controls, and compliance.
 AI Enablement and Innovation: Identify, prioritize, and help implement AI use cases that improve business analytics, automate manual reporting, accelerate insight generation, and support more proactive decision-making across stakeholder groups and business partners.
 Continuous Improvement: Continuously identify opportunities for process improvement, automation, and innovation within the analytics function, including ways to use AI to reduce manual effort and improve speed, consistency, and quality of insights.
 Technical Expertise: Stay abreast of industry trends, emerging technologies, and best practices in business analytics, AI, automation, and data products.
 AI Experimentation & Rapid Prototyping: Foster a culture of innovation by actively exploring emerging AI technologies, analytics tools, and automation capabilities. Roll up your sleeves to rapidly prototype, test, and validate new ideas, translating promising concepts into practical business solutions and scalable capabilities.
 Platform & Solution Development: Partner with technical teams and, where appropriate, directly contribute to the development of analytics products, AI-enabled tools, web applications, and user-facing solutions that improve access to data, insights, and decision support.

 Qualifications 
 7+ years of experience in business analytics and business intelligence within a B2B environment, ideally in financial services or asset management.
 Technical degree in Computer Science, Mathematics, Statistics, or related field.
 Proficiency in data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI), statistical software (e.g., Python), and CRM platforms (e.g., Salesforce); with a s trong working knowledge and understanding of SQL. 
 Demonstrated curiosity and hands-on experience evaluating, prototyping, and applying emerging AI, automation, and productivity technologies to solve business problems and drive innovation.
 Experience with cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure) and modern data architectures. 
 Exceptional leadership and people management abilities, with a focus on fostering a collaborative and results-driven team culture.
 Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills
 Effective communication and stakeholder management skills, capable of conveying complex data and insights to executive teams, business leaders, and partners.

 Preferred Qualifications 
 Experience developing user-facing analytics products, including web applications, AI-enabled tools, portals, or self-service solutions using technologies such as React, Streamlit, Power Apps, or equivalent frameworks, is an asset.
 Knowledge of asset management, financial services, or wealth management industries, with an understanding of business partner needs, engagement models, and product priorities.
 Experience leading AI-enabled analytics initiatives or partnering with technical teams to translate business needs into practical AI solutions.

 CI Financial is an independent company offering global wealth management and asset management advisory services through diverse financial services firms. Since 1965, we have consistently anticipated and responded to the changing needs of investors. We are driven by a commitment to provide individuals and institutions with the highest-quality investments and advice.   Our commitment to the highest levels of performance means that whatever their position, CI employees must be comfortable in a fast-paced environment that will stretch them to tap into their highest potential.  Employees with a healthy dose of ambition, a desire to commit to a curious mindset for continuous learning, and a willingness to go the extra mile thrive at CI.  

 A Supportive Environment for Success 
 We offer an in-office environment, competitive benefits, and a supportive workplace to help our employees thrive both personally and professionally.

 Modern HQ location within walking distance from Union Station 
 Training Reimbursement 
 Paid Professional Designations 
 Employee Savings Plan (ESP)

 Enhanced group benefits

 Paid time off for Volunteering

jobs.description:
At CI, we see a great place to work as one that is a safe place for everyone to have a voice, where people are empowered to take ownership over meaningful work, where there is an opportunity to grow through stretching themselves, where they can work on innovative products and projects, and where employees are supported and engaged in doing so.  

CI Financial is seeking a Director, Insurance Operations to lead the modernization and ongoing performance of our Canadian individual life insurance Operations function.

This role combines daily operational leadership with a significant transformation mandate. You will strengthen case progression and carrier advocacy, build actionable Operations Intelligence, improve operational data and technology, develop differentiated advisor service, and lead an established team through sustained change.

This opportunity is suited to an insurance operations leader who has personally delivered meaningful change while remaining accountable for people, service quality, and daily results. 

 What You Will Do: 
 Lead the daily performance and modernization of Insurance Operations.
 Assess current services, processes, systems, operational data, capacity, and cross-functional handoffs.
 Lead the development and phased implementation of an approved future operating model aligned with CI’s insurance growth, advisor-support, and client-service priorities.
 Build Operations Intelligence that turns pipeline progression, aging, service levels, capacity, carrier performance, and financial information into clear actions and decision-ready recommendations.
 Strengthen case ownership, underwriting follow-up, carrier advocacy, escalation, delivery, placement, and oversight of complex, high-value, or aging cases.
 Develop practical pre-submission navigation and complex-case routing while preserving clear boundaries between operational support, insurance advice, and underwriting authority.
 Design differentiated advisor and in-force service models, including enhanced support where internal involvement adds meaningful value.
 Define operational technology, data, automation, and self-service requirements in partnership with Technology teams and vendors.
 Deliver practical improvements within the current operating environment while longer-term modernization work proceeds.
 Assess future capability requirements and recommend the team design, development priorities, and resources required to deliver the approved operating model.

 Specific modernization priorities, sequencing, performance measures, and resource requirements will reflect the operating baseline, business priorities, available resources, and appropriate approval processes.

 What You Bring: 
 At least 7 years of progressive experience specifically in Canadian individual life insurance Operations, including a minimum of 3 years in a formal operational people-leadership role with direct accountability for people, workload, service quality, capacity, priorities, and escalations.
 Strong knowledge of Canadian individual life insurance products, carrier practices, application processing, underwriting requirements, medical and financial evidence, issue, delivery, placement, and in-force servicing.
 Proven experience modernizing an operation while continuing to deliver effective daily service.
 Experience implementing meaningful process, service, data, or technology improvements that achieved sustained adoption and measurable results.
 Strong analytical and commercial judgment, including the ability to challenge incomplete data, establish credible measures, and translate findings into action.
 Practical experience defining business requirements and working with Technology teams or vendors through assessment, testing, implementation, adoption, and post-launch improvement.
 Experience leading an established team through material change with respect, clarity, and accountability.

 Bilingual English and French capability is preferred but not required. CLU, MBA, or relevant insurance, business, operations, technology, or change-management credentials are considered assets.

 What Will Make You Successful 
 You are equally comfortable reviewing an aging case queue, challenging unreliable reporting, working with carriers, coaching experienced employees, and presenting recommendations to senior leadership.
 You can modernize an operation without losing control of daily service.
 You create useful intelligence from imperfect data rather than waiting for perfect systems.
 You simplify and clarify processes before attempting to automate them.
 You respect institutional knowledge while challenging practices that no longer serve the business.
 You understand that launching a change is not the same as achieving sustained adoption.

 Why This Role Is Different 
 This role combines leadership of an established operation with the opportunity to define and implement its next stage.
 You will help build stronger operational intelligence, improve case progression, modernize technology and data, develop differentiated service, and strengthen the capabilities required for the future.
 Candidates may currently hold a Director or Senior Manager role. Demonstrated scope, operational accountability, and evidence of sustained delivery will matter more than current title or employer type.
 Relevant experience may come from an MGA, national insurance account, life insurer, wealth-management insurance operation, or insurance transformation role with prior operational accountability.

 The Operating Model You Will Help Build 
 The role will help establish stronger operational visibility, case ownership and escalation, differentiated advisor support, practical pre-submission navigation, and priority process and data improvements.
 The specific sequence will reflect the operating baseline, business priorities, cross-functional dependencies, and approved resources. Success will be visible in how the operation performs, how the team works, and how consistently improvements are used in daily practice.

 Work Arrangement 
 Occasional travel may be required based on business needs.
 This role follows our in office work model and requires employees to be onsite four days per week to support collaboration and business needs.

 This opportunity is for an existing vacancy with the company. The anticipated base salary range for this position is $93,000 to $130,000. Exact salary depends on several factors such as experience, skills, education, and budget. Salary range may vary based on geographic location. In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for participation in a bonus program. In addition, The Company offers a variety of benefits to eligible employees, including health insurance coverage, wellness programs, life and disability insurance, retirement savings plans, paid leave programs, education-related programs, paid holidays and vacation time, and many others. Many of these benefits are subsidized or fully paid for by the company.

Since 1965, we have consistently anticipated and responded to the changing needs of investors. We are driven by a commitment to provide individuals and institutions with the highest-quality investments and advice.   Our commitment to the highest levels of performance means that whatever their position, CI employees must be comfortable in a fast-paced environment that will stretch them to tap into their highest potential.  Employees with a healthy dose of ambition, a desire to commit to a curious mindset for continuous learning, and a willingness to go the extra mile thrive at CI.

jobs.title: Director, Internal Controls
jobs.description:
At CI, we see a great place to work as one that is a safe place for everyone to have a voice, where people are empowered to take ownership over meaningful work, where there is an opportunity to grow through stretching themselves, where they can work on innovative products and projects, and where employees are supported and engaged in doing so.  

This is a high-visibility leadership role offering the opportunity to maintain and execute the control frameworks while working closely with executive leadership. You'll act as a trusted advisor across the organization, helping shape governance practices, enhance operational transparency, and ensure compliance in a fast-evolving, highly regulated environment. The ideal candidate thrives in dynamic settings and brings a balance of strategic thinking and hands-on execution. 

 The Director of internal controls ensures the integrity, efficiency, and effectiveness of the companies’ internal controls, policies, systems, and procedures. The role serves as a strategic partner to management, delivering independent, objective assurance and advisory services that support accountability, transparency, and continuous improvement across the organization. The ideal candidate is expected to apply a risk-based, value-added approach that aligns with international audit standards, strengthens governance, and upholds compliance with regulatory, contractual, and corporate-specific requirements.
 The Director of Internal Controls will be based at CI’s head office 15 York Street, Toronto, Ontario, and will oversee a team and internal control specialists and external consultants.

 WHAT YOU WILL DO: 
 Liaison between the company, internal audit, external audit, and Mubadala Capital (CI’s parent) in corporate audit projects.
 Ensure the effectiveness of CI’s internal controls over financial reporting (“ICFR”) by maintaining and executing the ICFR program.
 Support internal and external auditors in their audit duties – ensure all requests are delivered in line with agreed timetable.
 Ensure appropriate interpretation and implementation of required changes in a timely manner.
 Support all internal and external audit activities through the provision of required documentation when necessary.
 Undertake special assignments or cross-functional reviews to support organizational improvement and strategic decision-making.
 Stay current with industry leading trends, best practices, SOX requirements and all internal, legislative, and industry best practice.
 Working closely with the Management Team and the Compliance department, evaluate the design and effectiveness of internal controls, jurisdictional internal control matrices, policies, and procedures to safeguard assets, promote operational efficiency, and ensure compliance with organizational and corporate requirements.
 Conduct management testing over financial, operational, compliance, and IT controls across the organization to assess the strength of implemented controls.
 Conduct sample checks as part of the ICFR program to provide assurance over controls and risk mitigation measures, including sustainability of controls implemented by business management to address audit issues.
 Support activities related to the company's assessment of Internal Controls Over Financial Reporting (ICFR), including conducting IT process walkthroughs, testing, and summarization of results to support the ICFR program.
 Leading the management testing program areas such as scoping, scheduling, stakeholder management, workpaper review, etc., in communication with relevant stakeholders.
 Ensure that documentation supporting audit testing is sufficient, competent, and relevant to support conclusions.
 Identify risk, controls and process weaknesses, document main control points and provide evidential support for report recommendation.
 Propose value-added recommendations to address control weakness and/or process inefficiencies identified.
 Monitor management’s implementation of audit recommendations and maintain a tracking system to ensure timely resolution and accountability.
 Prepare and present reports with well-documented observations, risk ratings, and practical recommendations to Management and the Compliance Committee.
 Elevate the importance of internal controls through training and technical assistance on internal controls, risk management, compliance, and audit readiness, and coach team through the methods for evidence and retaining evidence of controls.
 Provide advisory services on internal control design, process improvement, and risk mitigation strategies for new systems, processes, or projects.
 Continue to build Floqast, CI’s risk compliance tool, to be best-in-class to maximize efficiencies from the tool.

 WHAT YOU WILL BRING: 
 Bachelor's Degree in Accounting, Finance, Internal Audit or any other related fields.
 CPA credential with a minimum of 6 - 10 years of audit experience in public accounting and/or internal audit, controls including effective root-cause analysis.
 At least 2 – 3 years of leadership experience.
 Self-driven and self-managed with the ability to work independently, prioritize tasks, and meet established deadlines.
 Strong project management skills.
 Preferred but not required: CISA or CIA Credentials.
 Fundamental understanding of core Information Technology processes and systems.
 Knowledge of internal control concepts and frameworks (COSO), Sarbanes-Oxley standards, and auditing processes.
 Extensive experience in auditing Sarbanes Oxley (SOX) IT General Controls (ITGC), IT Automated Controls (ITAC), including testing the completeness and accuracy (C&A) of key reports supporting business processes.
 Experience with testing various systems and technologies, such as ERP systems, cloud technologies, and other enterprise applications.
 Strong attention to detail and accuracy in data validation and record keeping.
 Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate and resolve discrepancies.
 Strong interpersonal and influencing skills and communication, reports and/or analytics, internal controls, compliance controls, knowledge and exposed to IT, back office and/or marketing operations, preferably in the online gaming industry.
 Superior written and verbal communication, listening and presentation skills to effectively communicate with individuals at all levels of an organization.
 Exceptional interpersonal, negotiating and influencing skills to achieve win-win solutions.
 Demonstrated leadership and strong commitment to collaboration and teamwork with proven success inspiring teams to high levels of performance and engagement.
 Proficient with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint).

 Personal Attributes 
 Team player, collaborative, approachable, supportive, positive, open, patient, diplomatic and respectful.
 A confident, proactive and results-oriented individual with the demeanor, maturity, and intellect required to quickly establish trust and credibility.
 Exceptional interpersonal, listening, and conflict management skills. High EQ and self-awareness.
 High level of tact, discretion, and diplomacy in dealing with highly sensitive and confidential matters.
 Influencer, able to persuade others to action without absolute authority.
 Not afraid to express opinions and provide feedback in a balanced and constructive manner.
 Highest personal standards of integrity; strong work ethic, diligent, reliable and trustworthy.
 Organized, focused, and flexible in managing competing priorities; able to manage multiple complex issues, lead change management, drive multiple projects, work independently and deal with ambiguity.
 Thrives within a dynamic, fast-paced, agile, and evolving work environment.

The Director, M&A Operations is responsible for leading the operational execution of the organization's book purchase and M&A initiatives from transaction close through successful integration.

The Director serves as the central leader coordinating all execution activities, ensuring transactions progress efficiently, risks are mitigated, stakeholders remain aligned, and integration objectives are achieved.

 To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com

 Our product team brings together business, data, and technology expertise to deliver meaningful solutions that create value for clients and the business. As a Senior Director, Product Owner, you'll set the vision and direction for your Squad, ensuring priorities align with Crew strategy and broader organizational goals. You'll develop and manage a strategic product roadmap, translate complex business and client needs into clear backlog priorities, and lead release planning to deliver impactful outcomes. You'll work closely with partners across Crews, Squads, and business units to manage dependencies, resolve issues, and keep delivery on track in a complex environment. You'll also help strengthen product practices by mentoring other Product Owners, championing continuous improvement, and promoting delivery excellence across teams.

 At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. You'll have the flexibility to manage your work activities within a hybrid work arrangement where you'll spend 1-3 days per week on-site, while other days will be remote. 

 How you'll succeed 

 Product strategy and vision - Set and champion the Squad’s vision, goals, and priorities, ensuring alignment with Crew strategy and broader business objectives. Build and communicate a strategic product roadmap that maximizes client and business value.
 Backlog and delivery leadership - Build, prioritize, and manage a complex Squad backlog by translating business and client needs into actionable user stories and requirements. Lead release and delivery planning, assess outcomes, and reprioritize work to respond to changing needs.
 Risk and dependency management - Anticipate, navigate, and resolve risks, issues, and dependencies across Squads and business units. Ensure work is delivered within established frameworks, guardrails, and compliance requirements.
 Cross-functional collaboration - Partner with Crew Leads, Crew Technology Leads, Chapter Leads, Agility Coaches, Squad members, stakeholders, and external partners to drive progress and achieve shared outcomes. Build strong relationships across teams to support decision-making and delivery.
 Thought leadership and continuous improvement - Provide mentorship to other Product Owners and share best practices that strengthen product delivery across teams. Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that enhance efficiency, effectiveness, and product outcomes.

 Who you are 

 You act like an owner. You thrive when you're empowered to take initiative, go above and beyond, and deliver results.
 Your influence makes a difference. You know that relationships and networks are essential to success. You inspire outcomes by sharing your expertise.
 You give meaning to data. You enjoy investigating complex problems and making sense of information. You communicate detailed information in a meaningful way.
 You embrace and advocate for change. You continuously evolve your thinking and the way you work in order to deliver your best.
 You can demonstrate experience in product ownership, strategic roadmap development, backlog management, agile delivery, stakeholder management, and navigating complex cross-functional dependencies in data, technology, or analytics-focused environments. It’s an asset if you bring experience in decision science, machine learning, optimization, product analytics, technical strategy, or consulting.
 You have a degree/diploma in computer science, engineering, mathematics, statistics, economics, operations research, physics, or a related quantitative discipline. Equivalent experience is also valued.
 You know that details matter. You notice things that others don't. Your critical thinking skills help to inform your decision making.

jobs.title: Head of Partnerships
jobs.description:
This posting reflects a current, actively recruited opening at Float. All applications are being reviewed on a rolling basis. 

 About Float 
 Float is on a mission to simplify finance for Canadian businesses, empowering them to eliminate complexity and unlock new opportunities. Through our innovative platform, Float enables businesses to streamline financial operations and optimize cash flow, so they can focus on what matters most: growth. 

 As one of Canada’s fastest growing companies and top-rated startups in 2025, 2024 and 2023, Float is customer-obsessed, passionate and entrepreneurial, with a team that includes leaders from Uber, Stripe, Shopify, Top Hat, Ada, Doordash, Snowflake, and Wealthsimple.

 At Float, everyone is an owner, bringing their unique perspective to our team and product. Your voice is important, and we take having a culture based on feedback seriously. We openly share our thoughts and differing opinions so we can continue to improve. We do our best to keep our decision-making decentralized so that all team members feel ownership in our success.

 Our Product 
 Float is Canada’s intelligent financial operating system, combining modern financial services and software to help businesses spend, save, and grow. Trusted by more than 10,000 Canadian companies, Float provides high-limit corporate cards, automated expense management, next-day bill payments, high-yield accounts, and industry-leading support, all built in Canada, for Canada. Float recently announced our $85 million Series C, and is backed by world-class investors, including Inovia Capital, Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, OMERS Ventures, and Silicon Valley Bank.

 Our team is a collection of ambitious, collaborative and mission-driven people from all walks of life but with one goal: helping Canadian companies not just survive but thrive. And we’re looking for bold innovators to help shape the future of business finance in Canada.

 AI Use in Our Hiring Process 
 We use technology, including artificial intelligence (AI), to support parts of our hiring process. This may include AI-assisted scheduling and candidate communications, and AI-generated interview notes, guides or summaries to help our team focus on the conversation. All hiring decisions are made by our hiring team.

 About the Role 
 Float’s partnerships channel is one of our newest growth motions, and the one with the most room to run.

 Accounting firms, affiliates and technology platforms already use Float as one place to manage their clients’ financial operations while growing their own. The foundation is strong. The playbook is still unwritten.

 As Head of Partnerships, you’ll report into our SVP of GTM and own the partnerships channel end to end: how we find and win partners across all three types, how we build a community that makes them want to stay, and how what they tell us shapes the product roadmap. You’ll take partnerships from promising to a meaningful share of Float’s growth.

 What You’ll Do 
 Write the partnership playbook 
 Build a multi-year partnership strategy with clear milestones tied to revenue and strategic value.

 Create the processes, playbooks and infrastructure to scale from a handful of partners to dozens.

 Set the targets and reporting. You define what a great channel looks like, then hit it.

 Win and grow partners 
 Find, win, activate and grow partners across accounting and bookkeeping firms, fractional finance teams and investor networks.

 Own the full deal cycle, from first conversation to signed partner.

 Design one-to-many distribution and enablement programs so one partner relationship reaches hundreds of clients.

 Start with the firms that bring the most reach, then widen from there. Once a partner is live, work with Sales to accelerate revenue through them.

 Build the community 
 Run the programs, events and community that make partners better at their jobs and make serving clients easier.

 Track what each partner type delivers, and double down on what works.

 Own how Float shows up for partners, in their language, alongside Marketing.

 Bring the outside in 
 Carry market intelligence and partner feedback back into company strategy and roadmap.

 Work with internal stakeholders to clear whatever slows partners down.

 Build the team 
 Grow a small team, shape it around where the channel is today, and decide where you stay hands-on.

 What You'll Bring 
 8+ years in partnerships, channel or ecosystem growth in B2B SaaS, fintech or payments, including building a partner program from the early stage

 Proven ownership of a partner funnel end to end (sourcing, conversion, activation, expansion) and fluency in the numbers behind each stage

 Comfort being the public face of a program: building community and representing us with external partners

 A marketer’s instinct for positioning a product for a specific audience, ideally professional-services firms

 Experience leading a small team

 Working knowledge of how accounting and bookkeeping firms operate

 Willingness to travel regularly across Canada for events and partner visits

 Strong command of AI tools, as both a user and a builder

 Nice to haves 
 A network in Canadian accounting, bookkeeping, VC or PE circles, or a background as an accountant or bookkeeper

 French proficiency (an asset, not a requirement)

 This May Not Be the Role for You If
 You need an established playbook and a large team before you can do your best work.

 You would rather manage a channel from the sidelines than meet partners yourself.

 You prefer a narrow, single-function remit. This role spans marketing, sales and product.

 You're not energized by feedback or fast-paced change.

 Our Hiring Philosophy 
 We hire for character, curiosity, and learning velocity before credentials. Titles matter less than impact, and every hire is expected to raise the bar for Float as a whole.

 Why You Should Join 
 Be part of an award winning company: we're one of Canada’s Top Growing Companies 2026 according to Report on Business, and Deloitte’s Technology Fast50 2026

 Make a real impact in a high-autonomy, high-growth role

 Collaborate with an ambitious and supportive team

 Competitive compensation, equity options, and benefits

 Hybrid work model: we are based in Toronto with in-office days for connection and collaboration

 Enjoy catered team lunches every Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday

 Bring your pup to our dog-friendly office

 Thrive in a high-trust, high-performance culture where your work truly matters

 In Short 
 At Float, you’ll thrive if you’re bold, curious, and eager to make a real impact. We're building something special—and having a lot of fun along the way. If you’re excited to build, grow, and win together, we’d love to meet you. 

 Protect yourself from recruiting scams. Float only contacts candidates from @ floatfinancial.com addresses and schedules interviews through Ashby or Float calendar invites. We will never ask you to install software, pay a fee, buy equipment or share bank or card details. If something looks off, don't engage. 

 We’re committed to building a workplace that’s welcoming and accessible for everyone. If you need any accommodations during the hiring process or once you join Float, just let us know! You can reach out to Vic ( victoria@floatfinancial.com ), and we’ll work with you to make sure you have what you need to succeed.

Who we are: 

 Geotab ® is a global leader in IoT and connected transportation and certified “Great Place to Work™.” We are a company of diverse and talented individuals who work together to help businesses grow and succeed, and increase the safety and sustainability of our communities. 

  

 Geotab is advancing security, connecting commercial vehicles to the internet and providing web-based analytics to help customers better manage their fleets. Geotab’s open platform and Geotab Marketplace ®, offering hundreds of third-party solution options, allows both small and large businesses to automate operations by integrating vehicle data with their other data assets. Processing billions of data points a day, Geotab leverages data analytics and machine learning to improve productivity, optimize fleets through the reduction of fuel consumption, enhance driver safety and achieve strong compliance to regulatory changes. 

  

 Our team is growing and we’re looking for people who follow their passion, think differently and want to make an impact. Ours is a fast paced, ever changing environment. Geotabbers accept that challenge and are willing to take on new tasks and activities - ones that may not always be described in the initial job description. Join us for a fulfilling career with opportunities to innovate, great benefits, and our fun and inclusive work culture. Reach your full potential with Geotab. To see what it’s like to be a Geotabber, check out our  blog  and follow us @InsideGeotab on  Instagram.  

 Who you are: 

 Geotab is looking for entrepreneurial product and business leaders to head our domains – focused teams that each own a customer outcome and the business results that come with it. As a Head of Domain, you'll own the strategy, roadmap and results for your area, lead a multi-disciplinary team of product managers, designers and engineers, and turn customer problems into products that customers adopt and pay for. 

 What you'll do: 

 This is a role for someone who has built and sold something: a leader who measures success by business results, not by what shipped, and who uses AI to change how work gets done. You'll report to Geotab's Technology Development Board and operate with real autonomy as the business owner of your domain. 

 We welcome applicants nationwide! If you’re based near one of our office hubs, this role follows our hybrid model, blending the comfort of working from home with regular on-site days to connect and collaborate. 

 This is an evergreen posting. We're building a pipeline of exceptional leaders for current and future domain leadership opportunities across Technology Development. 

 How you'll make an impact: 

 Own the outcome. Set the vision, strategy and roadmap for your domain and be accountable for its primary business results – adoption, revenue, retention and customer impact. 

 Run it like a business. Make clear build, buy and partner decisions, prioritize by customer and revenue impact, and say no when the return isn't there. 

 Stay close to customers. Ground your team in customers' real experience to find the problems worth solving, and work with sales, support and partners to bring solutions to market. 

 Lead the AI shift. Redesign how your domain works around AI to move faster, and help others across the organization do the same. 

 Build a high-performing team. Hire the right talent without settling, place people where their strengths matter most, set a clear and high bar, and develop the next generation of leaders. 

 Work across Geotab. Partner closely with platform, segment and other domain leaders, contribute beyond your own goals, and help shape strategy with the Technology Development Board. 

 Manage your investment. Own your domain's people and budget plan, make investment cases, and report on results and risks to the board. 

 What you'll bring to this role: 

 10+ years of experience in product management, product engineering, or related customer-facing product roles. 

 5+ years of senior product and people leadership with cross-functional scope and direct accountability for customer-facing business outcomes. 

 Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field (or equivalent combination of education and work experience). 

 Strong product leadership capability with demonstrated ability to define and execute customer-facing product strategy tied to measurable business outcomes, with P&L literacy and revenue attribution. 

 Cross-functional leadership experience managing teams across product management, product design, and product engineering disciplines, with proven capability in identifying and coaching high-potential leaders. 

 Excellent stakeholder management, change readiness, and communication skills to effectively collaborate with platform teams, segment leads, and executive leadership in evolving organizational structures. 

 Familiarity with modern product discovery, validation practices, and engineering practices (CI/CD, cloud-native delivery, agile), alongside the ability to redesign domain workflows around AI to compress effort. 

  

 Please note: Geotab does not accept agency resumes and is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes. Please do not forward resumes to Geotab employees. 

  

 This posting is not for an existing vacancy. 

  

 Why job seekers choose Geotab: 

 Flex working arrangements 
 Baby bonus & parental leave top up program 
 Online learning and networking opportunities 
 Electric vehicle purchase incentive program 
 Competitive medical and dental benefits 
 Retirement savings program 

 *The above are offered to full-time permanent employees only 

 How we work: 

 At Geotab, we thrive on a flexible hybrid work model that combines the dynamic energy and connection of in-person collaboration with the independence and flexibility of virtual work. We believe that coming together in person is fundamental to cultivating trust, nurturing a vibrant culture of belonging, and fostering meaningful innovation across our diverse teams. Office visit schedules are tailored thoughtfully based on role requirements. Specific expectations regarding workplace location and on-site attendance for this position will be shared during the hiring process. 

  

 #LI-Hybrid 

  

 We believe that ensuring diversity is fundamental to our future growth and progress and is an integral part of our business. We believe that success happens where new ideas can flourish – in an environment that is rich in diversity and a place where people from various backgrounds can work together. Geotab encourages applications from all qualified individuals. We are committed to accommodating people with disabilities during the recruitment and assessment processes and when people are hired. We will ensure the accessibility needs of employees with disabilities are taken into account as part of performance management, career development, training and redeployment processes. If you require accommodation at any stage of the application process or want more information about our diversity and inclusion as well as accommodation policies and practices, please contact us at careers@geotab.com. By submitting a job application to Geotab Inc. or its affiliates and subsidiaries (collectively, “Geotab”), you acknowledge Geotab’s collection, use and disclosure of your personal data in accordance with our Privacy Policy. Click here to read our Privacy Notice.

The actual base salary for this position depends on a variety of factors such as but not limited to skills, qualifications, education and overall experience, including the location the applicant lives while performing the job.  Who you are: 

 We are always looking for amazing talent who can contribute to our growth and deliver results! Geotab is seeking a Head of MyG Core Workflows who will own the MyGeotab workflows customers depend on, ensuring their usability, reliability, and evolution while enabling other product domains to build on shared capabilities. If you love technology, and are keen to join an industry leader — we would love to hear from you! 

 What you'll do: 

 The Head of MyG Core Workflows owns the MyGeotab workflows every customer depends on and is accountable for their usability, reliability, and evolution, both as customer-facing product and as shared capability other domains build on. The scope spans driver messaging; notifications (types, templates, recipients, and delivery channels, including reliability and latency); exception rules, stock rules, and how exceptions appear across reports and the map; system settings; the group hierarchy and its UI; and investigations that reconstruct what happened in context. This leader sets the vision for these workflows and how other domains build on rules, notifications, and groups, and answers to MyGeotab customers, the domain's primary customers, and the product domains that depend on it. 

 Key Accountabilities: 

 People leadership, development, and organizational health. 

 AI-native product development lifecycle, including AI-assisted modernization of legacy MyGeotab workflow pages. 

 Cross-domain communication and coordination. 

 Product ownership and engineering standards for MyGeotab core workflows 

 Customer outcomes and reliability, with MyGeotab customers as primary customers and dependent product domains as internal customers 

 How you'll make an impact: 

 Product Engineering & Technical Standards 

 Define, maintain, and evolve the technical standards, architectural patterns, and shared components for the domain's workflows. 

 Own the reliability, scalability, and performance of messaging, notification, rules UI, and exception services; accountable to customer-facing SLOs for notification delivery success and latency. Own regression protection and VIP-customer test coverage so no release silently breaks customers' rules or notifications. 

 Lead the identification and resolution of technical debt, security vulnerabilities, and compliance requirements in the domain, including the integrity of group-based data visibility, in coordination with Core API and Security. 

 Shape and communicate the vision for core workflows to solution and segment domains; publish and maintain the capability contract for rules, notifications, and groups — intended use patterns, integration standards, and system constraints — so consuming domains can build on reusable platform capability correctly and confidently; keep platform tooling decisions aligned with the needs of consuming domains. 

 Modernize legacy MyGeotab workflow pages to the Zenith/React stack, using AI-assisted conversion where practical, while preserving the behaviour customers depend on. 

 Customer Outcomes & Enablement 

 Treat product domain teams as internal customers of rules, notifications, and groups; proactively understand their evolving needs and remove blockers. MyGeotab customers remain the domain's primary customers. 

 Own product discovery and the domain roadmap with the domain's product manager and designers; prioritize transparently based on customer impact, reliability, and the needs of dependent domains.

 Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field.

 5+ years of relevant industry experience.

Geotabbers accept that challenge and are willing to take on new tasks and activities - ones that may not always be described in the initial job description. Join us for a fulfilling career with opportunities to innovate, great benefits, and our fun and inclusive work culture. Reach your full potential with Geotab. To see what it’s like to be a Geotabber, check out our  blog  and follow us @InsideGeotab on  Instagram.  

 Who you are: 

 We are always looking for amazing talent who can contribute to our growth and deliver results! Geotab is seeking a Head of Vocational who will own the end-to-end product and commercial success of Geotab's Vocational segment. You will defend and grow Geotab's position across diverse asset-intensive industrial and vocational sub-segments, while accelerating growth and market position in earlier-stage opportunities. If you love technology, understand complex industrial markets, and are keen to join an industry leader, we would love to hear from you! 

 What you'll do: 

 As a Head of Vocational, your key area of responsibility will be defining and executing the product, go-to-market, roadmap, and investment strategy for Geotab's full Vocational portfolio. You will be responsible for expanding market share, growing net revenue retention, capturing new opportunities, and making principled build, buy, and partner decisions that leverage Geotab's platform, solution building blocks, Off-Highway Platform, and Marketplace ecosystem. You will need to work closely with Revenue Generation leaders, Off-Highway Platform leadership, Marketing, Business Development, Solutions Engineering, Global Enablement, product domain teams, customers, channel partners, and industry associations. 

 To be successful in this role you will be a commercially minded, customer-obsessed, and strategic leader with strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to lead through influence across a complex, global organization. You will be comfortable navigating mature and greenfield markets, building credibility with industrial operators, and translating specialized customer needs into clear product and commercial decisions. In addition, the successful candidate will have strong product development, go-to-market, financial, stakeholder management, and people leadership skills, with an ability to manage competing priorities, use data to drive decisions, and sustain momentum through change. 

 How you'll make an impact: 

 Own the product, go-to-market strategy, roadmap, and execution for the Vocational segment across its full portfolio of industrial sub-segments. 

 Expand market share, grow net revenue retention, and capture new opportunities by aligning product strategy with the operating environments, duty cycles, safety requirements, and adoption drivers of vocational customers. 

 Develop deep expertise across utilities and energy infrastructure, mining, oil and gas, construction, air, rail, ship, and adjacent industrial markets, building trusted relationships with customers, associations, and channel partners. 

 Serve as the authoritative voice of the Vocational segment within Geotab's global product organization and close capability gaps through cross-domain collaboration, partner solutions, and effective solution packaging. 

 Coordinate a consistent go-to-market motion with Marketing, Business Development, Solutions Engineering, Global Enablement, Revenue Generation, customers, and partners across the segment's sub-segments. 

 Lead annual planning for product strategy, roadmap, headcount, budget, and OKR input; track and report revenue, growth, market share, pipeline, retention, and competitive win-rate KPIs to board leadership. 

 Build and develop a high-trust, high-accountability cross-functional team and foster a culture of segment expertise, customer obsession, commercial outcomes, AI-enabled efficiency, and continuous development. 

 What you'll bring to the role: 

 A bachelor's degree in Business, Engineering, or a related field; an equivalent combination of education and related work experience may be substituted. 

 10+ years of experience in a product or go-to-market role within vocational, industrial fleet, or commercial and asset-intensive vehicle industries. 

 5+ years of experience with accountability for revenue or commercial outcomes within a defined market segment and responsibility for product development. 

 Experience leading product development teams and 10+ years of leadership experience, including 8+ years working with senior leadership in cross-functional commercial or product roles. 

 Deep knowledge of vocational and industrial fleet operations, including operator business models, asset utilization, safety and regulatory requirements, telematics adoption patterns, and customer pain points. 

 Strong commercial, product development, go-to-market, partner development, revenue analytics, and market-share management skills, with experience defining strategy across multiple sub-segments simultaneously. 

 Excellent communication, stakeholder management, change leadership, coaching, and influencing skills, including the ability to lead across Sales, Marketing, Business Development, Product, Development, and Design without direct authority.

 Job Summary

 The role will support both programs. For Operational Risk, the Associate Director will support the execution and enhancement of HOOPP's ORM programs including vendor risk management, operational risk event reporting, key risk indicators and industry event surveillance. This role will also work directly with front office trading teams to review end-to-end processes and surface risks, inefficiencies and control gaps.  Job Summary 

 he Healthcare of Ontario Pension Plan (HOOPP) is a defined benefit pension plan serving members and employers in Ontario's healthcare sector. The Pension Services division supports the delivery of HOOPP's pension promise through accurate and reliable service to members and employers.
 Reporting to the Director, Actuarial Solutions, the Associate Director provides technical leadership to ensure the accuracy and integrity of pension calculations and pension-related data across HOOPP's administration system, member-facing solutions, and off-system tools.

 The Associate Director is a senior resource for pension calculations, pension data, system functionality, testing, defect management, and modernization of calculation capabilities. The role helps ensure that on- and off-system solutions using pension data or calculations are accurate, well controlled, and aligned with HOOPP's administration practices and member service objectives. The Associate Director works with various teams to translate plan provisions, legislation, policy, and administration practices into practical solutions through requirements, testing, implementation, and operational controls.

 What You Will Do 

 1. Calculation Accuracy and Technical Leadership
 Provide leadership to ensure the accuracy of pension calculations and member-facing pension information across HOOPP’s administration system, digital services, and off-system tools.

 Act as a senior subject matter expert for complex pension calculations and pension administration concepts, including escalated, precedent-setting, and high-risk cases.

 Identify inconsistencies among plan provisions, policy, administration practices, system logic, member communications, and calculation tools, and lead their resolution or escalation.

 Advise senior leaders on calculation risks, member impacts, and recommended courses of action while balancing calculation integrity, efficiency, and member experience.

 Promote consistent, explainable, and sustainable calculation logic across member-facing solutions.

 2. Cross-Functional Delivery and Strategic Initiatives
 Act as the actuarial lead for cross-functional initiatives, coordinating stakeholders, influencing project direction, identifying risks and dependencies, and helping ensure solutions involving pension calculations or pension data are delivered successfully.

 Ensure calculation- and data-related considerations are incorporated early in discovery, design, requirements, delivery, testing, and implementation.

 Assess proposed solutions for calculation accuracy, appropriate use of data, alignment with plan provisions, and member impact.

 Lead or support implementation of plan, legislative, policy, or administration-practice changes affecting calculations or pension data.

 Build effective relationships and influence decisions without direct authority, including challenging proposals where calculation integrity may be at risk.

 3. Calculation Requirements, Tools, and Modernization
 Lead the development of calculation requirements, implementation planning, testing strategies, and business readiness activities for calculation engine capabilities and other calculation solutions.

 Establish standards for and develop calculation requirements, including business intent, formulas, data inputs, dependencies, exception handling, auditability, and outputs.

 Ensure requirements are complete, maintainable, and sufficiently detailed for business analysts, developers, and end-users.

 Identify and lead opportunities to automate exception processing and recurring activities while maintaining appropriate controls and human oversight.

 Set standards for calculation tools and other off-system solutions, including testing, approval, version control, access, monitoring, and change management.

 4. Release Delivery, Testing, and Calculation Quality
 Lead the Actuarial Solutions team’s work on calculation-related changes to HOOPP’s pension administration system, from early design and requirements through to testing, implementation, and production monitoring.

 Set and execute testing approaches, ensuring they cover regression testing, complex cases, and data storage.

 Assess release readiness and ensure identified defects and required controls are documented and escalated.

 Coordinate and participate in production validations of calculation functionality, rate tables, and calculation controls after a release is deployed.

 Lead the review and resolution of calculation defects and production incidents, including impacted-member analysis, interim controls, correction methods, and validation of fixes.

 Act as the point of contact for external vendors and stakeholders as it relates to discussions involving calculations or pension data storage. Lead discussions and find resolutions that prioritize calculation and data accuracy in HOOPP’s pension administration system.

 Lead audits of HOOPP’s pension administration system and related tools to ensure consistent quality.

 5. Pension Data and Calculation Controls
 Provide oversight for the interpretation and appropriate use of pension administration data in calculations, member-facing solutions, and internal processes.

 Ensure the correct data fields and transformations are used where the results could affect pension amounts or related information shown to members, employers, or internal staff.

 Define data requirements for initiatives involving pension calculations, reporting, or the presentation of pension information.

 Partner with Pension Technology, Product & Delivery Management, Member & Employer Services, and other Pension Services teams to ensure pension data is used consistently and accurately across solutions.

 Recommend new pension data health checks, calculation controls, or monitoring activities where issues are identified.

 Recommend updates to existing pension data health checks based on changing needs.

 Assess and communicate risks arising from pension data quality issues or control gaps.

 What You Will Bring 

 University degree in actuarial science

 An ASA or ACIA designation is required; progress towards FCIA designation is preferred

 Ten or more years of progressively responsible experience in pensions consulting, actuarial work, pension administration, pension systems, or a related field.

 Several years of experience leading complex technical initiatives, establishing standards, making or recommending high-impact technical decisions, and influencing cross-functional project delivery.

 Deep knowledge of defined benefit pension administration, pension calculations, applicable legislation, plan provisions, and administrative policy.

 Demonstrated ability to interpret complex pension provisions and translate them into clear calculation requirements and business rules.

 Experience leading calculation-related system implementations, testing strategies, and defect resolution

 Ability to understand, review, and challenge complex system calculations, Excel-based calculation tools, and other off-system calculations.

 Ability to communicate complex actuarial and technical matters clearly to various teams and senior leaders.

 Strong judgment and decision-making ability where errors could affect member benefits, financial outcomes, regulatory compliance, or member experience.

 Demonstrated ability to set technical direction, prioritize competing demands, manage dependencies and risks, and deliver outcomes through influence rather than direct authority.

 Demonstrated ability to resolve complex technical issues and influence decisions across various teams and initiatives.

 Strong relationship-building skills, with the ability to influence across various teams and leaders.

 Job Summary: 

 HOOPP is seeking an accomplished institutional investment leader to help shape portfolio construction, investment strategy and risk-informed decision-making across one of Canada's leading pension funds.

 Reporting to the Vice President, Total Portfolio Risk & Analytics, this role operates at the intersection of investment strategy, portfolio construction, total fund analytics and risk insight. The successful candidate will partner closely with senior investment leaders to evaluate strategic opportunities, assess portfolio resilience and provide forward-looking insights that support decisions across public and private markets.

 As a senior leader within the Risk Division, the Senior Director will influence how investment risks and opportunities are understood at the total portfolio level. The role will help advance HOOPP's Total Portfolio Approach through innovative analytics, rigorous research, constructive challenge and strategic thought leadership.

 This is an opportunity to contribute to investment decisions spanning equities, fixed income, derivatives, real estate, infrastructure, private equity and private credit, while helping shape the continued evolution of total portfolio strategy, analytics and risk management at HOOPP.

 What you will do: 

 Strategic Portfolio Leadership
 Partner with Investment Management and the Total Portfolio Group to provide insights that support portfolio construction, strategic asset allocation and investment decision-making across HOOPP’s total fund.
 Act as a trusted advisor to senior leaders on portfolio design, investment strategy, risk-return trade-offs and portfolio resilience.
 Assess the interaction of public and private market exposures, providing an integrated view of portfolio opportunities, concentrations and vulnerabilities.
 Provide constructive challenge and independent assessment of strategic allocations, portfolio construction choices and material investment transactions.

 Total Portfolio Analytics & Risk Insight
 Lead enterprise-wide oversight of total portfolio risk across public and private markets, including equities, fixed income, derivatives, real estate, infrastructure, private equity and private credit.
 Monitor macroeconomic conditions, market developments and structural investment themes to assess their potential impact on total portfolio outcomes.
 Lead benchmark governance across asset classes, ensuring benchmarks appropriately reflect mandate objectives, risk exposures and return drivers.
 Oversee stress testing and scenario analysis frameworks, partnering with Investment Management and Actuarial teams to evaluate portfolio and funded-status outcomes across a range of market environments.
 Evaluate portfolio vulnerabilities, diversification benefits, liquidity dynamics and cross-asset interactions through a total fund lens.

 Research & Innovation
 Drive research and thought leadership in portfolio construction, asset allocation, risk factor modelling, diversification and advanced portfolio analytics.
 Advance analytical capabilities related to emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and data-driven investment insights, and assess their implications for portfolios, markets and investment processes.
 Lead innovation in cross-asset correlation, tail-risk analysis, scenario design and forward-looking portfolio assessment methodologies.
 Collaborate with technology partners, external experts and industry peers to strengthen analytical capabilities and investment decision-support frameworks.

 Leadership & Influence
 Lead, develop and mentor a high-performing team of portfolio risk and analytics professionals.
 Build trusted partnerships across Investment Management, Finance, Actuarial, Technology, Legal, Human Resources and other key stakeholder groups.
 Translate complex analysis into clear, actionable insights for senior leaders and governance forums.
 Represent HOOPP externally through industry forums, peer collaboration, research initiatives and thought leadership.
 Contribute to the long-term evolution of HOOPP’s Total Portfolio Approach and broader investment risk framework.

 What you bring: 

 A graduate degree in Finance, Economics, Mathematics, Engineering, Computer Science, Business Administration or a related discipline. A CFA, FRM, MBA or equivalent professional designation is considered an asset.
 12+ years of experience in institutional investing, portfolio construction, investment strategy, total fund management, multi-asset investing, OCIO, capital markets or investment risk leadership.
 Deep understanding of portfolio construction, asset allocation, investment decision-making and risk management across public and private markets.
 Experience evaluating complex multi-asset portfolios, including alternative investments and derivatives.
 Strong knowledge of total fund investing, stress testing, scenario analysis and quantitative portfolio analytics.
 Demonstrated ability to provide strategic insights that inform senior-level investment decisions and to exercise sound judgement when constructively challenging established views.
 Proven people leadership experience, including building, coaching and developing high-performing teams.
 Executive presence and exceptional communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to translate complex analytical concepts into actionable investment insights.
 Experience within a pension fund, sovereign wealth fund, endowment, insurance asset manager, OCIO platform or other sophisticated institutional investor is preferred. Canadian or international pension experience is considered an asset.
 Experience with Aladdin Risk, Ortec or comparable portfolio and risk management systems is considered an asset.
 Coding, software development, data science or advanced quantitative research experience is advantageous.

 Identify and implement both strategic and tactical opportunities to generate alpha specifically in Canadian and U.S. interest rate cash and derivatives markets, with an emphasis on disciplined trade implementation within the context of the Fund portfolios.

 Apply deep expertise of Canadian market liquidity sources to directly execute transactions.

 Identify trading signals and dislocations via analysis of central bank policy, market structure, macroeconomic investment themes and investor behaviors.

 Oversee portfolio construction and optimize capital allocation decisions for the portfolios across cash and derivative securities in accordance with the Firm’s opportunity set, VaR and capital usage, and liquidity guidelines.

 Ideate, develop and conduct quantitative research initiatives and analytical tool building to improve investment decision making and portfolio efficiency.

 Partner with Risk and analytics teams to enhance investment tools, stress testing, scenario analysis, and portfolio reporting.

 Assist in development and growth of Interest Rates business, including new and profitable adjacent strategies like inflation-linked and U.S. agency markets.

 Drive technological implementation of automation and AI-related initiatives.

 Develop, mentor and inspire investment professionals while strengthening leadership capability, succession pipelines, and talent retention.

 Build and maintain relationships with external market professionals: dealers, research providers, industry peers, and the broader investment community.

 Communicate clearly internally and externally to senior leadership and governance bodies on portfolio strategy and performance, risk positioning, market developments and recommendations.

 Collaborate closely with Total Fund Management, Balance Sheet and Liquidity Management, Risk, and other investment teams to support strategy, governance, liquidity planning, and asset mix decisions at the Fund level.

 An undergraduate degree in one of the following: Finance, Economics, Mathematics, Engineering, Business, or a related discipline; a CFA designation or advanced degree is preferred.

 15+ years of direct investment management experience with deep expertise specifically in Canadian and U.S. rates markets, including both cash and derivatives products, with experience in benchmark aware and proprietary macro investing across nominal and inflation-linked developed markets.

 A demonstrated record of success managing large institutional portfolios delivering strong risk-adjusted performance through different market cycles; implying strong skills in portfolio construction, capital allocation, direct trade execution and risk management, contributions to the strategic direction of the investment business.

 Proven leadership capability with experience leading an investment team and business: setting clear direction, developing talent at all levels, providing constructive feedback while fostering an accountable and high-performing team culture.

 Sound judgment and integrity, and the ability to communicate complex macroeconomic concepts to senior stakeholders, management and committees.

 Long established senior relationships across the Canadian fixed income buy side and sell side investment communities.

 Consistently demonstrates HOOPP's values of being Accountable, Compassionate, and Trustworthy through leadership, decision-making, and collaboration.

jobs.title: Director, Enterprise Communications
jobs.description:
Why you’ll love working here: 
 high-performance, people-focused culture

 our commitment that equity, diversity, and inclusion are fundamental to our work environment and business success, which helps employees feel valued and empowered to be their authentic selves

 learning and development initiatives, including workshops, Speaker Series events and access to LinkedIn Learning, that support employees’ career growth

 membership in HOOPP’s world class defined benefit pension plan, which can serve as an important part of your retirement security

 competitive, 100% company-paid extended health and dental benefits for permanent employees, including coverage supporting our team's diversity and mental health (e.g., gender affirmation, fertility and drug treatment, psychological support benefits of $2,500 per year, parental leave top-up, and a health spending account).

 optional post-retirement health and dental benefits subsidized at 50%

 yoga classes, meditation workshops, nutritional consultations, and wellness seminars

 the opportunity to make a difference and help take care of those who care for us, by providing a financially secure retirement for Ontario healthcare workers

 Job Summary: 

 Reporting to the Vice President, Enterprise Communications, the Director, Enterprise Communications owns the communications strategy supporting HOOPP's investment activities and the external profile of the Office of the CEO. The role carries enterprise level accountability for how the Plan, the Fund and HOOPP's investment approach are understood by external audiences.

 The Director in partnership with the Vice President, Enterprise Communication sets the direction for investment communications, partnering with Investment Management and other business stakeholders on the narrative around portfolio construction, Fund performance, and market conditions. The Director is also accountable for the CEO's speeches, presentations, thought leadership, and key messaging.

 The role leads through influence, directing cross functional teams and external partners on major initiatives and coaching communications professionals across the organization. It calls for an exceptional writer and strategic thinker who absorbs complex investment subject matter quickly, advises with confidence, and delivers at pace with sound judgement and discretion. Investment and financial knowledge is a requirement of this role to support credibility in the room with investment professionals.

 What you will do: 

 Investment communications
 Own HOOPP's investment communications strategy, including the narrative, messaging architecture and external positioning for the Fund.
 Act as senior communications partner to Investment Management, working with the Chief Investment Officer, asset class leaders and subject matter experts on complex investment topics.
 Translate portfolio, market and economic subject matter, including the Total Portfolio Approach, Liability-Aware Investing and Sustainable Investing, into clear communications for external audiences.
 Lead communications for Fund performance milestones, annual and interim results, program launches, new strategies and significant transactions.
 Direct the key messages, statements, question-and-answer documents, and remarks that prepare investment spokespeople for external and industry engagements.
 Build relationships with external stakeholders and investment community contacts to identify storytelling opportunities.

 CEO and executive communications
 Serve as lead communications advisor to the CEO, accountable for speeches, presentations, speaking notes, and key messaging.
 Develop and steward the CEO's external communications platform and thought leadership agenda, aligned to HOOPP's business priorities and reputation objectives.
 Prepare the CEO and Executive Team for high profile external engagements, including conferences, industry events, panels, and stakeholder meetings.
 Counsel the Executive Team and as required, the Board of Trustees on positioning, messaging, and reputational considerations.
 Lead communications for major organizational announcements, executive events, and enterprise-wide engagements.
 Develop executive presentations, Board materials and briefing packages that meet the standards expected at the most senior levels.

 Enterprise leadership and delivery
 Set the cross-channel approach for the communications programs in scope, informed by organizational priorities and audience insight.
 Direct cross functional project teams, agencies, writers, and external partners on major initiatives, setting direction and holding delivery to standard.
 Coach and mentor communications professionals across the team, raising the collective standard of writing, editing, and counsel.
 Set and uphold quality, review, and approval standards for communications products, including accuracy, brand alignment, and accessibility.
 Define how success is measured for the programs in scope and use those measures to sharpen strategy and demonstrate impact.
 Represent Enterprise Communications on enterprise projects and governance forums, and improve communications processes, tools and standards.
 Manage budgets, agency relationships, and external vendors for assigned programs.

 What you bring: 

 Education and experience
 Post-secondary degree or diploma in Communications, Journalism, Public Relations, Business, Finance, Economics, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
 8 to 10 years of progressive communications experience, including demonstrated ownership of a communications strategy or program at an enterprise level.
 Demonstrated investment and financial knowledge is required, gained through direct experience in investment communications, capital markets, asset management, banking, pension plans or another institutional investment environment.
 Experience as a communications advisor to C-suite executives, including speechwriting and external platform development for a CEO or equivalent.
 Experience developing executive presentations, Board materials, conference presentations, and strategic communications for senior leaders.
 Experience operating effectively within a complex, highly regulated, or stakeholder-rich environment.
 Experience leading through influence, including directing cross functional teams, agencies and external partners without direct reporting authority.

 Skills and capabilities
 Exceptional written and oral communication, editing and storytelling skills, adapted to diverse audiences and channels, particularly external ones.
 Solid working knowledge of investment and financial concepts, including asset classes, portfolio construction, capital markets, and risk and return, with the ability to read and interpret financial statements and performance reporting.
 Strong business acumen and the ability to understand complex financial and investment concepts 
 Strong critical thinking to assess communications needs and risks relevant to the CEO, the Executive Team, and the Board of Trustees.
 Deep understanding of corporate communications and multichannel storytelling in building and protecting external reputation.
 Excellent judgement, discretion, attention to detail and project management skills, with the ability to hold several senior priorities at once.
 Demonstrated ability to build trust, influence stakeholders at all levels and respectfully challenge perspectives when appropriate.
 Highly motivated self-starter who delivers high-quality work with minimal direction and brings structure to ambiguous problems.
 Demonstrated proficiency with artificial intelligence tools to improve the effectiveness, efficiency, and impact of communications, including content development, insight generation, stakeholder sentiment analysis and channel optimization.

 Assets
 A CFA, CIM, CAIA, MBA or accounting designation, held or in progress.
 Experience communicating on behalf of a pension plan, institutional investor, or other long-horizon asset owner.

jobs.title: Chief Scientist - Physical AI
jobs.description:
Huawei Canada has an immediate permanent opening for a Chief Scientist. 

 About the team: 
 Founded in 2012, the Noah’s Ark lab has evolved into a prominent research organization with notable achievements in academia and industry. The lab’s mission focuses on advancing artificial intelligence and related fields to benefit the company and society. Driven by impactful, long-term projects, the aim is to enhance state-of-the-art research while integrating innovations into the company's products and services, including LLMs, RL, NLP, computer vision, AI theory, and Autonomous driving.   

 About the job: 
 Work at the forefront of Embodied AI and Spatial AI, collaborating with researchers and engineers to solve real-world challenges and bridge cutting-edge research with scalable deployment. 

 Develop state-of-the-art approaches in Physical AI, including robotic foundation models, world models, multimodal representation learning, reasoning and planning, as well as imitation and reinforcement learning with integrated low-level control. 

 Translate advanced problem formulations and model designs into efficient, production-grade systems, enabling rapid iteration through large-scale experimentation. 

 Design and execute experiments across both simulation and real-world robotic platforms, covering data collection, evaluation, and performance analysis. 

 Drive closed-loop learning by integrating data, models, and real-world feedback to continuously improve system robustness and adaptability. 

 Collaborate cross-functionally across research, infrastructure, and robotics systems to ensure end-to-end system coherence and scalability. 

 Contribute to and lead high-impact research outputs, including patents and publications in top-tier venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR, and ICRA.
