 Nice-to-have qualifications: 

 Experience in EdTech, K-12 education, public sector, or local government, particularly with district procurement, RFPs, and contractual requirements. 

 Experience as a corporate secretary or managing capitalization tables and equity incentive programs. 

 Exposure to mergers and acquisitions, including due diligence, transaction preparation, or post-acquisition integration. 

 Previous responsibility for corporate insurance programs and enterprise risk management. 

 Benefits: 

 Competitive total on-target earnings (OTE) ranging from CAD 200,000 to CAD 250,000, combining base salary and variable compensation. 

 Remote working opportunity based in Kelowna, British Columbia, with a collaborative and supportive team environment. 

 Leadership autonomy and the opportunity to shape financial strategy, commercial operations, and organizational growth. 

 Opportunity to build and develop a finance function, lead a team, and implement scalable business processes. 

 Annual compensation reviews conducted in November, taking into account market benchmarks and individual performance. 

 Compensation philosophy focused on fairness, transparency, market alignment, and opportunities for professional growth. 

 Opportunity to contribute to a mission-driven technology business supporting educators and students. 

 Collaborative culture that values shared ownership, continuous learning, accountability, empathy, and individual contributions.

jobs.title: VP, Consulting & Transformation
jobs.description:
Consulting and Transformation Leadership

 Lead senior client engagements across digital and AI transformation, platform selection and replatforming, international expansion, B2B commerce, retail and point of sale (POS), loyalty, marketplaces, data, and operating models.

 Facilitate structured discovery across business objectives, customer insights, data, technology, organizational capabilities, and operating models.

 Translate complex or ambiguous client needs into clear goals, identified gaps, prioritized initiatives, and practical transformation plans.

 Develop compelling business cases that connect strategic roadmaps to funded initiatives, prioritizing opportunities based on business impact, customer value, effort, and dependencies.

 Create multi-year transformation roadmaps that define the desired future state and the steps required to achieve it.

 Provide independent recommendations on the best path forward for clients, including partner or co-delivery models when their needs extend beyond internal delivery capabilities.

 Client Retention, Account Expansion, and Commercial Growth

 Own long-term strategic plans for top-tier retained clients, aligned with their one-, three-, and five-year business objectives.

 Lead or co-lead Growth Councils and Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) alongside Client Partners, focusing on future opportunities, measurable return on investment, and business outcomes.

 Bring together strategy, AI and transformation, CRM and lifecycle, conversion optimization, SEO/GEO/AEO, design, and technology perspectives into a unified client growth strategy.

 Help evolve client relationships from individual project delivery into broader, multi-service partnerships.

 Contribute strategic judgment to client health assessments and monthly intelligence reporting, complementing AI-generated analysis.

 Ensure consulting services are clearly scoped, priced, and incorporated into retainers and new engagements.

 Support strategic sales opportunities by bringing senior-level transformation expertise into client conversations and pitches.

 Shape the scope and strategic approach of complex, multidisciplinary proposals before pricing, ensuring recommendations are differentiated and outcome-oriented.

 Own and continuously refine the strategic positioning and pitch narrative, presenting the business as a comprehensive digital services and transformation partner rather than solely a platform implementation provider.

 Practice Leadership and Commercial Performance

 Lead and develop a multidisciplinary consulting practice covering strategy, conversion rate optimization, CRM and lifecycle, SEO/GEO/AEO, and emerging AI services.

 Maintain a strong understanding of each discipline, including its core performance indicators, methodologies, and applications across project-based and retained engagements.

 Own practice quality, methodologies, playbooks, team structure, performance management, and day-to-day operations.

 Carry responsibility for practice margin and utilization targets.

 Build scalable documentation, frameworks, and evaluation criteria that enable each discipline to grow beyond the capabilities of individual contributors.

 Turn successful pilots, managed services, and AI commerce capabilities into repeatable offerings with clearly defined scope and pricing.

 Shape the practice's perspective on the broader digital commerce ecosystem, including search and discovery, personalization, lifecycle messaging, loyalty, subscriptions, PIM, ERP, OMS, DAM, data, and AI tools.

 Advise clients on whether their existing technology stack supports their growth ambitions and competitive requirements, and identify where investment or reinvention is needed.

 AI Transformation and People Leadership

 Champion the practical application of AI in client transformation roadmaps, connecting emerging capabilities to measurable business value.

 Bring AI-enabled capabilities into sales and advisory conversations, including AI discoverability, agentic commerce operations, and technology partner stack advisory.

 Redesign consulting methodologies and discipline deliverables for AI-native workflows, with a focus on measurable improvements.

 Mentor and develop discipline leaders, building trust while encouraging continuous improvement, stronger performance, and revenue growth.

 Establish clear performance standards and develop a leadership bench capable of operating independently and delivering results.

 Hold direct reports and practice leaders accountable for outcomes, ownership, and execution.

 At least 10 years of experience in consulting, strategy, or senior client leadership, including substantial experience in a senior client-facing role at an agency, digital consultancy, or consulting firm.

 Proven track record leading digital transformation engagements from ambiguous business challenges through funded roadmaps and successful delivery.

 Experience leading a consulting or strategy function and managing a multidisciplinary team or practice.

 Demonstrated ability to define consulting offerings, establish methodologies, manage commercial performance, and build and develop leadership teams.

 Strong experience developing and defending business cases for digital transformation initiatives, including ROI modeling and prioritization frameworks.

 Proven success growing retained or recurring revenue relationships, beyond acquiring new business.

 Strong understanding of digital commerce growth drivers, including demand generation, conversion, customer lifecycle and retention, merchandising, average order value (AOV), and the data connecting these areas.

jobs.title: VP, Marketing
jobs.description:
As VP of Marketing, you will oversee the complete marketing function, establishing its strategic priorities, operating processes, budget, and performance framework. You will be responsible for building a measurable growth engine, strengthening customer relationships, supporting revenue generation, and ensuring consistent market positioning across all channels. You will combine strategic leadership with hands-on execution while working closely with cross-functional teams.

 Marketing Strategy and Performance

 Develop and own the annual marketing strategy, operating plan, budget, and vendor management processes.

 Establish marketing performance scorecards with clear KPIs, targets, and leading and lagging indicators.

 Track and report marketing-sourced and marketing-influenced pipeline, bookings, revenue, and retention.

 Own marketing attribution, lead scoring, lead handoff processes, and data quality across marketing automation and CRM platforms.

 Present marketing performance and strategic priorities during executive reviews and quarterly business reviews.

 Optimize the marketing technology stack, manage vendor spending, and ensure all marketing accounts and assets remain under company ownership.

 Align marketing priorities and service-level expectations with other departments on a quarterly basis.

 Demand Generation and Revenue Growth

 Develop and execute demand generation campaigns and account-based marketing programs to generate qualified pipeline.

 Lead customer expansion, adoption, and retention initiatives in collaboration with Customer Success.

 Translate product value propositions into business-case tools and ROI materials that support sales conversations.

 Build and maintain a database of measurable customer outcomes demonstrating the value delivered by products and services.

 Maintain proposal and RFP content libraries, including materials supporting public-sector and government opportunities.

 Conduct win/loss analysis and share insights with Sales, Product, and marketing stakeholders.

 Product and Sales Marketing

 Partner with Product teams on product positioning, naming, packaging recommendations, and launch readiness.

 Develop and maintain product sheets, presentations, demonstration materials, customer case studies, and competitive battlecards.

 Ensure consistency and accuracy across all customer-facing marketing and sales materials.

 Lead co-marketing initiatives with technology and channel partners.

 Equip Sales and Customer Success teams with relevant messaging, competitive intelligence, and business-value materials.

 Events and Customer Engagement

 Develop an annual event strategy and calendar, establishing investment cases and measurable ROI targets for each initiative.

 Manage national and regional conferences from planning through execution, including meetings, booths, customer receptions, and follow-up activities.

 Organize webinars, virtual events, and customer conferences.

 Support internal company events, including annual employee conferences.

 Measure event performance through meetings generated, pipeline contribution, costs, and post-event ROI reporting.

 Brand and Communications

 Lead brand positioning and refresh initiatives, ensuring consistent brand standards across all communication channels.

 Own social media strategy, public relations, thought leadership, industry awards, and customer recognition programs.

 Maintain accurate and consistent external company profiles across directories, analyst platforms, and industry data sources.

 Support employer branding initiatives and recruitment-related communications.

 Website and Digital Marketing

 Lead website redesign initiatives and oversee ongoing website performance, including traffic, conversion rates, and lead quality.

 Own search engine optimization (SEO) strategy and improve visibility across traditional search engines and AI-powered search tools.

 Manage customer newsletters, email marketing campaigns, and digital engagement programs.

 Internal Communications and Market Intelligence

 Manage the company intranet and oversee its content and updates.

 Develop leadership newsletters and company-wide internal communications.

 Coordinate customer surveys through a centralized process to ensure feedback is collected, analyzed, and acted upon.

 Transform competitive intelligence and market insights into actionable messaging, sales enablement materials, and product recommendations.

 Produce market intelligence reports following major industry conferences.

 Collaborate with Product and Sales to define ideal customer profiles and market segments across healthcare, military, corrections, and higher education.

 Represent the voice of the customer in product development, positioning, and pricing discussions.

 AI-Enabled Marketing

 Lead AI adoption across the marketing function, implementing AI-first workflows for research, content creation, campaign management, personalization, and reporting.

 Develop and deploy practical AI tools and agents, including workflow automation within marketing automation and CRM platforms.

 Establish quality assurance, brand safety, and data privacy standards for AI-generated content and marketing activities.

 Measure and communicate the productivity, efficiency, and performance improvements achieved through AI adoption.

 Strengthen brand visibility across AI-powered search platforms and answer engines.

 Team Leadership and First-Year Delivery

 Align team responsibilities and individual strengths with strategic growth initiatives to maximize marketing effectiveness.

 Review existing marketing vendors and tools, identifying opportunities to optimize spending and improve efficiency.

 Establish baseline marketing performance metrics and deliver an initial marketing scorecard within the first 90 days.

 Develop an annual marketing plan and budget supported by clear investment cases and measurable objectives.

 Lead a brand refresh and website redevelopment, ensuring delivery within agreed timelines and budgets.

 Build a library of at least 10 quantified customer success stories and establish an active customer reference program.

 Increase content production and campaign execution capacity through effective AI adoption.

 Requirements:

 The ideal candidate is a results-driven B2B marketing leader with substantial experience in enterprise software or technology environments. You should combine strategic marketing expertise with hands-on execution capabilities, demonstrating a proven ability to generate measurable pipeline and revenue growth. Strong product knowledge, analytical skills, and practical experience implementing AI-powered marketing workflows are essential.

 At least 7 years of B2B marketing experience within software, SaaS, or technology organizations.

 Demonstrated success delivering measurable business results, including improvements in marketing-generated pipeline, revenue, conversion rates, or customer retention.

 Proven ability to lead strategic marketing initiatives from planning through execution and measurable outcomes.

 Hands-on experience building demand generation campaigns and implementing pipeline attribution using marketing automation platforms and Salesforce or comparable CRM solutions.

 Strong execution capabilities, including personally creating content, developing campaigns, managing marketing automation tools, and analyzing performance data.

 Ability to make data-driven decisions, provide actionable recommendations, and take ownership of strategic and operational outcomes.

 Strong product marketing expertise, including the ability to understand complex enterprise software, deliver product demonstrations, and communicate customer ROI.

 Practical experience using generative AI tools in daily marketing operations, including building or deploying AI-powered workflows or agents and demonstrating measurable improvements in productivity, quality, or results.

 Experience leading major marketing transformation initiatives, such as brand repositioning, brand refreshes, product launches, or rebuilding a marketing function.

 Proven experience managing industry conferences and events as measurable business investments, with clear pipeline and ROI objectives.

 Familiarity with marketing technology and analytics tools, including:

 Marketing automation platforms.

 Salesforce or comparable CRM systems.

 Website content management systems (CMS).

 Web analytics and campaign performance tools.

 Strong communication, leadership, and stakeholder management skills.

 Ability to coordinate cross-functional initiatives and collaborate effectively with geographically distributed teams across different time zones.

 Preferred Qualifications:

 Previous experience managing and developing a marketing team.

 Experience marketing both on-premise and cloud-based software solutions.

 Background in healthcare technology, healthcare foodservice, or clinical nutrition.

 Registered Dietitian credentials or professional experience working closely with dietitians are considered a strong advantage.

 Experience marketing to healthcare systems, government organizations, or military buyers within complex, multi-stakeholder sales environments.

 Experience working in private equity-backed or holding-company software environments.

 Previous responsibility for internal communications alongside external marketing activities.

 Benefits:

 Competitive annual base salary ranging from $115,000 to $140,000, depending on experience.

 Additional annual performance-based bonus.

 Employee benefits package.

 Fully remote working arrangement, with the position open to candidates in Canada.

 Opportunity to lead and shape the overall marketing strategy of an established enterprise technology business.

 Significant ownership and influence over marketing operations, brand positioning, and revenue growth initiatives.

 Opportunity to drive AI adoption and introduce innovative marketing technologies and workflows.

 Collaboration with executive leadership and cross-functional teams.

 Exposure to diverse industries, including healthcare, government, military, corrections, and higher education.

 Opportunity to make a measurable impact within a growing technology organization.

jobs.title: Director, Brand & Growth - Mntd
jobs.description:
Knix is an award-winning intimate apparel and activewear brand that is re-inventing intimates for real life. Through our innovative products and our engaged community, we are empowering people everywhere to be unapologetically free.  Launched in 2013, we are one of the fastest-growing intimate apparel brands in North America and are globally recognized as an innovator within the apparel space.  We reach over 3 million customers through our online stores, Knix retail locations across North America and channels such as wholesale and Amazon.  We are revolutionizing the apparel industry with our best-in-class customer experience, innovative products and brands Knix, Kt by Knix, and Mntd.  Come join us if you are looking for a purpose-driven and authentic career!


MNTD is looking for a highly entrepreneurial, commercially minded brand leader to help build the next stage of the business.
This is a broad, hands-on leadership role for someone who knows how to build a brand and grow a business at the same time. You will own the day-to-day performance of MNTD while shaping how the brand shows up in the market, from growth strategy and digital marketing to campaigns, retail, partnerships, storytelling, customer experience and commercial planning.
You will operate with the speed and resourcefulness of an early-stage business, while having access to the capabilities, infrastructure and expertise of the broader Knix organization.
The right person is equally comfortable developing the strategy, reviewing a P&L, briefing a creative campaign, managing an agency, evaluating paid media performance, building a retail or brand partnership and jumping in to solve an executional problem when needed.
This role requires someone who creates momentum rather than waits for direction. You should be excited by ambiguity, motivated by growth and comfortable moving between big-picture thinking and detailed execution.

jobs.title: Director, Cloud Engineering
jobs.description:
Who We Are; What We Do; Where We’re Going
 
Magnet Forensics is a global leader in the development of digital investigative software that acquires, analyzes, and shares evidence from computers, smartphones, tablets, and IoT-related devices. We are continually innovating so our customers can deploy advanced and effective tools to protect their companies, communities, and countries.
 
Serving thousands of customers globally, our solutions are playing a crucial role in modernizing digital investigations, helping investigators fight crime, protect assets, and guard national security.
 
With employees based around the world, Magnet Forensics has been expanding our global presence. This is a highly visible leadership role responsible for ensuring Magnet's cloud platform remains secure, reliable, compliant, cost-effective, and capable of powering the next generation of digital investigation products.
 
NOTE: Candidates must reside in Canada.

jobs.title: Director, Fraud Analytics & Risk Management
jobs.description:
At Manulife Bank, protecting our customers, advisors, and business from financial crime is a critical strategic priority. As Director, Fraud Analytics & Risk Management, you will lead the Bank's fraud analytics and intelligence capabilities, leveraging advanced data analytics, customer risk modeling, and fraud technologies to proactively identify, detect, and mitigate fraud across all banking products, channels, and customer journeys.

 This role is responsible for developing a data-driven fraud management ecosystem that delivers strong customer protection while enabling frictionless banking experiences. Working closely with Operations, Risk, Technology, Digital, Data & Analytics, and external partners, you will drive innovative solutions that enhance fraud detection, strengthen customer risk management, and improve fraud prevention outcomes.

 Reporting to the AVP/VP, Fraud Strategy & Operations, you will play a key leadership role in shaping the future state fraud capability at Manulife Bank.

 Position Responsibilities: 
 Lead Fraud Analytics & Intelligence 
 Develop and execute the Bank's fraud analytics strategy across deposits, lending, mortgages, payments, digital banking, contact centre, and advisor channels.
 Establish proactive monitoring and analytical capabilities to detect emerging fraud risks, customer scams, account takeover attacks, identity theft, synthetic identities, mule activity, and organized fraud networks.
 Leverage internal and external data sources to identify fraud trends, vulnerabilities, and opportunities for control enhancement.
 Lead fraud intelligence and root-cause analysis activities to continuously improve detection and prevention effectiveness.
 Build meaningful analytics, dashboards, and executive reporting to support fraud management decision-making.

 Own Customer Risk Scoring & Fraud Decisioning 
 Design, develop, and continuously optimize customer fraud risk scoring models across the customer lifecycle.
 Enhance risk-based authentication, transaction monitoring, and fraud intervention strategies.
 Leverage behavioural analytics, device intelligence, digital signals, transaction patterns, and external intelligence to improve customer risk segmentation.
 Monitor model performance and ensure appropriate governance, oversight, validation, and recalibration.
 Support development of real-time fraud detection and decisioning capabilities as the Bank evolves its payments and digital banking ecosystem.

 Advance Fraud Technology Capabilities 
 Lead evaluation, implementation, and optimization of fraud technology solutions that strengthen the Bank's fraud prevention capabilities.
 Partner with vendors to implement prevention and detection fraud toolkits
 Develop business cases and strategic recommendations for fraud technology investments.
 Manage vendor relationships, performance expectations, and ongoing solution effectiveness reviews.

 Strengthen Fraud Risk Management 
 Lead comprehensive fraud risk assessments across products, processes, channels, and strategic initiatives.
 Partner with Enterprise Risk Management and Compliance teams to ensure fraud risks are appropriately identified, measured, monitored, and mitigated.
 Define and maintain fraud risk indicators, thresholds, risk appetite metrics, and reporting frameworks.
 Identify control gaps and drive remediation strategies.
 Support regulatory, audit, and governance reviews related to fraud risk management.

 Enable Data-Driven Fraud Prevention 
 Partner with Analytics on developing predictive models to improve fraud detection and prevention outcomes.
 Leverage machine learning, network analytics, behavioural analytics, anomaly detection, and AI-enabled capabilities where appropriate.
 Balance fraud loss reduction objectives with customer experience considerations.
 Translate complex analytical findings into actionable business recommendations for senior leadership.

 Lead and Develop a High-Performing Team 
 Build and lead a team of fraud analytics, fraud intelligence, and risk professionals.
 Foster a culture of innovation, continuous improvement, accountability, and customer focus.
 Coach and develop talent while building future fraud analytics capabilities for the Bank.
 Serve as a trusted advisor to executives and stakeholders on fraud risk trends, emerging threats, and mitigation strategies.

 Required Qualifications: 
 University degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Data Science, Computer Science, Business, Finance, Risk Management, or a related discipline.
 10+ years of experience in fraud analytics, fraud risk management, financial crimes, banking analytics, or advanced data analytics. 
 Deep understanding of fraud risks across retail banking products and customer journeys.
 Experience developing fraud detection models, customer risk scoring frameworks, and fraud monitoring programs.
 Experience managing fraud technology vendors and implementing fraud 

 Preferred Qualifications: 
 Strong executive communication and stakeholder management skills. 
 Graduate degree in a quantitative or business discipline. Professional certifications such as: Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE) 
 Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialist (CAMS) 
 Certified Analytics Professional (CAP) 

 Experience with machine learning and AI-enabled fraud detection solutions. 
 Experience supporting real-time payments, digital banking, and emerging payment ecosystems.
 Experience working with SQL, Python, SAS, Power BI, Tableau, machine learning and predictive analytics tools, fraud detection and case management platforms, identity verification technologies, behavioural analytics solutions, and device intelligence platforms to support data-driven decision-making, fraud prevention, and operational effectiveness.

 Success in This Role 
 You will be successful if you:
 Demonstrate strategic thinking and strong business acumen.
 Drive measurable improvements in fraud control effectiveness.
 Proactively identify emerging fraud risks before they impact customers.
 Build strong partnerships across the Bank and Enterprise.

jobs.title: AVP, GTO Strategy & Transformation
jobs.description:
As AVP, GTO Strategy & Transformation, you will lead GTO's strategy, transformation agenda, and multi-year roadmap, while also overseeing the GTO global AI platform roadmap. Your focus will be on shaping where GTO is going and ensuring its transformation delivers measurable business value. You will lead multi-year strategy development, operating model transformation, AI enablement, value realization, workforce modernization, and enterprise-scale transformation initiatives. Working closely with Technology, Operations, Finance, People Partners, and business leaders, you will identify opportunities to redesign how work gets done, convert productivity gains into measurable business outcomes, and help build an AI-enabled growth engine that supports growth while maintaining expense discipline. This is an AI-native team — the team uses AI tools, agentic workflows, and LLM-connected platforms as its primary way of working, not as an occasional add-on. 

 Position Responsibilities: 
 GTO Strategy & Strategic Planning: Lead development of multi-year GTO strategy, transformation roadmaps, investment priorities, and strategic planning processes. Translate enterprise objectives into executable plans across Technology and Operations, ensuring strategic intent is reflected in investment and delivery decisions before resources are committed.
 AI-Native Operating Model Transformation: Design and evolve future-state operating models that combine AI, automation, workforce transformation, and technology productivity to sustainably improve capacity, customer outcomes, and efficiency across Technology and Operations — including delivery models, product operating models, workforce structures, and technology ways of working.
 Technology Productivity Realization: Partner with CIOs, COOs, and segment leaders to identify, quantify, and realize value from technology productivity improvements — including product operating models, engineering productivity, and delivery modernization — ensuring productivity gains translate into measurable operational and business outcomes rather than remaining theoretical.
 Operational Transformation & Value Realization: Lead enterprise operational transformation initiatives across customer service, operations, digital channels, workforce productivity, and support functions. Current focus areas may include contact centre transformation, containment optimization, service modernization, and AI-enabled efficiency programs — with the underlying methodology (diagnostic rigor, cross-source data reconciliation, quantified business cases) designed to generalize to future transformation priorities as GTO's agenda evolves.
 Workforce Transformation & Future Skills: Define workforce transition strategies, future-skill requirements, role redesign opportunities, and redeployment approaches required to support AI-enabled operating models. Partner with People Partners, L&D, and segment leaders to drive execution — setting direction, tracking progress, and identifying opportunities to accelerate adoption in partnership with segment leaders.
 Enterprise Value Realization: Own benefit targets and KPI commitments across the GTO transformation portfolio. Establish and govern enterprise value realization methodologies, validate assumptions, reconcile benefit calculations across data sources, create defensible performance baselines, and ensure reported outcomes remain transparent and defensible to senior leadership and ELT — explicitly separating transformation-driven impact from organic or external trends.
 Product & Portfolio Leadership Strengthened: Own and evolve the GTO AI product roadmap, defining priorities and sequencing releases across initiatives and reusable capabilities. Ensure product investments align with GTO strategic priorities and target-state operating model objectives, rather than being pursued independently of the broader transformation agenda.
 Executive & Board-Level Narrative Ownership: Own the preparation of ELT and Board/Technology Committee-ready materials — portfolio checkpoints, anticipated-Q&A briefs, and strategic narratives — translating complex, multi-segment operational and financial data into clear, decision-ready formats. Anticipate scrutiny across every segment and function represented, not just the primary owner's area, and ensure diplomatic, precise, and defensible framing throughout.
 GTO Global AI Platform Roadmap Ownership: Own and oversee the GTO global AI platform roadmap — set the AI direction and transformation agenda for GTO across 14 countries, translate enterprise AI vision into operational priorities, and ensure the platform roadmap is directly sequenced against GTO's broader multi-year strategy and transformation agenda rather than developed in isolation. Apply strategic rigour to problem framing and solution design, ensuring the right problems are prioritized before delivery resources are committed, and assess strategic AI hypotheses through structured pilots prior to scaling investment.
 Outcome Measurement: Establish clear success measures — adoption, operational impact, cycle-time improvements, reliability — and report progress to senior leadership.
 Delivery Execution: Lead end-to-end delivery planning and execution for approved transformation and AI initiatives, ensuring predictable release rhythms and timely removal of blockers.
 Competitive Intelligence: Maintain ongoing awareness of AI and transformation developments across financial services and the broader enterprise landscape. Translate external signals — competitor moves, emerging capabilities, regulatory shifts — into strategic implications for the GTO agenda.
 Production Readiness: Drive readiness reviews with Technology, Enterprise AI, and Risk partners to confirm controls, documentation, and deployment plans are in place prior to release.
 Cross-functional Escalation: Act as escalation point for delivery throughput issues, coordinating cross-functional resolution and trade-off decisions.
 Platform Reuse & Scaling: Lead the shift from project-by-project delivery to a reusable capability model — shared components, templates, evaluation patterns, and connectors.
 Governance Alignment: Ensure solutions align with Responsible AI and model risk expectations, including appropriate documentation and monitoring plans.
 Opportunity Identification & Prioritization: Identify, quantify, and prioritize AI and operational-transformation opportunities across GTO using structured analysis and operational input — including digital-capability heatmapping, deflection/containment sizing, and repeat-contact root-cause analysis.  People Leadership: Build and lead a high-performing team focused on operational discipline, delivery excellence, and continuous improvement.

jobs.description:

This role is accountable for leading the Quality Assurance and governance oversight function across Vendor Information Security Management (VISM), Vendor Governance Management (VGM), and Sourcing.

 The Director will lead and manage a team, providing clear direction, oversight, and ongoing development, while ensuring procurement-related third-party risk activities are executed in line with internal policies, audit expectations, and regulatory requirements.

 The successful candidate will bring deep expertise in audit, regulatory compliance, and Risk & Control Self-Assessment (RCSA) and will serve as a key point of contact for regulators (e.g., OSFI), Internal Audit, and Second Line Risk. This role requires a strong, confident leader with a strategic and critical mindset, capable of influencing stakeholders, challenging constructively, and delivering consistent, high-quality outcomes.

 Quality Assurance & Control Oversight 
 Lead and execute a comprehensive Quality Assurance Program across VISM, VGM, and Sourcing teams

 Ensure all activities are completed in accordance with defined TPRM processes, system requirements, and documentation standards

 Contracts executed prior to completion of required risk assessments

 Risk data accuracy and reporting integrity

 Regulators (including OSFI), Internal Audit, and Line 2 Risk

 Regulatory reviews and examinations

 Internal audit inquiries and testing

 Supplier due diligence and external questionnaires

 Ensure all outputs are accurate, consistent, evidence-based, and defensible

 Policy, Guidelines & Advisory 
 Develop and maintain TPRM guidelines, processes, and playbooks aligned to regulatory expectations

 Provide guidance to business units on:
 Handling supplier confidential documentation requests

 Application of TPRM requirements in complex or non-standard scenarios (e.g., exceptions, travel-related vendors)

 Leadership & Strategic Direction 
 Lead, manage, and develop a high-performing team, providing clear direction, priorities, and performance expectations

 Set and execute a strategic vision for Quality Assurance and TPRM governance

 Foster a culture of accountability, integrity, and continuous improvement

 Apply a critical and independent mindset to challenge processes, identify gaps, and strengthen the control environment

 Build team capability through training, coaching, and ongoing development

 Partner with senior stakeholders across Procurement, Risk, and Business Units to influence outcomes and strengthen risk management practices

 Required Qualifications: 
 10+ years of experience in Third Party Risk Management (TPRM), Operational Risk, Audit, or Compliance

 Deep expertise in:
 Audit practices and regulatory expectations

 RCSA frameworks, control design, and risk assessment methodologies

 Strong experience engaging with:
 Regulators (e.g., OSFI)

 Internal and external audit functions

jobs.title: Director, Global Technology & Operations Strategy & Transformation
jobs.description:
The Director, Global Technology & Operations Strategy & Transformation will help shape and execute strategic priorities across Global Technology & Operations (GTO), with a significant focus on leading the AI program and translating strategy into measurable business outcomes.

 The Director will lead the AI program across GTO, bringing together strategy, business case development, funding, program governance, technical delivery, adoption, and value realization. This includes managing AI program funding, ensuring funding is directed to the appropriate initiatives and teams, and maintaining visibility into how initiatives are progressing against delivery commitments, defined success criteria, and approved budgets.

 Working closely with the VP of GTO and senior stakeholders across Business, Technology, Enterprise AI, Finance, and Risk, the Director will provide an integrated view of the AI program, drive accountability across teams, identify areas requiring leadership attention, and enable informed decisions on priorities, funding, execution, and outcomes.

 The Director will also help shape how GTO delivers its AI agenda, establishing approaches to prioritize and sequence initiatives, accelerate execution, and scale reusable AI capabilities across segments and countries. This includes helping establish a practical path from opportunity identification through development, production, and adoption, while focusing resources on initiatives that can deliver the greatest strategic and business impact.

 Position Responsibilities
 GTO Strategy & Transformation: Partner with the VP of GTO and senior leaders to translate strategic priorities into executable strategies, roadmaps, initiatives, and measurable outcomes. Connect priorities across teams, identify opportunities and risks, and provide insights and recommendations to support executive decision-making.
 AI Program Leadership & Governance: Lead the end-to-end AI and Automation program across GTO, establishing a single integrated view of initiatives, priorities, dependencies, funding, and outcomes. Establish program governance and operating rhythms and work across Product Owners, Segment Leads, Technology, and business and functional partners to drive execution, alignment, and accountability.
 AI Strategy, Prioritization & Delivery Approach: Help define how GTO identifies, assesses, prioritizes, sequences, and delivers AI initiatives. Develop practical prioritization and delivery approaches that consider strategic alignment, business value, delivery readiness, scalability, complexity, funding requirements, dependencies, and risk. Continuously assess the portfolio to ensure resources remain focused on the highest-value opportunities and identify where initiatives should be accelerated, repositioned, or deprioritized.
 Business Case & AI Program Funding: Lead the planning, mobilization, and partner engagement required to develop business cases for AI execution and future funding, including cost-benefit analysis, expected outcomes, success criteria, delivery requirements, and risk considerations. Manage AI program funding and recommend allocation or reallocation across initiatives and teams based on strategic priorities, expected value, delivery readiness, and performance.
 Delivery Excellence, Performance & Value Realization: Oversee AI initiatives across technical delivery, business outcomes, adoption, success criteria, budget utilization, risks, and dependencies. Assess whether initiatives are delivering against their original commitments, drive accountability for results, and identify where intervention, reprioritization, or funding adjustments are required. Ensure realized outcomes can be traced back to approved business cases and defined success measures.
 Executive Reporting & Stakeholder Management: Provide the VP of GTO and senior leadership with a consolidated view of the AI program, including roadmap progress, funding utilization, delivery performance, value realization, risks, dependencies, and decisions required. Maintain effective engagement across sponsors, segments, Technology, Enterprise AI, Finance, Risk, and other partners, translating complex information into clear executive insights and recommendations.
 AI-Driven Transformation & Reusable Capabilities: Identify opportunities to fundamentally redesign processes and ways of working through AI and Automation, moving beyond incremental improvements. Drive the development, reuse, and adoption of scalable AI capabilities, standards, playbooks, and common approaches that accelerate delivery and reduce duplication across GTO.

 Required Qualifications
 8+ years of experience across strategy and transformation, technology, AI, program management, product management, or related disciplines, with demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional programs.
 Demonstrated experience leading large-scale AI, Automation, technology, innovation, or transformation programs, including program governance, prioritization, funding, delivery oversight, and performance management.
 Strong strategic and analytical capabilities, with demonstrated experience translating strategy into prioritized programs, roadmaps, business cases, funding recommendations, and measurable outcomes.
 Strong financial acumen, including experience developing and evaluating business cases, cost-benefit analysis, managing budgets and funding, establishing success measures, and assessing value realization.
 Strong understanding of AI platforms and modern AI solution patterns, with sufficient technical fluency to understand delivery plans, challenge assumptions, assess dependencies and risks, and engage credibly with Technology and AI leaders.
 Strong program leadership capabilities, including the ability to oversee multiple concurrent initiatives, establish governance and delivery frameworks, manage complex dependencies, and drive disciplined execution across Business and Technology teams.
 Exceptional executive communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to synthesize complex strategic, financial, business, and technical information into clear insights, recommendations, and decisions for senior leadership.
 Demonstrated ability to influence and challenge senior stakeholders, drive accountability without direct authority, create structure in ambiguous environments, and manage competing strategic priorities.
 Demonstrated use of AI productivity tools and agentic workflows to accelerate analysis, synthesis, reporting, decision-making, and content development.

 Preferred Qualifications
 Experience leading or managing an enterprise-scale AI, Automation, technology, innovation, or transformation program, including prioritization, funding, delivery, and value realization.
 Experience establishing program governance, portfolio prioritization frameworks, business cases, executive reporting, and value-realization models.
 Familiarity with enterprise AI architecture, MLOps/LLMOps, AI evaluation, Responsible AI, model governance, and the considerations involved in moving AI solutions from development into production.
 Experience scaling reusable AI capabilities across multiple teams, business segments, or geographies.
 Experience partnering directly with senior executives on strategy, funding, program performance, prioritization, and enterprise transformation.

jobs.description:
The VP Group Functions Technology (GFT) Finance Systems is accountable for formulating and driving global information services, technology strategies, management, and implementations for Manulife Group Finance (GF) as well as day to day operations for our finance and treasury portfolios. This role is the Information Services lead for the Finance and Treasury and has a clear mandate to identify opportunities to utilize technology to maximize productivity as well as efficiencies while supporting the evolving needs of the business and their clients across Canada, the United States, Japan, Hong Kong and the rest of Asia.  This includes developing the IS application strategy and overseeing its execution to meet goals within agreed targets and budget for GFT Finance Systems. 

 This role is accountable for effectively leading and managing large and complex IS application integrations and the coordination of technical infrastructure projects, ensuring that the communication of requirements and expectations are clear and projects are completed on time and deployed in a controlled and user inclusive manner across the enterprise globally. 

 This role will require a deep understanding of both financial processes and cash management best practices, as well as the ability to drive operational excellence and delivery efficiency.  This role has accountability directly to the SVP & CIO of Group Functions Technology and to provide services to the heads of the various Group Finance Functions and their teams including the VP, Chief Accountant as well the SVP & Treasurer.  

 Position Responsibilities: 

 Individual Accountabilities: 

 Partner with the functions and provide thought leadership, develop and provide authoritative advice related to emerging and innovative solutions. 
 Develop a service oriented team and culture across GFT and collaborate with cross-functional teams to define and prioritize technology requirements for finance and treasury initiatives. 
 Operate within budget targets to add value while ensuring business goals are met. 
 Oversee all technology roles, services, budgets and savings within GFT and manage the relative spend ratio between build and run. 
 Implement technology vision and operating model within GFT. 
 Drive operational excellence and continuous improvement in service management to effectively achieve associated SLA’s and SLO’s and enable the success of the technology strategy for business units throughout the enterprise. 
 Maintain and adhere to governance for Sox compliance, regulators, internal and external auditors as well as all key risk and control standards for Information Risk Management. 
 Execute technology talent strategy and headcount planning across the areas of accountability and the selection, retention and development of senior level professional staff for the GFT group, across Canada and global operating area. 

 Key Shared Accountabilities: 

 Leveraging technology to optimize efficiencies and standardized business processes.  
 In conjunction with the Global Enterprise Architecture & Engineering Office, develop appropriate application architecture standards for Group Functions and enforce adherence.  
 With a focus on key vendors, leverage global practices for the execution of vendor management strategy in coordination with Procurement and vendor management policies.  
 Active participation and input into appropriate Business Continuity Planning, Disaster Recovery, Information Risk and Security globally for GFT.                                                                                                            

 Required Qualifications: 

 Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field. 
 Finance Technology / General Ledger experience is mandatory. 
 15+ years of increasing responsibility in strategy, process or technology oriented areas with deep and broad knowledge of financial services and the insurance industry. 
 Strong understanding of financial and cash management frameworks, regulations, and industry standards. 
 Ability to manage multiple high profile conflicting priorities typically found in a large and complex project portfolio that spans multiple business lines, ensuring deliveries are on time and budget. 
 International exposure and ability to work with a variety of cultures and perspectives.  Senior professional with extensive experience developing and integrating complex services and systems.  
 Strategic thinker, thinks conceptually beyond day-to-day business realities, creates a clear vision for the business and adopts a long-term perspective.  
 First-hand experience in management of unexpected crisis and ensures timely resolution. 
 Ability to engage and influence at all levels of the organization.  Interacts in ways that gain acceptance and commitment, influence opinion and resolve conflicts. 
 Proven interpersonal skills: two-way communications skills (oral and written), ability to build relationships, influence others, work with a diverse internal and international customer base. 
 Solid track record of delivering innovative sustainable technology solutions, reducing costs, increasing productivity. 
 Able to function as an organizational change agent and see beyond current situations towards enterprise-wide higher level process and systems improvements and reengineering departments through leadership, and innovation. 
 Strong services and systems aptitude; demonstrated project management and planning skills; balances strategic skills with tactical execution skills. 
 Strong operations efficiency orientation (process, costing, etc.) and ability to effectively manage ongoing operations within budget targets while identifying opportunities for ongoing efficiency.

jobs.title: Director, Risk Management
jobs.description:
Our Purpose 

 Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential. 

 Title and Summary 

Director, Risk Management 

Overview:
Mastercard is a global technology company in the payments sector. We power payments and provide products and services for individuals and industries all around the world. Our people, technology, data and brand provide the capabilities that drive our success. We believe in connecting people to priceless possibilities.

As a company, we know that our success is driven by the skills, experience, integrity and mindset of the talent we hire. By building an inclusive, world-class culture, our employees have once-in-a-career opportunities to be a part of teams that have a greater impact on our community and our world. We invite you to join our team to find out how you too can start something priceless. 

Role Description:
The Digital Asset Risk & Compliance team is looking for a Director, Operational Risk & Controls to help build and operate Mastercard’s Second Line operational risk and control capabilities for digital assets.
The role will establish a consistent approach to identifying, assessing, monitoring and reporting operational risks across Mastercard’s digital asset strategy, products and operations. The Director will partner with the First Line to establish and maintain effective controls, risk and control self-assessments, control testing and monitoring in line with Mastercard policies and standards.
The Director will also support BVNK’s integration into Mastercard by aligning operational risk frameworks, controls, governance and reporting while preserving the ability of the business to grow and innovate.

Role:
Digital Asset Operational Risk & Controls
• Build and operate the operational risk and controls capability for Digital Assets and BVNK.
• Partner with the First Line to identify material operational risks and establish effective controls, monitoring, and escalation.
• Lead risk assessments, RCSAs, control reviews, and issue management across digital asset products, operations, technology, and third-party providers.
• Assess control effectiveness and identify emerging risks, control weaknesses, and opportunities for improvement.
• Establish practical and scalable approaches to monitoring, testing, reporting, and remediation
Governance, Reporting & Business Partnership
• Integrate operational risk considerations into strategy, product development, operating model decisions, and business growth.
• Establish governance and reporting that provides management with a clear view of risks, controls, issues, and required actions.
• Partner across Product, Technology, Operations, Finance, Compliance, Security, and Risk to support responsible growth.
• Provide independent challenge while helping the business develop practical and scalable solutions.
• Promote a strong risk and control culture across Mastercard and BVNK.

BVNK Integration
• Build the long-term operational risk and controls capability for Digital Assets as part of BVNK's integration into Mastercard.
• Assess current-state practices and identify priority enhancements based on business growth, risk profile, and regulatory expectations.
• Align governance, RCSAs, control monitoring, testing, issue management, and reporting with Mastercard standards.
• Track integration commitments and remediation plans through completion.
• Drive simplification, scalability, and automation of operational risk and control activities.

All About You:
• Experience in Operational Risk, Controls, Audit, Compliance, Risk Management, or a related discipline.
• Demonstrated ability to build and enhance risk and control frameworks, including risk assessments, controls, testing, monitoring, and issue management.
• Strong understanding of Second Line oversight, independent challenge, governance, and risk appetite.
• Ability to identify material risks, assess control effectiveness, and drive practical improvements.
• Experience partnering across business, product, operations, technology, and risk functions.
• Strong stakeholder management and ability to influence without direct authority.
• Ability to simplify complex issues and translate them into clear actions, decisions, and reporting.

jobs.title: Sr. Director, HR Global Operations
jobs.description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

 What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

 Position Summary 

 The Senior Director, HR Global Operations, provides strategic direction, integrated leadership, and end-to-end accountability across multiple HR Operations disciplines. Reporting to the Vice President, Employee Care, this role leads Benefits Operations, Talent Acquisition Operations, Workforce Administration (e.g., reduction in force, personnel records management), and specialized HR operational support.
 This role is an enterprise and operational leader, not the primary subject-matter expert or day-to-day practitioner within each discipline. The Senior Director leads through functional leaders and subject-matter experts, setting strategy, priorities, governance, performance expectations, and resource direction while ensuring each area maintains the technical depth required for effective delivery.

 The Senior Director translates enterprise HR strategy into an integrated HR Operations agenda and holds the collective organization accountable for accurate, timely, compliant, and employee-centered service delivery. The role creates the HR Operations technology and continuous improvement strategy, identifies cross-functional dependencies, resolves competing priorities, removes barriers, and ensures matters requiring specialized expertise are owned and addressed by the appropriate functional leader.

 As the senior HR Operations leader, the position advises HR and business leadership on service delivery, operational risk, workforce needs, process effectiveness, and employee experience. The role partners across Employee Care, HR Centers of Excellence, HR Technology, HR Business Partners, Legal, Privacy, Payroll, Finance, and other enterprise functions to strengthen controls and advance scalable solutions.

 Organizational Scope
 Benefits Operations
 Talent Acquisition Operations
 Special Workforce Actions Team (aka Workforce Administration)
 Specialized HR operational support, including Global Mobility & Immigration

 Leadership Model:  The Senior Director is accountable for overall strategy, integration, governance, prioritization, performance, resource direction, and talent across the portfolio. Functional leaders remain accountable for subject-matter expertise, technical decisions, and day-to-day execution within their respective disciplines.
 Key Responsibilities

 Portfolio Strategy and Leadership 
 Establish and execute the multi-year strategy and operating model for HR Operations, aligned with enterprise HR priorities, workforce needs, and business objectives.
 Set shared direction across Benefits, Talent Acquisition, Workforce Administration, and other assigned capabilities, relying on functional leaders for discipline-specific design and execution.
 Translate enterprise HR programs and policies into coordinated operational priorities.
 Define decision rights, service boundaries, escalation paths, and cross-team dependencies.
 Advise senior HR and business leaders on operational priorities, service trends, risks, capacity, and investment needs.

 Integrated Service Delivery 
 Direct overall delivery and continuous improvement across the portfolio, holding functional leaders accountable for their respective areas rather than personally owning discipline-level execution.
 Establish common governance, service standards, and operating rhythms while preserving appropriate functional ownership.
 Reduce fragmentation, strengthen handoffs, and improve the end-to-end employee and leader experience.
 Ensure complex matters are routed to the appropriate experts, resolved through clear escalation, and elevated for leadership decisions when required.
 Balance enterprise consistency with business, workforce, and jurisdictional requirements.

 Governance, Risk and Performance 
 Establish portfolio-level policies, controls, performance expectations, and governance practices that enable consistent execution and appropriate risk management.
 Convene and align Legal, Privacy, Payroll, HR Centers of Excellence, and other experts to identify and mitigate operational, regulatory, financial, and employee experience risks.
 Maintain leadership visibility into service performance, material risks, control issues, recurring defects, and remediation plans.
 Set organizational goals and measures across quality, timeliness, accuracy, customer experience, risk, capacity, productivity, and cost.
 Make cross-functional priority and resource decisions based on business need, service demand, risk, and expected value.

 Operational Excellence and Transformation 
 Sponsor modernization and simplification through process redesign, automation, analytics, AI-enabled capabilities, and improved self-service.
 Set cross-functional priorities with HR Technology and enterprise teams while functional leaders define detailed requirements and lead implementation within their disciplines.
 Identify opportunities to consolidate fragmented processes, eliminate unnecessary manual work, and create scalable practices.
 Use operational data, employee feedback, case trends, and control outcomes to direct continuous improvement.
 Develop operating plans, resource strategies, budget recommendations, and investment priorities for the organization.

 People and Organizational Leadership 
 Lead, coach, and develop a multi-disciplinary organization through functional leaders and senior subject-matter experts, preserving clear technical ownership within each discipline.
 Set clear expectations for ownership, collaboration, customer orientation, decision-making, and accountability.
 Build leadership capability, organizational depth, and succession readiness across Canadian HR Operations.
 Create an inclusive, high-performing environment in which leaders are empowered to make decisions and accountable for results.
 Assess portfolio-wide capability and make decisions on structure, roles, skills, capacity, and resource deployment as business needs evolve.

 Executive and Cross-Functional Partnership 
 Translate complex operational issues, risks, and trends into decision-ready recommendations for senior leaders.
 Influence priorities and solutions across teams where direct authority may not exist.
 Represent HR operational requirements in enterprise planning, transformation, and governance forums.
 Lead initiatives requiring coordination across multiple HR disciplines and stakeholder groups.

 Minimum Job Qualifications 
 Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience.
 Typically, 13+ years of progressive professional experience in HR operations, shared services, employee services, talent acquisition operations, HR transformation, or a related discipline.
 Typically, 6+ years of diversified leadership, planning, communication, organization, and people-management experience.
 Demonstrated experience leading a portfolio of HR disciplines or operational teams through managers, functional leaders, and senior subject-matter experts; deep practitioner expertise in every discipline is not required.
 Experience establishing operating models, governance practices, operational policies, performance measures, budgets, and service-delivery standards.
 Demonstrated success leading complex, cross-functional transformation or continuous-improvement initiatives in a large, matrixed organization.
 Strong understanding of HR operational risk, controls, data privacy, and compliance considerations, with the judgment to engage the appropriate experts.
 Ability to use data, service insights, and cost-benefit analysis to guide priorities and improve organizational performance.
 Executive-level communication and influence skills, including the ability to frame decision-ready recommendations.

 Preferred Qualifications 
 Experience leading HR operations or supporting a geographically distributed workforce.
 Broad leadership exposure across two or more of the following: Talent Acquisition, Employee Care, Global Mobility, HR Case Management, or HR Shared Services.
 Experience leading HR service-delivery transformation, process automation, analytics, or AI-enabled operational improvement.
 Experience managing vendor-supported HR services or third-party relationships.
 Experience partnering with HR Technology teams on platform enhancements, integrations, workflow optimization, or digital employee experiences.
 Bilingual English and French capability is an asset where relevant to the supported workforce.

 Critical Leadership Capabilities 
 Portfolio leadership: Sets shared direction across distinct disciplines, enables functional experts to lead their areas, and holds leaders accountable for integrated results.
 Enterprise and country-level perspective: Connects enterprise HR strategy with Canadian workforce and operational requirements.
 Operational judgment: Balances employee experience, service, cost, risk, and compliance while engaging experts for technical decisions.
 Executive influence: Communicates complex operational topics clearly and provides actionable recommendations.
 Transformation leadership: Leads teams through operating-model, technology, and process change.
 Systems thinking: Understands how HR policies, processes, technologies, data, and services interact across the employee lifecycle.
 Talent leadership: Builds organizational capability, develops leaders, and strengthens succession depth.
 Data-driven management: Uses performance measures, service trends, risk indicators, and employee insights to shape decisions.
