jobs.title: Director, Cash Management
jobs.description:
Job Description 

 What is the opportunity? 
 This Director-level position provides strategic leadership and operational oversight for cash management operations supporting RBC's global Capital Markets and Retail nostro accounts. The role combines deep technical expertise in intraday liquidity risk management with leadership capabilities to manage complex stakeholder relationships across Corporate Treasury, trading desks, operations teams, and external financial market infrastructures. The incumbent is responsible for ensuring operational excellence in daily cash positioning, developing and maintaining contingency playbooks, and establishing robust measurement and monitoring frameworks that support regulatory compliance and enterprise liquidity risk management objectives.

 What will you do? 

 Intraday Liquidity Management & Operations 
 Provide strategic oversight and direction for the monitoring of cash flows as they relate to trades, transactions, and payments required for accurate positioning, forecasting, and funding of nostro accounts globally under prescribed guidelines and procedures
 Ensure operational capabilities for frequent monitoring of payment and settlement flows during the day while managing the timing of liquidity outflows where possible, including real-time monitoring and escalation procedures to Designated Liquidity Managers
 Demonstrate ability to identify and estimate unsettled items through intraday nostro reconciliation to determine additional intraday liquidity requirements at any point in time
 Monitor and track all time-sensitive payments (TSP) throughout the day and ensure timely settlement, including managing delays or promoting payments to improve intraday liquidity position with FMIs as permitted
 Monitor cash balances at FMIs to ensure positions remain within both maximum long and short intraday position limits where established
 Oversee daily maximum intraday liquidity usage observation and reporting to oversight functions within reasonable timeframes
 Lead the compilation of cash flow forecasts for funding and intraday collateral needs, demonstrating capabilities to forecast key intraday liquidity risk items for large time-sensitive payments

 Risk Management & Controls 
 Act as subject matter expert for FMI relationships, including FMI operating procedures, rule books, credit requirements, and understanding of business line FMI usage in support of Recovery and Resolution requirements
 Identify cash flow errors or potential value at risk to the Bank and manage to resolution or escalate to senior management with clear recommendations
 Ensure monitoring and management of intraday liquidity resources made available to resolve intraday demands, including demonstrating ability to transfer cash from central bank accounts or pledge/lodge collateral at discount windows
 Maintain reporting to show available cash or collateral at the start of the day and real-time if requested to oversight functions
 Oversee the monitoring of total value of time-sensitive payments settled each day and the timing and recurrence of material TSP
 Ensure compliance with prescribed risk appetite requirements, limits, and thresholds; report and escalate excesses to any established metrics in a timely manner

 Strategic Planning & Contingency Management 
 Maintain the operational aspects of intraday FMI playbooks to document scenario and procedural response strategies and escalation of intraday events in times of stress in coordination with local and enterprise Liquidity Contingency Plans
 Lead the development of contingency playbooks and support asset monetization strategies to ensure timely access to liquidity resources
 Provide leadership in the review and acknowledgment of liquidity stress testing and parameter documents as subject matter expert prior to GRM review and approval
 Support Corporate Treasury and Capital Markets Treasury in establishing appropriate liquidity buffers for intraday liquidity risk based on stress parameters

 Stakeholder Management & Reporting 
 Deliver high-quality subject matter expertise to Retail and Capital Markets teams in relation to projects and ad hoc requests involving the funding and liquidity of nostro accounts
 Effectively interact with and provide leadership engagement with TS Funding & Liquidity Trading Desk, Account Managers, Branches, Trading Operations staff, and correspondent banks in the handling and resolution of inquiries and discrepancies
 Update and deliver daily and monthly reports to Traders, Corporate Treasury, Capital Markets Treasury, and senior management in a timely manner
 Provide data to support the monitoring, measuring, and reporting of material intraday liquidity risk exposures potentially on a real-time basis as agreed with Corporate Treasury
 Lead/coordinate efforts with IT partners and Model Development Owners to ensure supplied data is accurate and complete

 Systems & Process Improvement 
 Apply expert knowledge of Treasury Operations systems (CLM, IntelliMatch, Rimm, RATS, Prowide, BESS) and external systems (CDSX, CARS, LYNX, ACSS) to effectively calculate and manage the bank's current, overnight, and forward positions
 Lead the identification of departmental system or process changes to streamline and improve service and efficiency
 Identify service gaps provided by Cash Management to internal clients as well as service gaps from correspondent banks and make recommendations to senior management for improvement
 Support the process of creating, updating, and maintaining desk procedures and operational documentation

 Leadership & Team Development 
 Provide leadership and direction to cash management teams, fostering a strong commitment to teamwork, open two-way communication, and positive staff morale
 Ensure strict adherence to policies and regulatory requirements across the team
 Uphold the reputation of RBC and Operations at all times and ensure timely escalation of operational risk or loss events, control deficiencies, and risks

 Regulatory & Compliance 
 Ensure compliance with OSFI Liquidity Adequacy Requirements Chapter 7 - Intraday Liquidity Monitoring Tools and all applicable regulatory requirements
 Participate in the review of the material FMI list and provide relevant attestations as outlined in policy requirements
 Support regulatory submissions and intraday liquidity reporting requirements

 What do you need to succeed? 

 Required: 
 10+ yrs of experience with advanced understanding of Cash Management processes, procedures, and intraday liquidity risk management principles
 Extensive knowledge of Capital Markets and banking operations/trading activity
 Deep understanding of market infrastructure including Settlement Agents, Nostro Agents, Clearing Houses, and Large Value Payment Systems
 Comprehensive understanding of operational risks, impacts, and controls in a capital markets environment
 Proven leadership experience managing complex operational processes and teams
 Strong knowledge of BCBS Principles for Sound Liquidity Risk Management and OSFI regulatory requirements

 Preferred: 
 Professional designation (CTP, CFA, FRM) or equivalent advanced degree
 Experience with regulatory stress testing and recovery/resolution planning
 Background in both Capital Markets and Retail banking operations
 Experience managing relationships with central banks and major FMIs

 What’s in it for you? 
 We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. jobs.title: Director, Capital Markets Operational Risk Controls and Governance
jobs.description:
Job Description 

 What is the opportunity? 
 Operational Risk Controls and Governance (ORC&G) acts as trusted advisors and subject-matter experts for the Capital Markets businesses and COO groups on risk mitigation practices, providing guidance to front line units on controls best practices.

 We are looking for an eager and high-performing individual to oversee the maintenance of an effective operational risk management program within CM. This role will focus on controls assurance by ensuring the consistent application of the Operational Risk Framework and associated policies in the business, and supporting a culture of risk ownership, awareness and management in the business and functions.   

 In addition to supporting the broader operational risk mandate, this role will have the unique opportunity to gain exposure to every business and control function within RBC Capital markets, and to work directly with Senior CM leaders by managing the full end to end governance of the North American New Business Committees, as well as supporting ongoing efforts to establish clear and concise reporting.

 What will you do? 
 Strategic Risk Governance & Change Management: 
 CM-sponsored Change Initiatives: Participate in the end-to-end detailed risk assessment process for CM change initiatives through input into and membership of the NBC, IRP, and PAR processes, per procedures outlined in the CM Risk Assessment of Change Initiatives procedures document, and the NBC Standing Order;
 Review post-NBC control documentation status, to ensure that new or amended controls that were required to support an NBC-approved initiative have been implemented and are confirmed to be effective, either through design review of controls or through robust post-implementation reviews of NBC initiatives;
 Monitor North American NBC pipeline via periodic meetings with NBC Secretaries to review conditionally approved, in progress papers, items placed on hold, and performing escalation with CM stakeholders where required;
 Oversee the execution of periodic product risk assessments and post-implementation review for CM initiatives;
 Lead and co-ordinate remediation for Second Line of Defense (2LOD) and Internal Audit (3LOD) Findings assigned to ORC&G, ensuring timely closure of issues and action plans.

 Operational Risk Event (ORE) Management: 
 Oversee the capture, analysis, and reporting of Operational Risk Events and Issues/Actions across Capital Markets, working closely with Line of Business leads and Managers to ensure compliance with Enterprise Policy and Standing Order requirements.
 Lead thematic reviews of OREs to identify areas that may warrant highlighting in management reporting or additional control evaluation/enhancement/new control creation;
 Establish governance frameworks and oversight mechanisms for the capture, analysis, and reporting of Operational Risk Events and Issues/Actions across Capital Markets, ensuring compliance with Enterprise Policy and Standing Order requirements and driving consistency in ORE management practices;
 Set strategic direction for 1st Line of Defense (LOD) guidance in managing and mitigating operational risk, establishing clear accountability frameworks and ensuring alignment and consistency in the regional execution of operational risk tools, processes, and practices with the Global ORC&G approach;
 Oversee the development, delivery, and continuous enhancement of enterprise-wide training and awareness programs to embed a control-conscious culture and ensure clear understanding of control ownership, internal control management principles, and expected conduct, behaviours, roles, and responsibilities across the business;

 Enterprise Policy & Change Governance: 
 Support the Managing Director ORC&G through participation in projects to review and implement new enterprise policies that impact Capital Markets in North America, which may include assisting in the establishment of procedures/guidelines, liaising with internal and/or external parties to understand requirements and define parameters;
 Lead engagement with the appropriate Centre of Governance groups to provide input into the development of new/changed enterprise policies, clarifying proposed requirements in order to initiate discussions with the in-scope business units to assess the impact on the CM business processes and controls;
 Provide interpretation and guidance to broader ORC&G Team on Enterprise Methodology changes impacting Controls Management, Risk and Control Self Assessment (RCSA), OREs and Issues Management.

 Reporting: 
 Direct the development and production of monthly and quarterly Operational Risk reporting, including trend analysis, executive commentary, and business insights to support Regional, Legal Entity, and Line of Business governance reporting requirements; 
 Synthesize ORE data, control assurance results, assessment findings, and emerging risk trends into strategic insights and recommendations for senior leadership, identifying areas warranting executive escalation, policy intervention, or enterprise-wide action;
 Establish analytics and management information standards to support informed decision-making and governance across the operational risk portfolio;
 Oversee and review information consolidation for ad-hoc regulatory reporting/regulator information requests, as required.

 Relationship Management: 
 Spearhead engagement with CM Senior Management, Business and Functional Heads in matters relating to the internal risk and control environment.
 Represent ORC&G at the New Business Committee

 What you need to succeed? 
 Minimum Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant experience in Finance, Engineering, Science or Math desirable
 7 - 10 years of experience in Project Management, Risk Management, Audit and/or Financial Services industry
 Strong knowledge of trading and supporting systems used within Capital Markets. 
 Proven people management & development skills; ability to work effectively in a project team environment, demonstrated facilitation and leadership skills, strong listening and interview skills. 
 Good working knowledge of Capital Markets operational functions and processes
 Detailed understanding of RBC Capital Markets organizational structure (front office sales and trading, middle office, product control, BCS, regulatory/compliance, etc.)
 Self-motivated, able to work independently and within a team
 Ability to prioritize, plan and execute work to meet tight deadlines
 Strong innovative, problem-solving and analytical skills; a self-starter capable of functioning in an autonomous manner. 
 Capable of building strong relationships with clients and stakeholders across the enterprise

 What will you do? 
 Central Point for Issue Lifecycle Management 
 Serve as the primary point of contact for all non-financial risk issues for Capital Markets businesses. Own and manage the complete issue lifecycle from initial identification through resolution and closure.
 Establish and maintain processes to document all identified issues with clear descriptions, root causes, and potential impacts on business.
 Document lessons learned from resolved issues to inform preventive strategies.

 Tracking and Monitoring 
 Maintain comprehensive issue registries and dashboards, tracking the status of all identified issues/risks from inception through resolution. This includes monitoring remediation timelines, validating the effectiveness of corrective actions, and providing regular status updates to stakeholders.
 Identify patterns and trends in operational risk issues to support strategic risk mitigation.

 Escalation and Reporting 
 Escalate critical or overdue issues through appropriate governance channels and preparing summary reports for senior management, risk committees, and regulatory bodies as needed.
 Ensure transparency regarding risk status and trend analysis.
 Maintain audit trails and documentation for all issues and remediation activities.

 Governance and Compliance 
 Work within RBC's operational risk governance framework, ensuring alignment with regulatory requirements and internal policies.
 Coordinate with compliance, audit, and business units to ensure consistent application of risk management standards.
 Maintain compliance with internal policies and external regulatory reporting requirements.

 Stakeholder Coordination 
 Collaborate with business units, control functions, and senior leadership to address root causes, develop remediation plans, and implement preventive measures.
 Facilitate communication between technical teams and risk management to ensure issues are resolved effectively.

 Perform root cause analysis to identify systemic weaknesses and systemic risks and support data analytics initiatives to enhance predictive risk identification.

 What do you need to succeed? 
 A minimum 5 years of related experience with in-depth knowledge of Capital Markets business, and/or non-financial risk management.

jobs.title: Senior Director, AI Product Management
jobs.description:
Job Description 

 Senior Director, AI Product Management 

 What's the opportunity? 
 We're looking for a product leader who can turn a strategic product vision into shipped reality at scale. As Senior Director, AI Product Management, you will own user-focused product success for RBC's internal Agentic AI platform, defining the product vision and translating it into a tangible roadmap, community, and ecosystem. You will build discipline around ensuring relentless customer focus and a business-strategy lens on what we build and why. You will lead a team of Product Managers and own Voice of the Customer, feature prioritization, adoption and community building around the product across RBC.
 You will be expected to set the operating rhythm, make the hard tradeoff and resourcing calls, and hold a quality bar — bringing the credibility that comes from having built and shipped AI products at scale, not just managed roadmaps.

 Your responsibilities will include: 
 Team leadership: Leading and developing Director-level leads (across Product Strategy & Roadmap, Community & Adoption, Ecosystem & Partnerships) and the teams beneath them, with clear career paths and succession

 Integrated delivery: Owning a single execution plan that aligns roadmap delivery, community programs, and partnership milestones to one cadence

 Operating cadence: Establishing and running sprint reviews, quarterly planning, and OKR setting and tracking

 Tradeoff and escalation ownership: Serving as the primary escalation point for cross-pillar dependencies, tradeoffs, and resourcing decisions

 Product quality: Maintaining acceptance criteria, release gates, and documentation standards across the squad

 Adoption and outcomes: Using analytics, telemetry, and adoption measurement to drive decisions and report progress, risks, and resource needs

 Ecosystem health: Ensuring the community and partnership programs sustain engagement and healthy adoption across the RBC user base

 You're our ideal candidate if you: 
 Have 10+ years of product management experience, including 3+ years leading multi-team product organizations as a manager of managers

 Have a track record of customer discovery and translating user needs into product strategy and prioritization

 Have hands-on experience delivering end-user facing AI products — ideally generative or agentic AI — at production scale

 Have run large-scale internal or enterprise product launches with measurable adoption outcomes

 Bring strong operational discipline: agile delivery, OKR frameworks, and release management

 Are data-driven, comfortable with analytics, telemetry, and adoption metrics as the basis for product decisions

 Have financial services experience, or the ability to rapidly develop it  - understanding how banking employees work and the regulatory constraints on internal tooling

 Have a working knowledge of LLM evaluation, prompt engineering, or RAG architecture — sufficient to shape product decisions and engage technical teams

 Nice to have: 
 MBA or Master's in a technical or business discipline

 Product management certification (CSPO, SAFe, AIPM, or Pragmatic Institute)

 Background in platform engineering or developer experience teams

 Experience in a major bank's technology or digital transformation function

 What's in it for you: 
 Drive AI transformation at one of Canada's largest and most respected financial institutions, with exposure to senior leadership across RBC

 Be part of a newly formed, high-impact function within RBC's AI Group alongside experienced transformation leaders

 A comprehensive Total Rewards Program including bonuses and flexible benefits, competitive compensation, commissions, and stock options where applicable

 Leaders who support your development through coaching and managing opportunities

 Ability to make a difference and lasting impact from a local-to-global scale

 About the AI Group: 
 RBC's AI Group is the AI accelerator for RBC, with a focus on driving the shift from early-stage AI projects to scaled, client outcomes that amplify the impact of RBC's people. In addition to helping scale the biggest AI opportunities at RBC, the AI Group is responsible for advancing research into emerging use cases across generative and agentic AI, while maintaining expertise in security, responsible AI and regulatory expectations.

 What is the Opportunity? 
 This role establishes a strong link between Role Design, Technology partners, and Personal and Commercial Banking partners to enable the optimization, development, and delivery of digital tools and applications used by Canadian Banking advisors.

 Primary Focus 
 Drive horizontal strategy across all CRM and Branch Platforms to ensure integrated and consistent advisor experiences
 Work across LOBs, including Personal Bank, Commercial and Private Banking on defining strategic vision and transformational roadmap for next generation of use cases and capabilities
 Establishing the rigor for the ongoing management and evolution of the platform and realization of business benefits.

 Responsible for strategic alignment across major, Big Rock/large initiatives and digitization with Client360 Platform.
 Ensure technology roadmaps align with advisor needs, RBC strategic direction and enable engagement across preferred channels
 Establish and maintain strategic governance and reporting across platforms, driving alignment between business objectives and technology delivery

 Secondary Focus 
 Collaborate with AI team partners to integrate Actionable insights into the Advisor’s path into Client360 (and other Advisor platforms) for enabling pre-dive, post-dive and in the moment efficiencies and effectiveness
 Lead rapid POC development cycles with authority to "fail fast / scale fast," designing multi-agent interactions across vendor agents, enterprise agents, and native/internal agents to AI-enable advisors through integration to the existing suite of technologies used by advisors
 Act as Integrator to Client360 / Advisor Platform for agentic workflows—owning use case shaping through validated solution patterns, defining success metrics, and driving iteration based on advisor feedback and usage metrics

 Advocate on behalf of the advisor community in enterprise tool development and provide ongoing feedback loops
 Develop business-centric programs and reporting that enhance daily advisor operations
 Identify stakeholder needs, negotiate priorities across competing interests, and collaborate with developers/partners to implement requirements effectively
 Keep business and technology stakeholders apprised of roadmap status and gather feedback
 Deploy processes and technologies that safeguard Advisors and Clients (compliance and regulatory requirements)
 Conduct advisor research and act as the voice of the Advisor community in platform development
 Negotiate and prioritize enhancements to mitigate technical and financial risk
 Partner with Technology, Procurement, and third-party vendors to execute strategic initiatives

This includes staying current with Salesforce product roadmaps and identifying opportunities to integrate new FSC innovations into Client360's strategic direction.
 Business Strategy & Bridge from Strategy to Implementation

The candidate must be able to develop comprehensive business strategies aligned with organizational objectives while maintaining a keen understanding of implementation realities. This includes translating strategic visions into actionable roadmaps, managing stakeholder expectations, prioritizing initiatives based on business impact and resource constraints, and ensuring accountability for delivery. Experience in leading cross-functional teams to execute complex transformation programs is essential.
 Expert-Level Understanding of Client360 – Depth of Implemented Capabilities 
 Possesses deep, hands-on knowledge of Client360's current functionality, architecture, and implementations across diverse user groups and business units. The candidate should understand how different user personas leverage Client360, identify capability gaps, recognize overlaps, and articulate both strengths and limitations. This expertise enables informed decision-making about platform enhancements, feature prioritization, and strategic investments. The ability to draw on real-world implementation examples to validate strategy is critical.
 Exceptional Executive Communication & Presentation Skills 
 Capable of distilling complex technical and strategic concepts into compelling, clear narratives for C-suite and board-level audiences. The ideal candidate can prepare polished executive presentations, develop strategic briefs, and communicate across diverse stakeholder groups with varying levels of technical sophistication. This includes strong data storytelling, ability to frame business cases persuasively, and the confidence to present recommendations with conviction while remaining open to feedback.

jobs.title: VP, People
jobs.description:
Rewind is a service that protects the critical data that powers businesses of all sizes. Our focus is on backing up data that lives in the cloud - in apps like Jira, GitHub, Confluence and Shopify. We are backed by Insight Partners, Inovia, Bessemer and Atlassian Ventures and are proud to be recognized as one of Canada's 50 fastest growing technology companies ( 2023 Deloitte Fast 50 ). We invite you to read our startup story to learn where we came from and where we’re going.
 Read about our mission, story and values here.
To find out more about our perks, click here.
Some of our Blogs might help you get a better understanding of what we do here. You can find them all here.
 Thriving at Rewind: 
 We embrace the fast-paced, ever-changing nature of startup life. If you love working with speed, agility, and creativity, you’ll feel right at home here. Here's what it takes to succeed with us:
 Team-First Mentality: We put teamwork at the core of everything we do, believing that we are better when we are together. Success is shared, and when the team wins, we all win.

 Performance-Driven Mindset: We are proactive, goal-oriented, and focused on delivering tangible, high-quality results. We go beyond meeting expectations - we aim to exceed them.

 Flexible Work-Life Approach: We encourage balance and understand the need to recharge. While we stay agile for urgent needs, we make sure there's time to recover and enjoy life.

 Customer Centricity: Our commitment to customers shapes everything we do. We listen, build relationships, and innovate - from our dedicated customer support team to our engineers, everyone at our company is focused on solving problems that matter most to our users.

 Taking Initiative: We value ownership and proactive problem-solving. We encourage team members to think creatively, take ownership, and lead improvements. Your ideas and actions drive our success.

 We Make Time for Fun: We work hard and make time to enjoy the journey. It’s not just about hitting milestones—it’s about making the experience rewarding along the way.

 Rewind's mission is to help businesses protect their most valuable digital assets. As we
 continue to scale, we are building the systems, leadership capabilities, and operating practices
 that enable us to grow intentionally while maintaining our culture and values.
 The Vice President, People, leads the design and execution of people strategies and systems that scale with the business. This role ensures our people practices, leadership capabilities, and operating model enable high performance, clear accountability, and sustained growth.

 You are accountable for translating Rewind's values into durable systems, meaningful people
 metrics, and a consistent operating cadence that supports how the company attracts, develops, and retains exceptional talent. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who enjoys building structure where it matters, challenging assumptions, and building culture.

 What You'll Do 
 People Strategy & Culture Stewardship
 Set and evolve Rewind's people strategy in support of company goals, growth plans, and long-term sustainability.

 Act as a trusted advisor to the CEO and executive team on organizational health, talent risks, leadership effectiveness, and culture decisions.

 Translate Rewind's values into operating principles, decision frameworks, and leader expectations.

 Partner with leaders to maximize the effectiveness of distributed teams and leverage the benefits of hybrid work.

 Develop and implement organizational health assessments and action plans that strengthen leadership effectiveness, employee engagement, and business performance.

 People Operations & Execution
 Own the operating model of the People team, including structure, capacity,prioritization, and delivery standards.

 Design and implement people processes and operating rhythms that support effective planning, decision-making, and execution across the organization.

 Align People team priorities with company objectives and business needs.

 Establish clear forums and cadences, including talent reviews, leadership reviews, and retrospectives that connect people insights to business decisions.

 Ensure leaders across the company have clarity on expectations, accountability, and follow-through as the company scales.

 People Metrics & Organizational Insights
 Define, track, and continuously improve People team KPIs, including engagement, retention, hiring effectiveness, and performance outcomes.

 Develop and maintain dashboards and reporting that connect people metrics to business outcomes and provide actionable insights to leaders and the executive team.

 Use people data and operational insights to inform discussions regarding organizational capacity, productivity, workforce planning, and organizational health.

 Provide strategic recommendations and action plans based on trends and emerging risks.

 Remote-First & Distributed Work
 Own and evolve Rewind's remote and hybrid work strategy to ensure clarity, equity, and consistency across teams.

 Design systems and norms that support strong performance, collaboration, and connection in a distributed environment.

 Regularly assess what is working, what is not, and where adjustments are needed as the company grows.

 Talent, Performance & Leadership
 Oversee talent acquisition, onboarding, performance management, learning and development, and succession planning.

 Coach leaders to be strong people managers who set clear goals, provide meaningful feedback, and hold themselves accountable.

 Support leadership development with a focus on execution, trust, and growth.

 Ensure performance management practices are consistently applied, including timely feedback, development plans, and decisive action when expectations are not met.

 Mergers, Acquisitions & Organizational Change
 Lead HR due diligence activities for mergers, acquisitions, and strategic transactions.

 Develop and execute people integration strategies, including organization design, change management, communications, and talent retention plans.

 Partner with business leaders to ensure seamless organizational transitions and achievement of business objectives.

 Employee Communications & Change Management
 Develop and execute the company's employee communications strategy and annual communications plan.

 Draft and oversee executive and organizational communications that support change initiatives, reinforce company values, and strengthen employee engagement.

 Ensure consistent, transparent, and timely communication during periods of growth and transformation.

 This role is open for candidate located in Ontario. 

 What You'll Bring 
 Proven experience in a senior people leadership role (VP or Senior Director level) in a scaling technology or SaaS organization that is PE or VC backed.

 Demonstrated success building and scaling people functions and operating models.

 Have built the People function, rather than inheriting a mature one

 Experience in a Canadian or cross-border (Canada and US) workforce

 Strong business acumen with the ability to connect people strategies to business outcomes.

 Demonstrated expertise in organizational design, change management, and organizational effectiveness.

 Experience leading M&A due diligence and post-acquisition integration.

 Experience supporting remote and distributed teams.

 Exceptional communication, influencing, and relationship-building skills.

 Sound judgment and the ability to navigate complex people and organizational situations.

 A pragmatic, hands-on approach and the ability to balance strategic thinking with operational execution.

 Compensation Philosophy 
The actual base salary will vary based on various factors, including market and individual qualifications objectively assessed during the interview process. 
 In some cases, we’re open to hiring at a higher level for the right person and are committed to paying competitively and fairly.
 If your experience is closer to an earlier career stage, we may still consider your application. In that case, we would evaluate the role at a different level within our levelling framework.
 Pay is just one part of the overall compensation at Rewind.

 Why join Rewind 
 At Rewind, you’ll help shape the future of data protection for thousands of businesses. We’re performance-driven, innovative, and not afraid to challenge what’s possible. You’ll join a team that values trust, accountability, and respect for people’s time — and encourages every employee to experiment, think critically, and grow.
 We support innovation through experimentation — including smart use of AI tools — and believe the best ideas come from those who aren’t afraid to push boundaries.

 How Rewind Will Support You 
We know that enjoying the journey is just as important as reaching our goals. We work hard to create a positive, inclusive environment where fun and laughter are part of our everyday routine. We also offer a variety of benefits to support your success both at work and in your personal life which includes but is not limited to: 
 Flexible work hours

 Employee stock options

 Health benefits

 3 weeks vacation

 7 life leave days

 2 Level Up days for professional development

 1 volunteer day

 Summer Fridays and office closed during the holiday break in December

 Paid parental leave

 $2000/year wellness/home office allowance

 $5000/year professional development allowance

 Rewind is committed to building an inclusive, supportive place for you to do the best and most rewarding work of your career. We value how each new hire is an opportunity for us to bring in a different perspective, and we are always eager to further diversify our company. We strongly encourage candidates of all different backgrounds and identities to apply.

 AI Usage 
 Our recruitment process may include the use of artificial intelligence–enabled tools to help manage and review applications efficiently. These tools assist our team, but hiring decisions are ultimately made by human reviewers.

jobs.title: VP, Revenue Operations
jobs.description:
Location: This role can be based anywhere in Canada (excluding Quebec) as a fully remote position. For candidates located in the Vancouver, BC Lower Mainland, there is flexibility to work remote, hybrid, or onsite at our Surrey headquarters. This role is also open to candidates in the USA as a fully remote position.

 Please note that employment is contingent upon the successful completion of reference checks and background checks.

Safe Software is looking for a VP, Revenue Operations to join our Revenue Operations team. As VP, Revenue Operations, you will design and enforce the operating model our entire go-to-market organization runs on, reporting directly to the Chief Revenue Officer and presenting regularly to the board. This is a builder’s mandate: the CRM isn’t fully configured, the forecasting process is mostly informal, the Rules of Engagement are still being written, and the AI tooling stack is unevaluated. You’re not fixing a broken system — you’re building the one Safe’s revenue org will run on for years. We have an immediate opening and are excited to find the right candidate to join our team. 

 About The Team 
 As a part of the Revenue Operations team, you’ll build and lead a function that’s still taking shape — RevOps analysts, a Sales Enablement team, and a broader GTM Enablement capability, five to seven hires in total. Safe builds FME, the only All-Data, Any-AI Enterprise Integration Platform, trusted by 25,000+ enterprise customers in 125+ countries to bring their data to life. Profitable, growing, and scaling toward $250M ARR with a clear path to $700M, Safe is building a multi-motion revenue engine — direct field, inbound and outbound BDR, partner channel, EMEA, and Canada — and it needs a single operating authority to keep those motions from colliding. That’s this role. You’ll report to the CRO and work daily with VP Sales East, VP Sales West, and the EMEA leader, each of whom has strong opinions and moves fast.

 What You’ll Be Doing 
 As VP, Revenue Operations, you will operate at all altitudes — one week presenting forecast accuracy to the board, the next telling a VP Sales their deal doesn’t meet the bar to advance stage, regardless of how the conversation started. Both are the job.

 Rules of Engagement — Ownership & Accountability 
 Write the rules everyone will actually operate inside. Safe is building a multi-motion revenue engine — direct field, inbound BDR, outbound BDR, partner channel, EMEA, Canada — and without clearly defined and enforced Rules of Engagement, those motions conflict, accounts get double-touched, partners get burned, and trust between functions collapses. You write it, socialize it across every stakeholder (including strong-willed VP Sales leaders who will push back), get it approved by the CRO, and enforce it through process design and CRM configuration.

 Define territory and account ownership. Who owns what account, what happens at renewal, how partner and direct conflict is resolved, and what triggers an escalation to the CRO.

 Set lead routing and BDR handoff standards. How inbound and outbound leads are qualified, assigned, accepted, and rejected, with SLA definitions for each stage and accountability for every gate.

 Design the partner co-sell and channel conflict policy. Clear rules for when the partner leads, when direct leads, and how sourcing credit is allocated, reviewed and agreed with the Partner Leader and EMEA Leader at launch.

 Hold the qualification gates. Define MEDDPICC field requirements by stage, what must be true before a deal advances, and what RevOps will kick back regardless of who is asking.

 GTM Enablement 
 Close the ramp gap. At Safe’s current hiring pace across AEs, BDRs, SEs, CSMs, and partners, the difference between a 30-day ramp and a 90-day ramp is a material revenue number — this role owns closing that gap.

 Build the function, not just the content. The Sales Enablement team reports directly into this role. You’ll build it, hire against a capability scorecard, and hold the team accountable to ramp and productivity outcomes, not just content creation.

 Design role-based onboarding. Structured, milestone-gated onboarding tracks for every GTM role — AE, BDR, SE, CSM, and partner — with clear ready-to-carry-quota certification criteria and a defined ramp timeline per role.

 Own the sales methodology and playbook. The single source of truth for how Safe sells — pitch structure, discovery framework, objection handling, competitive positioning, and deal execution standards — updated quarterly with input from the field and calibrated against win/loss data.

 Turn Gong data into a coaching loop. Use Gong and other tooling to create a systematic feedback loop from deal recordings and call reviews to enablement content updates, so the playbook reflects what actually wins, not what the last training deck said.

 Revenue Architecture & AI-Native GTM Stack 
 Give the CRO one version of the truth. Build the weekly, monthly, and quarterly forecasting process — call accuracy, coverage ratios, deal velocity — so the CRO walks into every board meeting with zero surprises.

 Own the numbers that matter. Pipeline model, funnel metrics, win-rate analytics, rep productivity, CAC payback, and NRR by segment and vertical, owned by you, trusted by the board.

 Evaluate and integrate the AI-native GTM stack. CRM (HubSpot), conversation intelligence (Gong), outbound automation, intent data, and agentic AI workflows — owning use-case prioritization, adoption, and value realization across the revenue org. AI architecture, security review, and governance decisions are made in partnership with IT and Engineering.

 Enforce data governance with teeth. Own the data model in CRM, ensuring field hygiene, account hierarchy, and MEDDPICC field consistency across every pod, globally.

 Executive Leadership & Cross-Functional Authority 
 Earn credibility through data, not hierarchy. Working with high-performing, highly opinionated VP Sales leaders is a feature of this role, not a bug — you’ll push back on a VP Sales who wants to move a deal to the wrong stage, enforce an ROE that a regional leader finds inconvenient, and do it in a way that preserves the relationship.

 Present to the board and hold up under questioning. You’ll present pipeline health, forecast accuracy, and GTM efficiency metrics directly to Safe’s board — output that’s clear, accurate, and defensible, from someone who can handle hard questions from investors without flinching.

 Own the cross-functional cadence. Finance, Marketing, CS, Product, and Legal all have legitimate interests in how the GTM org operates — you mediate those interests and own the QBRs, planning cycles, and headcount models that keep the org moving in the same direction.

 Leadership & Impact 
 This is single-threaded ownership of the operating system, not a shared function. You set the Rules of Engagement, own the forecasting methodology, and hold budget and vendor authority over the RevOps and Enablement tooling stack. When a VP Sales and the model disagree, the model doesn’t move without your sign-off — and you carry that authority directly to the CRO and, on a regular cadence, to the board.
 The board stops asking why the number moved. Forecast accuracy becomes predictable enough that variance is the exception the CRO has to explain, not the norm.

 The rules hold under pressure. Rules of Engagement survive contact with a strong-willed VP Sales who wants an exception — and when they don’t, that’s a deliberate call you made, not a gap they found.

 RevOps becomes a real team. What starts as a single-person mandate becomes a functioning function of RevOps, Enablement, and analytics talent that other departments route through by default.

 GTM tooling delivers measurable outcomes. AI and automation investments are evaluated against clear success criteria — rep productivity, pipeline data quality, forecast accuracy, and adoption rates — before scaling. Pilots that don't meet the bar are discontinued; those that do are operationalized.

 Qualifications, Skills, and Competencies 
 Safers come from a variety of backgrounds with a diversity in skills and knowledge. That said, we find that those who are most successful in this role have experience with the following areas.
 Required skills: 
 10–15+ years in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, or GTM Strategy at a scaling B2B SaaS company, at VP or Senior Director level with direct board-level exposure

 Experience building and enforcing a Rules of Engagement framework across multiple GTM motions, including the hard conversations with sales leaders who push back

 A track record presenting pipeline health, forecast, and GTM efficiency metrics directly to a board or equivalent investor group

 Experience holding strong field sales leaders accountable through data and rigor rather than hierarchy

 People leadership experience — hiring, developing, and holding accountable a multi-functional team spanning RevOps analysts and sales enablement

 Ownership of the full RevOps stack — CRM architecture, forecasting model, territory design, quota mechanics, and tooling evaluation

 Strong analytical range: comfortable building a bottoms-up coverage model, explaining CAC payback to a CFO, and translating rep-level data into a board-ready narrative

 Hands-on experience evaluating, piloting, or deploying agentic workflows or AI-assisted tooling in a live GTM environment — including the ability to assess feasibility, data readiness, and security requirements before committing to production

 Deep HubSpot or Salesforce architecture experience, including data model and process enforcement design

 Effective communication skills

 Desired skills / Bonus points: 
 Background in data, infrastructure, or integration software

 Experience with MCP, Salesforce Agentforce, Clay, or similar agentic GTM infrastructure at production scale

 Experience navigating a PE-backed or founder-owned growth inflection from $100M to $250M+

 Familiarity with partner channel economics and co-sell Rules of Engagement design

 Experience building a RevOps function from solo operator to a team of 3–5

 A Bachelor’s degree in a related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience

 About Safe Software 
 Safe Software transforms organizations with FME, the only All-Data Any-AI Enterprise Integration Platform connecting all your data, anywhere, at any velocity. 
 With over 30 years of expertise and 25,000+ enterprise customers across 125+ countries, we simplify your data journey, wherever it leads.
 Founded in 1993, Safe is headquartered in Surrey, BC with over 300 team members and counting. We’re always looking for talented individuals with diverse backgrounds who are determined to learn and grow. Are you ready to join the team?

 Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion 
 Safe Software is an equal opportunity employer and we truly believe that innovation and strength begin with diversity and inclusion. 
 We welcome all candidates regardless of race, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, ability, disability, national or ethnic origin, political belief, religion, or family status. 
 Should you require accommodations during the recruitment process, please contact hr_dept@safe.com.

 Notice Regarding Use of Automated Tools in Hiring 
 At Safe Software, we use automated tools to help us process applications and identify qualified candidates. These tools may assist in screening resumes and summarizing interview content based on the information you provide. This helps our team review applications efficiently while ensuring every candidate is considered based on the requirements of the role.
 Please be assured that the final hiring decision is always made by a member of our team. For more information on how we protect your privacy, please see our policy. If you have questions about this process, please contact us at hr_dept@safe.com.

jobs.title: Head of Toronto AI Center
jobs.description:
Lab Summary: 

 Samsung Research America (SRA) develops next-generation technologies in software, user experience, and services for future products. Headquartered in Silicon Valley with locations across North America, we partner with industry and academia to translate research and innovation into tangible outcomes. We lead in machine intelligence by building AI that is user-centric and physically grounded—AI that understands not just what users want, but their physical context and environment.

 Samsung is uniquely positioned to bring this vision to life through nearly 500 million connected devices we sell annually. Our mission is to holistically integrate AI into connected ecosystems—homes, offices, robotics, and beyond—creating a platform that scales quickly while providing deep contextual understanding and spatial awareness.

   The AI Center in Toronto, Canada plays a pivotal role in developing next-generation software, user experiences, and intelligent services that enrich consumers’ lives. This lab actively contributes to the international research community through publications and presentations at major conferences.

   Areas of Research: 

 Computer Vision

 Contextual/Multi-Modal Modeling

 3D Perception & Scene Understanding

 Inference and Reasoning

 Machine and Deep Learning

 Human Computer Interaction (HCI)

 Natural Language Processing

 Position Summary: 

 Samsung’s AI research team in Toronto is looking for an outstanding and highly self-motivated leader to head the lab. The candidates should have extensive expertise in deep learning, computer vision and physics-based AI.

 The AI research center is a key part of Samsung’s global R&D effort and aims to have direct impact on future Samsung products reaching hundreds of millions of users globally. The candidate will work with a team of research scientists and engineers tackling real-world problems involving Samsung’s Artificial intelligence products. The candidate can also have the opportunity to publish at top-tier conferences in deep learning, computer vision, and language understanding.

 Position Responsibilities: 

 Build, manage, develop, lead, and support the AI research team, with the outcome of high-impact research insights that influence the product roadmap

 Present research findings and insights both within and outside of the company

 Serve as a thought partner with the executive, cross-functional, and line of business leadership teams

 Be an evangelist of research practices throughout the company, influencing partner teams

 Drive innovation programs within the relevant fields of Artificial Intelligence,

jobs.description:

 Sierra is the leading platform for customer-facing AI agents, working with many of the world's biggest brands — including The GAP, Rocket Mortgage, SoFi, Sutter Health, and SoftBank — to transform how they serve customers and grow their businesses. We are primarily an in-person company based in San Francisco, with growing offices across North America, Europe, and Asia.
 We are guided by a set of values that are at the core of our actions and define our culture: Trust, Customer Obsession, Craftsmanship, Intensity, and a commitment to balancing Family along the way.  Job Description: 
 About the role 

 Reporting to the Assistant Vice President, Emerging Risk Management & Strategic Risk Initiatives, the Director, Corporate Risk Information Management is accountable for the oversight of the information management, records management, and data governance policy requirements and underlying programs across Corporate Risk, which includes Enterprise & Operational Risk Management, Insurance & Financial Risk Management, Investment & Credit Risk Management, and the Corporate and DBTS Business Group Risk Office teams. The Director sets direction, maintains the framework and methodology, and holds Information Stewards, Records Officers, Records Custodians, Data Custodians and Risk Office teams accountable so that information assets are properly classified, protected, retained, disposed of, and governed in alignment with the Enterprise Information Management Policy, regulatory expectations, and business needs. The Director leads continuous improvement of the program, including enhancements to tools, and strengthens program governance, effectiveness, and efficiency.

 The Director is the accountable owner for structured and non-structured business records and information assets within Corporate Risk, in line with the Enterprise Information Management Policy.

 The role holds the Records Steward, Records Officer, Data Governance Operational Lead, and Non-Structured Data Information Stewardship accountabilities for Corporate Risk, reflecting the centralized operating model of the function. It provides integrated oversight of information lifecycle management, repository governance, data quality, metadata, reporting, and information risk management, and ensures consistent execution of records and information management requirements across Corporate Risk.

 What you'll be doing 

 Lead information governance, risk, and compliance
 Serve as the accountable lead for Non-Structured Information Management governance for Corporate Risk.
 Maintain the Corporate Risk information management framework, operating guidelines, and standards, aligned to the Enterprise Information Management Policy, and oversee adherence to policy and related control expectations.
 Provide guidance and advice to Business Group Risk Office teams and business leaders when judgement or clarification is required on information governance obligations, risks, and implementation requirements. Provide advice into strategic decisions and program improvements.
 On a quarterly basis, independently evaluate the Corporate Risk information management risk profile, including Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and Key Risk Indicators (KRIs), and report results, material non-compliance, and significant issues to senior management and the Operational Risk and Compliance Committee (ORCC) in a timely manner.
 Oversee and coordinate Corporate Risk's response to Risk Control Self Assessments, audits, compliance reviews, and regulatory examinations, and oversee related issue remediation activities related to information management.
 Prepare an annual report to senior management and ORCC on the status of the information management, records management, and data governance program.
 Establish, maintain, and continually enhance the oversight and monitoring frameworks for the program.
 Monitor and benchmark Corporate Risk information management practices against industry standards, regulatory expectations, and best practices, and assess complex information risk issues to guide solution recommendations.
 Develop and own the short- and mid-term strategy and roadmap for information management, records management, and data governance in Corporate Risk, aligned to enterprise and Business Group strategy, and provide significant input to Corporate Risk's strategic and long-term plans.
 Set program roll out objectives and plan and prioritize program resources, milestones, and dependencies across Corporate Risk.

 Records and information lifecycle management
 Direct and oversee records management activities, including records classification, retention, legal holds, disposition, and remediation planning.
 Perform and oversee Records Officer responsibilities for Corporate Risk, retaining accountability for consistent execution of records management requirements, guidance, monitoring, and issue follow-up.
 Oversee Records Impact Assessments (RIAs) and Records Management Risk Reviews when new or changed processes, systems, repositories, vendors, or operating models may affect the creation, storage, access, retention, transfer, or disposition of Corporate Risk business records, and provide guidance on complex or high-risk cases.
 Oversee the maintenance of records and repository inventories and ensure ownership and stewardship assignments remain current.
 Determine how Corporate Risk business records are identified, classified, captured, stored, protected, retained, and disposed of, and hold Records Custodians accountable for applying those determinations.
 Make final decisions within Corporate Risk on record designation, retention and disposition, legal hold implementation, and exceptions to records requirements, and escalate only matters that require enterprise policy interpretation or an exception to enterprise policy.

 Advance data governance and repository oversight
 Provide oversight and approval of Data Governance artifacts and Business Impact Statements prepared by Information Stewards.
 Lead data quality, metadata, business glossary, lineage, classification, and critical information inventory practices, including the related standards and methodology.
 Monitor and report Data Governance KPIs and oversee remediation of identified issues.
 Lead governance of SharePoint, Teams, shared mailboxes, network drives, and other non-structured business repositories.

 Enable change and stakeholder engagement
 Build strong working relationships with Information Owners, Records Custodians, Information Custodians, Risk Offices, Compliance, Legal, Technology, Data Governance teams, and other relevant teams involved in records and data management to drive execution of key deliverables within the Three Lines of Defense model.
 Develop, maintain, and deliver training, communications, and practical guidance to Information Stewards, Records Custodians, Risk Office teams, and other stakeholders to support adoption of information governance practices.
 Lead cross-functional discussions to resolve issues, mature governance practices, and embed sustainable ways of working.
 Represent Corporate Risk on peer Steering Groups and provide direction on information management matters.
 Work closely with Business Group Risk Office teams on the effective roll-out of program changes.
 Develop and communicate the vision for information governance in Corporate Risk and build consensus on operating goals aligned with the Risk division.

 What you'll need to succeed 

 University degree in Information Management, Data Governance, Records Management, Business Administration, Risk Management, Library Sciences, Information Technology, or a related discipline, and/or relevant certification.
 5+ years of risk management, records management, data governance, or information governance experience, with a proven track record of designing and implementing effective programs, controls, and processes, ideally within a major federally regulated financial institution.
 Direct experience writing policies and guidelines, and implementing governance frameworks, standards, controls, or enterprise operating procedures.
 Demonstrable experience leading cross-functional initiatives, developing strong working relationships, and influencing senior stakeholders in a large, matrixed organization within the Three Lines of Defense model.
 Proven experience dealing with complexity and ambiguity, using broad knowledge, keen analysis, and sound professional judgement to arrive at quality decisions.
 Working knowledge of Sunlife’s information management, records management, data governance, privacy, compliance, and operational risk practices.
 Ability to translate complex policy, risk, records, and data governance requirements into clear business guidance, communications, training, and sustainable operating practices.Strong knowledge of information management, records management, and data governance principles, including information lifecycle management, repository governance, metadata management, information classification, and data quality management, with the ability to assess, measure, and monitor information risk.
 Strong knowledge of the information and records management landscape, financial industry leading practices, and regulator expectations.
 Exceptional analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making abilities, with keen attention to detail, and experience in risk assessment, control design, compliance monitoring, reporting, and analytics.
 Working knowledge of Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Teams, shared mailboxes, network drives, and other collaboration platforms.
 Experience implementing, managing, and maintaining a records, information governance, or GRC tool.
 Strategic mindset, with the ability to understand business requirements and develop innovative solutions.
 Excellent communication, facilitation, influencing, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to communicate complex concepts to a diverse audience.
 Well-developed writing and visual presentation skills to articulate analytic results, options, recommendations, and reporting.
 Effective change management and change leadership through impact and influence skills, with governance oversight and a continuous improvement mindset.• Proactive and adaptable mindset, with the ability to thrive in a fast-paced and rapidly evolving organization.

 What's in it for you: 

 Being a member of the Sun Life family, a group of people united by our Purpose: to help Clients and Employees achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives.
 In 2024, Sun Life ranked among the top 100 most sustainable global corporations by Corporate Knights for the 15th consecutive year, leading Canadian insurers.

 We’re also listed as one of the Best Workplaces for Women and Best Workplaces with Most Trusted Executive Teams.
 Our unique Sabbatical Program gives you the opportunity to take up to 6 weeks off, every five years.
 Care Days available for self-care or care of others (i.e., family or others you may support) and Sick Days to support your well-being.

In addition to Base Pay, eligible Sun Life employees participate in various incentive plans, payment under which is discretionary and subject to individual and company performance. A diverse workforce with wide perspectives and creative ideas benefits our Clients, the communities where we operate and all of us as colleagues.  Persons with disabilities who need accommodation in the application process, or those needing job postings in an alternative format, may e-mail a request to thebrightside@sunlife.com.

 Job Description: 
 About the role 

 At the intersection of strategy, risk management and execution, the AVP, Emerging Risk Management & Strategic Risk Initiatives leads enterprise-wide capabilities and strategic initiatives that strengthen Sun Life's ability to anticipate, assess and respond to evolving risks. The role provides second-line leadership for emerging risk management, AI risk governance, risk culture and selected strategic risk initiatives. Working across Business Groups, Corporate Functions and Risk teams, the AVP translates strategic direction, external developments and internal risk signals into forward-looking insights, practical governance and risk management actions that support risk-informed decision-making across the organization. The role is flexible and future-focused, leading the development and implementation of operating models, methodologies, governance structures and management reporting that turn emerging or conceptual issues into practical and sustainable risk management capabilities. 

 What you'll need to succeed 

 More than 10 years of progressive experience in risk management or a related discipline, preferably within a major federally regulated financial institution.
 Significant experience leading enterprise-wide initiatives and influencing senior stakeholders across multiple businesses, functions and jurisdictions.
 Demonstrated people or functional leadership experience, including leadership through matrix reporting relationships.
 Expert knowledge of risk management within a large, complex financial institution.
 Strong understanding of first-line and second-line risk management accountabilities and the respective roles.
 Demonstrated ability to develop and execute enterprise strategies, operating models and multi-year transformation roadmaps.
 Proven ability to lead through influence across a federated or matrix organization and gain alignment among senior stakeholders with competing priorities.
 Has led or has exposure to the development of AI risk governance models in an organization
 Strong business and industry acumen, with the ability to assess complex and sensitive risk matters and provide pragmatic recommendations.
 Demonstrated experience developing executive and committee reporting that translates complex risk information into clear implications and decisions.
 Strong knowledge of regulatory expectations and leading practices relating to risk.
 Experience translating enterprise policy and methodology into first-line execution guidance.
 Strong knowledge of Sun Life’s products, businesses and operational risk environment.
 Exceptional written, verbal and presentation skills, including the ability to communicate with and influence senior executives.
 Strong change leadership, communication, negotiation, and decision-making capabilities.
 Demonstrated sound judgment and ability to operate autonomously in complex and ambiguous situations.
 University degree in business, risk management, finance, technology or a related discipline; a relevant graduate degree or professional designation is preferred.

 What you'll be doing 

 Risk Management Framework and Associated Governance  
 Identify where emerging risks, AI or other evolving risk management capabilities may require changes to the Risk Management Framework, risk taxonomy, policies, standards or related governance.
 Work with the AVP, Enterprise Risk Management and relevant policy owners to recommend and support appropriate changes while maintaining clear accountability with the applicable framework or policy owner.

 AI Risk Governance and Oversight  
 Lead the development and ongoing evolution of the second-line approach to AI risk governance and oversight, including the target operating model, governance forums, roles and accountabilities, escalation pathways and management reporting.
 Bring together relevant risk and policy owners to support coordinated identification, assessment and oversight of risks arising from AI across the Enterprise.
 Provide second-line risk advice, oversight and challenge on material AI initiatives, including risks arising as AI systems become more capable, autonomous or influential in business decision-making.
 Monitor developments in AI technology, regulation and industry practice and assess implications for Sun Life’s risk governance and capabilities.

jobs.title: VP Technology & Innovation
jobs.description:
Teladoc Health is the global virtual care leader, offering comprehensive virtual care solutions spanning virtual care including primary, mental health, expert medical, devices and licensed platform services. Teladoc Health serves the world's leading insurers, employers, and health systems and helps millions of people around the world resolve their healthcare needs with confidence. Serving over 9 million Canadians, Teladoc Health has been in Canada for more than 20 years and operates in 175 countries world-wide.

 Position Summary 

 The Vice President, Technology and Innovation (“VP”) is responsible for defining and executing Teladoc Health Canada’s technology, product, innovation and cybersecurity strategy. The VP leads the development and delivery of Teladoc Health Canada's digital products and technology ecosystem, including product management, software engineering, enterprise architecture, cybersecurity, data and analytics, technology operations, and innovation. The role is accountable for building a secure, reliable, scalable, and modern technology environment that enables high-quality virtual and hybrid care, an exceptional client, clinician, and patient experience, and operational excellence.

 The VP provides executive leadership for Teladoc Health Canada's digital strategy and multi-year technology roadmap, ensuring technology investments and product capabilities align with Canadian market needs, regulatory requirements, enterprise priorities, and Teladoc Health's global strategy. Working closely with clinical, commercial, operations, legal, privacy, compliance, and global technology leaders, the VP plays a key role in advancing Teladoc Health Canada's enterprise data governance framework and responsible use of data and AI, while delivering technology solutions that drive revenue growth, innovation, quality of care, security, and operational efficiency.

 Essential Duties and Responsibilities 

 Technology Strategy & Delivery 
 Develop and refresh Teladoc Health Canada’s digital strategy and multi-year technology roadmap aligned with organizational strategy and business objectives;

 Provide secure, scalable, resilient and sustainable digital solutions and technology infrastructure that meet Canadian business, market and regulatory requirements;

 Lead the strategy, design, development, delivery, and lifecycle management of Teladoc Health Canada’s technology ecosystem, including enterprise architecture, applications, integrations, infrastructure, and digital platforms;

 Develop and execute Teladoc Health Canada’s cybersecurity strategy, ensuring appropriate security controls, resilience, and cybersecurity risk management across technology platforms and information assets

 Own the budget, portfolio, and project management of digital initiatives and ongoing technology operations, ensuring disciplined prioritization, resource allocation, and value delivery; and

 Develop and manage strategic relationships with technology partners and vendors.

 Product Strategy & Delivery 
 Lead Teladoc Canada’s multi-year product roadmap to enable operational excellence, high-quality clinical care, commercial growth, and exceptional client, clinician and patient experiences;

 Translate market, regulatory, clinical, and operational requirements into innovative digital products;

 Champion user-centred design by incorporating the perspectives of clients, clinicians, patients, and internal users throughout the product lifecycle to deliver intuitive, accessible, and seamless digital experiences; and

 Integrate customer feedback, clinical insights, analytics, and user research into product planning, development and continuous improvement.

 Data, Analytics & AI Enablement 
 Lead the operational implementation of Teladoc Health Canada's enterprise data governance framework, including data architecture, stewardship, quality, metadata, lifecycle management, and data governance technologies, in partnership with the legal, privacy and compliance teams, and business stakeholders.

 Champion enterprise analytics, business intelligence, and AI-enabled capabilities that support operational excellence, clinical quality, innovation, and informed business decision-making.

 Develop and maintain secure, scalable, and reliable data management capabilities that enable high-quality clinical insights, operational intelligence, performance measurement, forecasting, and the responsible use of AI.

 Oversee enterprise data and analytics for the Canadian business, delivering timely, accurate, and actionable insights that support strategic planning, operational performance, and continuous improvement.

 Governance, Risk & Compliance 
 Partner with legal, privacy and compliance teams to ensure technology solutions meet applicable legal, regulatory, contractual, security, and clinical quality requirements, relevant market standards and clinical-quality expectations (e.g., PHIPA, PIPEDA, provincial health and privacy regulations, virtual care standards, responsible AI practices);

 Establish and oversee technology governance, including enterprise architecture, software development lifecycle (SDLC), cybersecurity, and cloud governance frameworks and processes, while partnering with the legal, privacy and compliance teams on enterprise data and AI governance and technology vendor risk management; and

 Identify, assess, and manage technology and cybersecurity risks by implementing appropriate controls, monitoring, and mitigation strategies to support the organization’s enterprise risk management framework, business resilience, audit readiness, and compliance with applicable legal, regulatory, contractual, and organizational requirements.

 Technology Operations & Cybersecurity 
 Ensure reliable, scalable, and secure IT operations that support business continuity, organizational growth, and compliance with applicable organizational, contractual, and regulatory requirements;

 Oversee the performance, availability, and reliability of Teladoc Health Canada’s technology ecosystem through proactive monitoring, incident management, issue triage, root cause analysis, and continuous improvement to prevent recurrence and improve system resilience;

 Provide executive oversight of Teladoc Health Canada's cybersecurity program, including information security operations, vulnerability management, identity and access management, incident response, disaster recovery, business continuity, and continuous enhancement of security controls.

 Lead technology support services for clinicians, clients, and internal users, while coordinating with Global/International teams on shared platforms, infrastructure, devices (e.g., HHS, GSD), escalation management, and operational support.

 People, Culture & Capability Building 
 Build, lead, and develop a high-performing, multidisciplinary technology organization;

 Strengthen organizational capabilities across product management, software engineering, enterprise architecture, cybersecurity, data and AI, cloud and infrastructure, and technology operations;

 Foster a culture of innovation, continuous improvement, accountability, collaboration, security-by-design, and user-centred product development.

 Yes

 $230,000 to $250,000/year

 Backfill

 Qualifications Expected for Position 
 Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Software Engineering, Health Informatics, Business or related field (advanced degree preferred);

 12+ years of progressive senior leadership experience in technology, product management, digital transformation, and/or data and analytics, within healthcare, virtual/hybrid care, or a highly regulated sector;

 Demonstrated ability to develop and execute technology strategies that align with organizational objectives and deliver measurable business outcomes;

 Deep understanding of cybersecurity, enterprise architecture, cloud technologies, data and analytics, AI, and emerging technology trends;

 Demonstrated experience leading technology modernization, digital transformation, and enterprise technology operations;

 Strong executive communication, stakeholder management, and change leadership skills, with the ability to collaborate with clinical, commercial, operations, legal, privacy, and compliance functions, and global counterparts;

 Demonstrated success leading multi-disciplinary, distributed, and high-performing teams within a complex, multinational corporate structure; and
