jobs.title: Director, Platform Engineering
jobs.description:
Join the team leading the next evolution of virtual care.  

 At Teladoc Health, you are empowered to bring your true self to work while helping millions of people live their healthiest lives.

 Here you will be part of a high-performance culture where colleagues embrace challenges, drive transformative solutions, and create opportunities for growth. Together, we’re transforming how better health happens.

 Position Summary 
 We are seeking a Director, Platform Engineering & DevOps to lead the development and maturation of our enterprise Platform Engineering organization.

 This leader will be responsible for building a modern, automation-first platform primarily focused on Microsoft Azure, while supporting remaining legacy workloads in AWS and on-premises data centers during the company's migration to Azure.

 The Director will lead the Platform Engineering team and partner closely with Network Engineering, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), Security, and application Engineering to deliver secure, reliable, scalable, and highly automated infrastructure platforms.

 A key objective of this role is to move the organization toward a self-service Platform Engineering model, enabling application teams to deploy and manage infrastructure using standardized patterns, Infrastructure as Code, automation, and cloud governance.

 Role and Responsibilities 
 Build, lead, and develop the Platform Engineering organization, including engineering strategy, roadmap, standards, and operating model.
 Lead the design and evolution of the company's enterprise Microsoft Azure platform, including landing zones, governance, identity, networking, security, observability, and resiliency.

 Support the migration of applications and infrastructure from AWS and on-premises environments to Azure.

 Establish Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and automation as the standard approach for provisioning and managing infrastructure.

 Develop reusable Terraform modules, CI/CD pipelines, reference architectures, and standardized deployment patterns.

 Build self-service platform capabilities and "golden paths" that improve developer productivity and reduce manual infrastructure provisioning.

 Partner with Network Engineering on hybrid cloud connectivity, cloud networking, Private Link, DNS, routing, firewalls, and application delivery.

 Partner with SRE to establish platform availability objectives, observability standards, resiliency practices, incident improvements, and operational readiness, leveraging Datadog Application

 Partner with SRE and Application Engineering to establish consistent standards for application and platform telemetry, including metrics, logs, distributed traces, dashboards, alerting, and service-level monitoring.

 Ensure cloud and platform services are appropriately instrumented and integrated with the enterprise observability platform.

 Partner with Security to implement secure-by-default platform patterns, cloud governance, policy enforcement, and compliance controls.

 Establish cloud cost-management and FinOps practices across Azure and remaining AWS environments.

 Recruit, mentor, and develop engineering leaders and senior technical talent.

 Provide executive-level communication regarding platform strategy, technology risks, investments, reliability, and cloud transformation progress.

 Required Qualifications 
 10+ years of progressive experience in cloud infrastructure, DevOps, Platform Engineering, systems engineering, or related disciplines, including significant engineering leadership experience.

 Deep technical knowledge of Microsoft Azure, including enterprise cloud architecture, networking, security, governance, resiliency, and platform services.

 Strong experience with Infrastructure as Code and automation, particularly Terraform, CI/CD pipelines, and Git-based engineering workflows.

 Demonstrated experience leading complex cloud transformation initiatives, including hybrid environments, enterprise cloud migrations, or modernization of mission-critical infrastructure.

 Preferred Qualifications 
 Experience building or leading an enterprise Platform Engineering organization or Internal Developer Platform.

 Working knowledge of AWS and experience supporting or migrating AWS workloads.

 Experience with Azure Landing Zones, Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework, Azure Well-Architected Framework, and Azure Verified Modules.

 Experience with Kubernetes and Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS).

 Experience with GitHub Enterprise, GitLab, GitHub Actions or comparable DevOps platforms.

 Experience with enterprise observability and APM platforms, preferably Datadog, and technologies such as OpenTelemetry.

 Experience implementing SRE practices including SLIs, SLOs, error budgets, resiliency engineering, and incident management.

 Experience implementing cloud FinOps and cost optimization practices.

 Experience operating technology platforms in healthcare, SaaS, financial services, or another regulated environment.

 Success Metrics for the Role 
 Success will be measured by the Director's ability to build a scalable Platform Engineering organization and improve the speed, reliability, security, and efficiency of infrastructure delivery.
 Increased percentage of infrastructure deployed and managed through Infrastructure as Code.

 Increased adoption of standardized Azure landing zones, reusable platform services, and self-service capabilities.

 Reduced infrastructure provisioning and application deployment lead times.

 Progress migrating targeted AWS and on-premises workloads to Azure.

 Improved platform availability and achievement of defined SLOs.

 Increased adoption and effectiveness of standardized observability and APM practices across platform and application services, including improved service visibility and reduced mean time to detect and restore.

 Reduction in infrastructure-related incidents, configuration drift, and manual production changes.

 Improved developer satisfaction and adoption of Platform Engineering services.

 Improved cloud governance, security compliance, and cost efficiency.

 Successful recruitment, development, and retention of a high-performing Platform Engineering team.

 As part of our hiring process, we verify identity and credentials, conduct interviews (live or video), and screen for fraud or misrepresentation. Applicants who falsify information will be disqualified.

 Why join Teladoc Health? 

 Teladoc Health is transforming how better health happens. Learn how when you join us in pursuit of our impactful mission. 

 Chart your career path with meaningful opportunities that empower you to grow, lead, and make a difference.

 Join a multi-faceted community that celebrates each colleague’s unique perspective and is focused on continually improving, each and every day.  

 Contribute to an innovative culture where fresh ideas are valued as we increase access to care in new ways.   

 Enjoy an inclusive benefits program centered around you and your family, with tailored programs that address your unique needs.

 Explore candidate resources with tips and tricks from Teladoc Health recruiters and learn more about our company culture by exploring #TeamTeladocHealth on LinkedIn.

 As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we never have and never will discriminate against any job candidate or employee due to age, race, religion, color, ethnicity, national origin, gender, gender identity/expression, sexual orientation, membership in an employee organization, medical condition, family history, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, parental status, or pregnancy). In our innovative and inclusive workplace, we prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind. 

 Teladoc Health respects your privacy and is committed to maintaining the confidentiality and security of your personal information. In furtherance of your employment relationship with Teladoc Health, we collect personal information responsibly and in accordance with applicable data privacy laws, including but not limited to, the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA).  Personal information is defined as: Any information or set of information relating to you, including (a) all information that identifies you or could reasonably be used to identify you, and (b) all information that any applicable law treats as personal information. jobs.description:
Telesat (Nasdaq and TSX: TSAT) is a leading global satellite operator, providing reliable and secure satellite-delivered communications solutions worldwide to broadcast, telecommunications, corporate and government customers for over 55 years.  Backed by a legacy of engineering excellence, reliability and industry-leading customer service, Telesat has grown to be one of the largest and most successful global satellite operators.
Telesat Lightspeed, our revolutionary Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite network, scheduled to begin service in 2027, will revolutionize global broadband connectivity for enterprise and Government users by delivering a combination of high capacity, security, resiliency and affordability with ultra-low latency and fiber-like speeds. Telesat is headquartered in Ottawa, Canada, and has offices and facilities around the world.
 
The company’s state-of-the-art Satellite fleet consists of 12 GEO satellites, the Canadian payload on ViaSat-1 and one LEO 3 demonstration satellite.  For more information, follow Telesat on X and LinkedIn or visit www.telesat.com

jobs.title: Director and Practice Lead, Data Engineering
jobs.description:
Who We Are 
 Welcome to TELUS Digital — where innovation drives impact at a global scale. As an award-winning digital agency and the digital division of TELUS, one of Canada’s largest telecommunications providers, we design and deliver transformative customer experiences through cutting-edge technology, agile thinking, and a people-first culture.
 With a global team across North America, South America, Central America, Europe, Africa, and APAC, we offer end-to-end expertise across: Digital Product Strategy & Innovation, Digital Marketing Services, Web & Mobile App Development, Data & AI, Cloud Engineering, and Enterprise Technology Modernization.
 From mobile apps and websites to voice UI, chatbots, AI, customer service, and in-store solutions, TELUS Digital enables seamless, trusted, and digitally powered experiences that meet customers wherever they are — all backed by the secure infrastructure and scale of our multi-billion-dollar parent company.

 Location & Flexibility 
 Our Director & Practice Lead, Data Engineering will operate remotely in Canada OR be based out of either our Toronto, ON or Vancouver, BC office locations.

 The Opportunity 
 TELUS Digital's Data, AI & Cloud (DAIC) practice is the multidisciplinary engine behind enterprise AI, blending boutique innovation with the breadth of a global services portfolio to help organizations architect, scale, and secure their transformations. Spanning our full family of specialized capabilities, the DAIC practice delivers end-to-end solutions across AI Advisory, AI Solutions, Data & AI Platforms, and Cloud Transformation.
 As a premier Google Cloud partner, our Cloud practice is at the forefront of helping enterprises adopt and scale on Google Cloud infrastructure: delivering complex engineering, deployment, and migration programs for some of the largest organizations in Canada and beyond.
 The Director & Practice Lead, Data Engineering will define and own the Data Engineering Practice along with its market positioning, P&L, talent, and the quality of work we deliver for clients. This role is for someone who has led data and AI practices before, understands how to turn messy enterprise data estates into strategic assets, and earns trust with C-suite executives through genuine expertise. You will shape how we help clients move from data ambition to durable, AI-ready infrastructure.
 This role will have four core anchor responsibilities:
 Strategy: Set the practice vision and align Data & AI capabilities to where enterprise demand is heading.

 P&L: Own revenue targets, margin, and growth while being accountable for the practice's full commercial performance.

 Talent & Culture: Build a practice where data-driven thinking, innovation, and engineering rigour are the baseline.

 Client Impact: Act as a trusted advisor to enterprise CxOs navigating data strategy, AI adoption, and governance.

Director, CX AI Delivery

 Welcome to TELUS Digital — where innovation drives impact at a global scale.  Location & Flexibility 
 This role will operate remotely in the United States or Canada OR be based out of one of our major North American office locations - Charlottesville, VA, Durham, NC, Columbus, OH, Boston, MA, Toronto, ON, or Vancouver, BC.
 This role may involve travel of up to 25% to contact center and client locations.

 The Opportunity 
 We are seeking a Director, CX AI Delivery: a consultant and delivery expert who can turn complex contact center and AI programs into predictable, measurable outcomes. You will lead delivery across our CX AI portfolio, spanning Contact Center as a Service (CCaaS) platforms, conversational and agentic AI, agent assist, and CX intelligence, and serve as a trusted advisor to client executives. You will manage a portfolio of client engagements (generally ~$15–20M in revenue), directly lead delivery, product, and engineering leaders, and step in to stabilize and recover programs when needed.

 This is a delivery-first leadership role with an AI lens. You will bring the rigor of a seasoned delivery executive together with a working command of how AI is changing CX: from AI-driven routing and virtual agents to copilots, knowledge, and agentic automation. You will help clients adopt these capabilities responsibly, at scale, and in iterative releases that get value into production quickly. You will also help evaluate vendor and partner solutions and decide how and when new tools enter the ecosystem.

 This position reports to the Managing Director, CX AI Delivery and typically manages 8–12 direct reports, including senior managers, managers, and principal-level delivery and technical leaders. It is primarily evaluated on delivery success, client and team feedback, forecast accuracy, portfolio profitability, and growth of key accounts. This is an opportunistically billable position.
 Responsibilities 
 Strategic Account Governance & Growth 
 Be the executive partner. Act as the primary escalation point and strategic advisor for client executives, ensuring TELUS Digital is viewed as a “Doctor” (consultative partner), not a “Waiter” (order taker).

 Run portfolio health. Drive the commercial success of a ~$15–20M portfolio, leading Quarterly Business Reviews that connect delivery progress to the client’s long-term CX and business goals.

 Grow organically. Identify expansion opportunities in existing accounts by understanding client pain points and bringing a relevant point of view on CX and AI. Support renewals, upsell, and expansion in partnership with strategic sales and customer success teams.

 Extend into managed services and advisory as the practice matures: shape Day 2 support models, operational readiness, and advisory engagements that keep clients engaged after go-live.

 Delivery Excellence & Risk Mitigation 
 Lead a global, multidisciplinary team across multiple concurrent workstreams, ensuring product, engineering, and delivery leaders operate as a cohesive unit to deliver measurable outcomes.

 Manage risk proactively. Identify “red” and “yellow” programs early; step into recovery situations to provide clarity, reset expectations, and stabilize teams and client relationships.

 Push for iterative delivery. Favor smaller releases and faster cycles over big-bang launches, especially for AI capabilities where learning in production is essential.

 Optimize delivery models, balancing onshore/offshore teams, automation, and repeatable assets to improve margins and scalability.

 Manage vendor and partner ecosystems. Work with CCaaS and AI platform partners (e.g., Genesys, Google, AWS, Zendesk, Five9, ElevenLabs, Cresta, Parloa) to deliver joint solutions as well as surrounding services in the client ecosystem.

 Partner on pre-sales. Support the commercial team to shape innovative solutions and lead scoping, estimation, and handoffs into delivery so engagements start with clear requirements and goals.

 Leadership & Talent Development 
 Coach and mentor delivery, product, and engineering leaders on leading their own teams and navigating complex client dynamics.

 Build a high-performance culture with regular 1:1s and performance reviews grounded in radical candor and growth, delivering feedback upward, across, and down with grace and clarity.

 Raise the bar on talent. Participate in senior-level hiring, contribute to the Delivery Playbook, and build career paths and skill development (including AI and platform certification pipelines).

 Operational & Financial Stewardship 
 Own portfolio financials: gross margin, utilization, and effective billable rates.

 Forecast accurately. Maintain precise revenue and resource forecasts so the business can plan hiring and growth with confidence.

 Influence with data. Use reporting language, data visualization, and storytelling to influence internal and external decisions and inspire confidence in stakeholders.

 Collaborate across the business with peers and practice leaders to improve internal processes and operational efficiency, and bring energy to moments that matter: new relationships, key presentations, and recovery situations.

 Qualifications 
 10+ years in the technology industry, including 4+ years in a senior leadership role in a professional services, consulting, or agency environment.

 Proven record managing a diverse portfolio of client accounts (ideally $10M+ in annual revenue) with a focus on retention and organic growth.

 Experience delivering large-scale CX or contact center transformations that influenced VP- and C-level decision making.

 Working knowledge of how AI is applied in CX: conversational and voice AI, agent assist and copilots, AI-driven routing, knowledge and content for AI, and CX intelligence; ability to discuss architecture, risk, and ROI credibly with both technical and executive audiences.

 Hands-on delivery experience with one or more leading CCaaS or CX AI platforms (e.g., Genesys, Amazon Connect, Zendesk, Google); platform certifications and experience across multiple verticals are a plus.

 Deep understanding of the SDLC and Agile delivery, with a track record of leading complex, custom-built software solutions from discovery to launch, and comfort with iterative, experiment-driven delivery.

 Experience managing and coaching leaders across Product, Engineering, and Delivery, and leading large, globally distributed teams.

 Strong command of professional services metrics, including gross margin, utilization, forecast accuracy, and effective billable rates.

 Exceptional ability to navigate “recovery situations” and high-stakes client conversations with poise, clarity, and a solution-oriented mindset.

In this business leadership capacity, you will establish priorities, set governance standards, and ensure sustained adoption and measurable value creation. Operating as the primary business counterpart to Technology and working in close partnership with the Chief Financial Officer and senior leadership, you will oversee the strategic roadmap to replace manual, fragmented workflows with a trusted, single source of financial data and insight that accelerates enterprise decision-making and supports global growth.

 Finance Transformation & Portfolio Delivery
 Own and champion the multi-year Digital Finance roadmap and unified backlog across the CFO organization, prioritizing initiatives by business value, control requirements, readiness, effort, and operational cost in close collaboration with Technology.
 Sponsor and drive end-to-end process redesign across record-to-report, plan-to-perform, procure-to-pay, and order-to-cash workflows to modernize core operations.
 Establish robust business cases for all digital initiatives, tracking adoption metrics, cycle-time reductions, redeployed capacity, and internal control enhancements.
 Authorize the decommissioning of legacy reports, spreadsheets, and manual steps following the rigorous validation of modern digital replacements.

 Act as the accountable Finance business owner for Workday Financials and Workday Adaptive Planning in collaboration with Controllership and FP&A process owners, establishing high standards for clean data capture, straight-through processing, chart-of-accounts governance, and audit-ready planning workflows.

 Partner with Technology, external implementation specialists, and Workday to conduct recurring architecture reviews and remediate configuration gaps.
 Oversee and approve the business roadmap for the broader finance application ecosystem (close management, consolidations, billing, accounts payable, expense management, treasury, and tax), actively identifying rationalization opportunities.
 Align application release schedules with the financial close calendar, collaborating with Technology, Risk, and Internal Audit to enforce rigorous segregation of duties, access controls, and Internal Control over Financial Reporting (ICFR).
 Finance Data, BI & Analytics
 Direct the team responsible for designing, building, and operating finance data models, data pipelines, and certified financial data products on Snowflake, establishing a single source of truth across all global entities.
 Establish robust semantic layer governance, ensuring every certified data product possesses an assigned Finance owner, approved definitions, and ongoing reconciliation to general ledger accounting outputs.
 Oversee Finance’s enterprise Business Intelligence (BI) capabilities and visualization standards, transitioning teams from static reporting to dynamic, interactive dashboards and executive decision environments utilizing tools such as Amazon QuickSight and native cloud analytics capabilities.
 Accelerate data-driven insights across Finance by collaborating with Finance Business Partners and operational data teams to integrate financial and operational drivers, including trading, clearing, listings, and market data subscriptions.
 Applied AI & Intelligent Automation
 Identify, prioritize, and oversee the rollout of high-impact finance AI use cases—such as variance analysis, exception triage, predictive forecasting, narrative document synthesis, and anomaly detection—ensuring each deployment maintains clear quality thresholds, human-in-the-loop oversight, and independent model validation.
 Drive end-to-end automation of data collation, reconciliation, and distribution throughout the reporting cycle while safeguarding professional financial judgment and formal authorization checkpoints.
 Market Innovation & Continuous Improvement
 Monitor evolving capabilities across Workday, Snowflake, business intelligence ecosystems, and emerging financial technologies, assessing business viability and integrating high-value opportunities into the strategic roadmap.
 Provide strategic advisory to the Finance Senior Leadership Team on emerging technology trends, fostering shared ownership of digital adoption.
 People Leadership & Change Enablement
 Lead, mentor, and develop a multidisciplinary team spanning finance systems, data engineering, business intelligence, and advanced analytics, establishing clear strategic direction while scaling functional capacity.
 Drive enterprise change management, communication, and training programs to embed digital literacy and analytical curiosity across the broader finance organization.
 Manage the Digital Finance operational budget, serving as the business partner to Technology and Procurement for vendor selection and delivery partner management.

 Must Have(s) 
 12+ years of progressive finance experience with comprehensive knowledge of core accounting and financial processes, coupled with advanced financial analysis capabilities.
 Professional accounting or financial credential (CPA preferred; MBA or CFA will also be considered).
 Demonstrated success serving as the business lead for major finance transformations (e.g., enterprise ERP implementations, EPM/planning platforms, or enterprise data and reporting overhauls) from conception through operational adoption and value realization.
 Proven leadership experience guiding data, BI, or analytics personnel, underpinned by sufficient technical literacy in data modeling, SQL, cloud data platforms (e.g., Snowflake), and modern BI suites to establish standards and guide technical execution.
 Deep knowledge of financial governance frameworks, internal controls, and ICFR requirements within large-scale system and process transformation environments.
 Demonstrated track record managing multi-year business cases, departmental budgets, third-party software vendors, and systems integration partners.
 Proven leadership acumen in ambiguous, matrixed environments with strong cross-functional stakeholder management and executive presentation skills.

 Nice to Have(s) 
 Experience with Workday Financials and Workday Adaptive Planning, including Foundation Data Model (FDM) architecture and data integration with Snowflake.
 Direct technical experience with data querying and scripting languages (e.g., SQL, Python).
 Practical experience deploying artificial intelligence or machine learning solutions within corporate finance environments, including model validation and risk management frameworks.
 Industry experience within capital markets, financial services, financial technology, or software organizations.
 Leadership background within multi-entity, multi-currency, and multinational operating structures.
 Experience building, structuring, and scaling a digital or transformation function from early-stage maturity.

jobs.description:
Position Summary... 
The Senior Director, Business Intelligence Strategy & Media Insights (Canada) is responsible for leading Walmart Connect Canada’s analytics, measurement, and media intelligence capabilities. This role ensures data driven insights are embedded across media planning, investment decisions, performance measurement, and executive reporting.

Working in close partnership with the International Business Insights & Analytics organization, this role implements and operates global measurement, reporting, and data governance frameworks within the Canadian market, ensuring alignment to global standards while delivering insights tailored to Canadian business needs.

This position plays a critical role in driving omnichannel measurement excellence, commercial performance, and operational insight across Walmart Connect Canada.  

 What you'll do... 
 Business Intelligence & Analytics 
 • Lead the strategy and execution of business intelligence, analytics, and performance measurement for Walmart Connect Canada.
 • Ensure analytics and insights inform media planning, optimization, and investment decisions.
 • Oversee omnichannel attribution and media effectiveness measurement across digital and in‑store channels.

 Global Measurement & Reporting Alignment 
 • Implement global measurement, reporting, and data governance frameworks within the Canadian market.
 • Partner with International Business Insights leaders to support consistent adoption of global standards.
 • Provide ongoing feedback related to framework effectiveness and local market considerations.

 Reporting & Performance Management 
 • Deliver Canada‑level executive reporting, including WBRs, MBRs, QBRs, and leadership reviews, aligned to global standards.
 • Ensure timely, accurate, and actionable reporting for senior stakeholders.
 • Ensure Canadian performance insights are incorporated into international reporting processes.

 Commercial Performance & Optimization 
 • Partner with Sales, Product, Marketing, and Finance teams to identify growth opportunities and quantify impact.
 • Support advertiser performance measurement and ROI accountability frameworks.

 Cross‑Functional & Cross‑Market Collaboration 
 • Serve as the primary point of contact between Walmart Connect Canada and the International Business Insights organization.
 • Collaborate with Walmart Connect U.S., MAP, and internal Canada teams to enable aligned decision‑making.
 • Support shared priorities while representing Canadian business requirements.

 People Leadership 
 • Build, lead, and develop a high‑performing Canada‑based analytics and insights team.
 • Establish clear goals, performance expectations, and development plans.
 • Foster a culture of analytical excellence, innovation, and continuous improvement.

 Minimum Qualifications 
 • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Analytics, Economics, Engineering, or a related field.
 • 12+ years of experience in business intelligence, analytics, data strategy, or related disciplines.
 • Experience leading analytics or insights teams in a complex, cross‑functional organization.
 • Experience supporting executive‑level reporting and decision‑making.
 • Strong analytical, communication, and stakeholder‑management skills.

 Preferred Qualifications 
 • MBA or advanced degree.
 • Experience in retail media, advertising, marketplaces, or adjacent industries.
 • Experience working with global or regional analytics organizations.
 • Demonstrated ability to link insights to commercial performance and growth outcomes.
 • Walmart Connect or similar retail media experience.

 Core Competencies 
 • Advanced analytics and business intelligence expertise
 • Measurement, attribution, and performance reporting acumen
 • Executive‑level communication and data storytelling
 • Commercial and financial understanding
 • Strong people leadership and talent development capabilities
 • Ability to operate effectively in a matrixed, international environment

Builds high-performing teams; seeks, and embraces differences in people, cultures, ideas and experiences; creates a workplace and experiences where all associates feel seen, supported and connected through culture of belonging so associates thrive and perform; drives a positive associate and customer experience for all.
Creates a discipline and focus around developing talent through feedback, coaching, mentoring, and developmental opportunities; builds the talent pipeline, fosters an environment allowing everyone to bring their best selves to work, empowers associates and partners to act in the best interest of the customer and company, and regularly recognizes others’ contributions and accomplishments; supports strategies and drives initiatives that attract and retain the best talent.
Builds strong and trusting relationships with team members and business partners; works collaboratively and cross-functionally to achieve objectives; and communicates and listens attentively, with energy and positivity to motivate, influence, and inspire commitment and action.

Maintains and promotes the highest standards of integrity, ethics and compliance; models the Walmart values and leads by example to foster our culture; supports Walmart’s goal of becoming a regenerative company by taking action to advance opportunity, sustainability, community, and integrity (e.g., creating fair opportunities for associates and suppliers, driving local giving efforts).

jobs.title: Associate Creative Director, Art Director
jobs.description:
Build something people love 
 Wealthsimple is Canada’s leading financial innovator. The company offers a full suite of simple, sophisticated financial products across managed investing, do-it-yourself trading, cryptocurrency, tax filing, spending and saving. Wealthsimple currently serves more than 4 million Canadians and holds over $169 billion in assets under administration. The company was founded in 2014 by a team of financial experts and technology entrepreneurs, and is headquartered in Toronto, Canada.

 We're proud of what we've built — and we're just getting started. Read our Culture Manual and learn more about how we work.

 At Wealthsimple, we're interested in humans and money — and the complicated ways humans feel about money. Our goal in the creative department is to be a part of that conversation in meaningful ways that are completely innovative and new. We have a deep aversion to making things that already exist and to ads that feel like ads.

 We are looking for an experienced Associate Creative Director, Art Director to help us create innovative, human and ridiculously entertaining work. In this role you will often work as a team with a copywriter partner, but you’ll also collaborate with designers, writers, marketers and engineers across the org. You will be responsible for all aspects of creative development and production on integrated brand campaigns and projects large and small, and you will be leading creative voice in some of our biggest brand moments.

 In this role, you’ll have the opportunity to: 
 Be a highly conceptual thinker with strong storytelling and design skills.

 Develop big ideas and bring them to life through every stage of production.

 Own large and small brand projects and campaigns from kickoff to completion, often balancing multiple projects at once.

 Be a maker-owner, but also a director-delegator, and find the right balance between those two roles for each project.

 Provide art direction on visual design for integrated brand campaigns and projects of various scales and types – from film, social, digital, to interactive experiences.

 Be a creative and strategic thinker who can see how creativity can solve business problems.

 Use AI in a variety of ways. Whether it’s moving ideas into functional prototypes, drafts, mockups or animatics that can be evaluated more quickly, or developing and refining AI workflows for internally created assets.

 Present work in a clear, passionate and dynamic way, championing the creative and vision to internal stakeholders.

 Manage relationships with outside production partners when necessary.

 Skills You Bring 
 6-10+ years of experience as an Art Director (agency experience preferred, but not necessary).

 Ability to concept and art direct, developing storyboards, comps or animatics without assistance from the Design team

 Extensive experience with integrated campaigns, from strategic development through creative development and delivery

 Production experience across all platforms - film, digital, social, and print

 Well-versed in Adobe Creative Suite and able to be a hands-on creative delivering comps, layouts, and assets across all media types as well as give direction to studio designers where applicable

 Familiarity with AI image and video generation tools.

 A truly collaborative creative approach.

 Give and receive constructive feedback in a respectful manner

 Travel for production when necessary.

 Why Wealthsimple? 
 🌸 Top-tier health benefits and life insurance
 📈 Long-term group savings with employer match, through Wealthsimple for Business
 🌴 20 vacation days, 4 wellness days, and unlimited sick and mental health days per year*
 ✈️ 90 days away: work outside Canada for up to 90 days per year*
 👥 Employee resource groups, including Rainbow (2SLGBTQ), Women of WS, and Black at WS
 🌎 We are a hybrid team with over 1,500 employees across North America. The people are one of the best parts of working here: you'll collaborate with incredibly talented, curious, and driven teammates who are deeply committed to doing great work.

*Unlimited paid sick days, Wellness Days and the 90 day away program do not apply to certain roles. 

 ICYMI 
 Technology & Innovation at Wealthsimple: We move quickly and build thoughtfully. That means we're always looking for better ways to work — whether that's new tools, AI, or rethinking how we approach a problem. We don't expect you to have all the answers, but we do expect curiosity and a willingness to evolve alongside the products we're building.

 Inclusion Statement: We're building products for a diverse world, and we need a diverse team to do it well. We strongly encourage applications from everyone, regardless of race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, or disability status.

 Accessibility Statement: We're committed to an accessible hiring experience. If you need any accommodations throughout the interview process, please let us know — we'll work with you to make sure you have what you need. We also welcome any feedback on how we can better accommodate candidates with accessibility needs.

 AI in Hiring: We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of our hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses. These tools assist our team but don't replace human judgment – all final hiring decisions are made by people. If you have questions about how your data is used, reach out to us.

jobs.title: Director, FinOps
jobs.description:
Zafin is an AI platform company helping regulated institutions modernize how critical work is designed, governed, and delivered. Our technology enables organizations to move faster while maintaining the governance, accountability, and control required in highly regulated environments.

 Our portfolio includes Zafin AIOS, an agent orchestration platform for governed AI work; the Zafin Banking Platform, which helps banks modernize product, pricing, offers, billing, loyalty, and relationship management; and Zafin IO, an integration platform that connects data, systems, and workflows across complex enterprise environments.

 Headquartered in Toronto, Canada, Zafin partners with leading financial institutions across North America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Asia-Pacific. As AI transforms the future of financial services, we're building the platforms that help regulated organizations adopt AI responsibly and at scale.

 What is the Opportunity?

 Lead the FinOps function. As Director, FinOps (Cloud Financial Management), you will shape and advance Zafin’s cloud financial management strategy. You will build and lead a scalable FinOps function that delivers measurable, sustainable cost savings while safeguarding platform reliability, security, and engineering productivity.

 Shape cloud investment decisions. You will define how Zafin manages and optimizes cloud investments across its banking technology platforms. Working with Engineering, Cloud Operations, Product, and Finance, you will strengthen financial accountability, increase cost visibility, and embed cost-conscious decision-making across technology and business operations.

 Apply AI and automation. You will use AI-driven analytics, automation, and intelligent cost monitoring to improve forecasting, identify optimization opportunities, detect spending anomalies, and strengthen cloud financial governance.

 Deliver sustainable business value. Your leadership will improve cloud cost efficiency and financial predictability, ensuring Zafin’s cloud investments generate lasting value.

 What Will You Do?

 Define and lead Zafin’s FinOps strategy, governance framework, and cloud cost optimization program across Microsoft Azure and platform services.

 Deliver measurable cloud savings through resource optimization, improved utilization, cost avoidance, and stronger financial accountability.

 Lead cloud budgeting, forecasting, variance analysis, and financial reporting to increase cost visibility and improve predictability.

 Partner with Engineering, Cloud Operations, Product, and Finance to embed cost-efficient practices in architecture, infrastructure, and operational decisions.

 Optimize Azure infrastructure spending across compute, storage, networking, AKS/Kubernetes, Reserved Instances, and observability services.

 Establish cost allocation models, tagging standards, financial controls, and unit economics to strengthen cloud cost management.

 Implement FinOps tools, dashboards, AI-assisted analytics, automation, and anomaly detection to uncover savings opportunities and reinforce financial governance.

 Provide executives with clear reporting on cloud spending, savings performance, financial risks, and strategic recommendations.

 Build and mentor a high-performing FinOps team, foster cross-functional collaboration, and create a culture of cloud cost accountability.

 What Do You Need to Succeed?

 Must Haves 

 Relevant experience: 10+ years in cloud infrastructure, platform operations, technology finance, financial planning and analysis (FP&A), or FinOps, including at least three years in a leadership role.

 Cloud financial management: Proven success designing or leading initiatives that deliver measurable, sustained cost savings and improve cost-to-serve.

 Azure expertise: Strong knowledge of Microsoft Azure and the cost drivers for compute, storage, networking, Kubernetes/AKS, and observability services.

 Financial planning and analysis: Expertise in cloud budgeting, forecasting, variance analysis, financial modelling, ROI assessment, and savings measurement.

 Financial insight: Ability to translate complex cloud architecture and infrastructure decisions into clear financial implications and actionable optimization strategies.

 Governance and accountability: Experience establishing financial governance practices, cost allocation models, accountability frameworks, and performance reporting.

 Analytical problem-solving: Ability to identify key cost drivers, generate meaningful insights, and translate them into measurable business outcomes.

 Cross-functional influence: Demonstrated success aligning Engineering, Finance, Product, and Technology stakeholders and advancing initiatives without direct authority.

 Executive communication: Excellent stakeholder management skills, with experience presenting financial performance, strategic recommendations, and operational metrics to senior leaders.

 Leadership and change management: Proven ability to build scalable processes, establish operational discipline, lead high-performing teams, and drive organizational change in complex technology environments.

 Nice to Have 

 FinOps Foundation certifications, such as FinOps Certified Practitioner or Professional, and/or relevant Microsoft Azure certifications.

 Experience implementing showback/chargeback models and cloud unit economics at an enterprise scale.

 Familiarity with Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and GitOps practices, including Terraform, Argo CD, or equivalent technologies.

 Experience integrating cloud cost controls and financial governance into engineering delivery pipelines.

 Exposure to AI-driven cloud cost analytics, intelligent forecasting, anomaly detection, and automated optimization solutions.

 Experience establishing a FinOps function or cloud financial management capability within a growing technology organization.

 Familiarity with cloud infrastructure supporting financial services, banking platforms, or other regulated industries.

 Additional Job Details

 Vacancy Status: Open Position to be Filled

 Expected Salary Range: CAD 170,000 –190,000

 In addition to base salary, this position offers eligibility for an annual incentive bonus and a comprehensive benefits package to support your health, financial well-being, and work-life balance.

 Mode of Work:  Onsite at Toronto, Canada office

 Use of AI: Zafin may use Artificial Intelligence (AI) and/or other forms of automated technology to screen and/or assess applicants for this position. Zafin will not utilize AI for conducting interviews and/or making hiring decisions.

 What’s in It for You? 

 At Zafin, you’ll join a culture that values diversity, teamwork, and high-quality work, with opportunities for professional growth and career advancement. We invest in our people through a comprehensive rewards program that supports your health, financial well-being, and work-life balance, including:

 Competitive salaries and annual bonus opportunities

 Fully company-paid health benefits

 Generous vacation, holidays, and paid volunteering days

 RRSP matching

 Employer-paid insurance coverage

 Wellness resources and extensive paramedical benefits

 Explore career opportunities and learn more about life at Zafin at zafin.com/careers.

   Accessibility 

 Zafin welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodation is available upon request for candidates participating in any stage of the selection process.

   Applicant Privacy 

 Zafin is committed to protecting the privacy and security of applicants’ personal information throughout the recruitment process. For details on how we collect, use, store, handle, retain, and disclose your information, please review Zafin’s Privacy Notice.

 By submitting a job application, you confirm your agreement to the processing of your personal data as described in the candidate privacy notice.
 What’s in it for you 

 Joining our team means being part of a culture that values diversity, teamwork, and high-quality work. We offer competitive salaries, annual bonus potential, generous paid time off, paid volunteering days, wellness benefits, and robust opportunities for professional growth and career advancement. Want to learn more about what you can look forward to during your career with us? Visit our careers site and our openings:  zafin.com/careers

jobs.title: VP, Financial Planning & Analysis
jobs.description:
About ClearGov 

 ClearGov is building the modern financial operating layer for the public sector. 

 We help US local governments and school districts plan, budget, report, and communicate their finances with clarity and confidence. From long-term planning to financial reporting, compliance, and transparency, our platform connects the work finance teams are already doing and makes it easier to deliver for their communities. 

Today, more than 2,000 public sector organizations use ClearGov, and we continue to expand our platform and reach as we grow.

 Our Core Values 

 Be Clear & Credible  

 We are authentic in our interactions, communicating with clarity, speaking with honesty, and following through with consistency. We turn transparency into our greatest competitive advantage. 

 Be Human   

 We are human partners to our colleagues and customers and lead with consideration and kindness - making space for others to do the same. We turn empathy into a shared strength.

 Be Better Together   

 We are committed to building an inclusive community where everyone thrives. We share successes, support each other through challenges, and show up for our teammates the way we show up for our customers. We turn togetherness into our greatest advantage and collaboration into our greatest multiplier.

 Be Honourable/Honorable   

 We are responsible to our colleagues and customers. We bring our full selves to every conversation, every project, every decision, and every relationship. We act with intention, deliver on our commitments, and lead with integrity - even when no one is watching. We turn honour into the foundation that powers everything we do.

 Be Connected 

 We are culture builders where people are seen, welcomed, and celebrated. We show up in every interaction - the laughs, the wins, the hard days. We turn connection into opportunities for people to feel they belong.

 What Makes You a Great Fit 

 You take ownership and follow through

 You communicate clearly and effectively

 You're comfortable solving problems and figuring things out

 You learn quickly and adapt as things change

 You care about the team, not just your own work

 You bring a sense of humor and perspective to what you do

 About the Opportunity 

 We are seeking a hands-on Vice President, Financial Planning & Analysis to own enterprise-wide planning, forecasting, and performance analytics for a growth-stage SaaS business. This is not a purely oversight role, the VP, FP&A will be in the models directly, building and stress-testing scenarios, and translating the numbers into decisions. Reporting to the CFO, this person will be a key partner to executive leadership and business unit owners, and will play a central role in the company's next chapter of growth.

 We're looking for someone who wants to build, not just review, someone as comfortable inside the mechanics of a model as they are presenting its output to the CFO and board. 

 Key Responsibilities: 

 10+ years of progressive finance experience, including FP&A leadership, with a track record of being genuinely hands-on in the model — not several layers removed from it.

 Direct experience in a SaaS or recurring-revenue business, fluent in ARR, NRR, churn, cohort, and unit economics analysis.

 Strong financial modeling and scenario-planning skills — able to build complex models from scratch and pressure-test assumptions in real time.

 Exposure to an exit, sale process, recapitalization, refinancing, or similar transaction, with a working understanding of what "diligence-ready" actually looks like.

 Executive presence — able to move fluidly between deep model work and clear, confident presentation to the CFO and board.

 Strong judgment about what's urgent, what's important, and what can wait — able to prioritize across competing asks from the CFO, business leaders, and the sponsor.

 Nice-to-haves: 

 M&A diligence or post-acquisition integration experience.

 CPA, CFA, or MBA.

 Prior experience building or scaling an FP&A function from a less mature state.

 Compensation: 

 In the spirit of transparency, we are excited to share the base salary for this position is $200,000 - $240,000 USD and $185,000 - $225,000 CAD and exclusive of fringe benefits or potential bonuses. If you are hired at ClearGov, your final base salary compensation will be determined by factors such as skills, interview performance, education and/or experience. In addition to those factors, we believe in the importance of pay equity and consider internal equity of our current team members as a part of any final offer. Please keep in mind that the range mentioned above is the full base salary for the role. Hiring beyond the base range would not be typical in order to allow for future & continued salary growth. We also offer a generous compensation and benefits package (more information on benefits listed below).

 Why Join ClearGov 

 Remote and flexible work environment

 Meaningful work that impacts communities across the United States

 Collaborative, high-performing team

 Competitive compensation and benefits

 Opportunities to grow as we scale 

 Benefits 

 Medical, dental & vision insurance

 FSA, HSA, and/or Dependent Care FSA (US)

 Life + AD&D insurance, plus short-term and long-term disability insurance (US)

 Life + disability insurance (Canada)

 401(k) (US) / RRSP (Canada) with 3.5% match

 10 company holidays

 3 wellness days

 Paid vacation time off

 Sick and safe time off

 Paid parental leave

 Paid bereavement leave

 Paid jury duty + civic service leave

 Employee assistance program

 2 summer days + annual end-of-year "Dimming of the Lights"

 Employee referral bonus program

 How to Apply 
Ready to join us? Apply online today! 

 Equal Opportunity Employer 
ClearGov is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion. We prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind based on race, color, sex, religion, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, age, or any other protected characteristic. Hiring decisions are based solely on qualifications, merit, and business needs.

jobs.title: Director, Enterprise AI Strategy & Transformation
jobs.description:
JOB PURPOSE 
 Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, the Director, Enterprise AI Strategy & Transformation leads the development and execution of the organization’s enterprise AI strategy and transformation agenda to drive measurable business value, productivity, operational efficiency, innovation, and informed decision-making. The role serves as the organization’s AI subject matter expert and enterprise coordinating point, providing strategic guidance on AI opportunities, investments, governance, risk, technology, adoption, and value realization. 

 The Director partners with business and functional leaders to identify, prioritize, and implement AI and intelligent automation opportunities aligned with organizational objectives and financial goals. The role initially focuses on leveraging AI to enhance financial and operational performance, including forecasting, reporting, analysis, productivity, workflow efficiency, cost management, and decision-making, with successful capabilities and practices progressively expanded across other functions. The Director oversees the enterprise AI portfolio and lifecycle from opportunity assessment and business case development through solution selection, implementation, adoption, benefits realization, ongoing monitoring, and retirement. 

 KEY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 
 AI Strategy, Portfolio & Value Management Develop and maintain the enterprise AI strategy, operating model, portfolio, and roadmap aligned with corporate objectives and financial goals. 
 Identify, evaluate, and prioritize AI opportunities based on strategic alignment, business value, cost, complexity, data readiness, risk, and organizational readiness. 
 Develop business cases, investment recommendations, and implementation roadmaps, including build, buy, configure, or partner options. 
 Establish performance measures, baseline metrics, and value-realization frameworks to track AI adoption, ROI, productivity, cost savings, revenue impact, and other business outcomes. 
 Provide executive leadership with visibility into AI investments, performance, realized benefits, opportunities, and risks. 
 AI Solution Development & Implementation Lead the evaluation, design, development, and deployment of AI solutions across enterprise productivity, function-specific applications, intelligent automation, advanced AI, and emerging agentic capabilities. 
 Partner with business units and end users to identify opportunities, develop practical AI-enabled solutions, and improve processes and ways of working. 
 Oversee AI pilots, proofs of concept, and enterprise implementations through the full lifecycle—from opportunity identification and feasibility through deployment, adoption, benefits realization, monitoring, and retirement. 
 Coordinate with Cybersecurity, Human Resources and other stakeholders to ensure solutions are appropriately designed, implemented, adopted, and measured. 
 Assess solution performance and recommend whether initiatives should be scaled, enhanced, consolidated, paused, or retired based on business value, adoption, cost, and risk. 
 AI Governance, Risk & Responsible Adoption Establish and maintain enterprise AI governance frameworks, policies, standards, controls, and risk-based processes to support responsible AI adoption. 
 Ensure AI initiatives are appropriately assessed for cybersecurity, privacy, data, intellectual property, legal, ethical, third-party, model, and business continuity risks. 
 Maintain an enterprise inventory of approved AI technologies, platforms, models, agents, and material use cases, with appropriate review, approval, testing, human oversight, monitoring, and escalation requirements. 
 Ensure data quality, classification, access, security, information governance, and regulatory requirements are addressed before AI solutions are deployed. 
 Monitor the evolving AI landscape, regulatory expectations, and associated risks, and update governance practices as required. 
 Enterprise AI Adoption & Change Management Lead enterprise AI literacy, adoption, and change-management initiatives across executives, leaders, employees, technical teams, and advanced AI users. 
 Develop and deliver role- and function-specific training, guidance, and resources to promote effective and responsible use of AI. 
 Serve as the enterprise resource for AI strategy, best practices, use-case guidance, and adoption support. 
 Measure AI utilization, adoption, training effectiveness, employee feedback, and business outcomes to continuously improve AI enablement. 
 Coordinate internal subject matter experts, technology teams, business stakeholders, and external partners to support successful AI adoption 
 Vendor, Technology & Partner Management Evaluate AI technologies, vendors, consultants, platforms, and implementation partners against business requirements, value, security, architecture, scalability, risk, and total cost of ownership. 
 Manage AI technology and vendor relationships to ensure service quality, effective implementation, and value realization. 
 Maintain oversight of the enterprise AI technology portfolio to identify duplicate capabilities, unnecessary licensing, overlapping solutions, and opportunities for consolidation. 
 Monitor emerging AI technologies—including generative AI, large language models, predictive AI, intelligent automation, computer vision, and agentic AI—and assess their practical business applicability and potential value. 
 QUALIFICATIONS, SKILLS, AND EDUCATIONAL REQUIREMENTS 
  Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field; Master’s degree preferred. 
 Minimum seven (7) years of progressive experience in AI, data analytics, digital transformation, automation, technology, or related fields, including significant experience leading enterprise AI or generative AI adoption. 
 Proven experience leading complex, enterprise-wide AI or business transformation initiatives from strategy and business case development through implementation, adoption, scaling, and measurable value realization. 
 Strong business and financial acumen, including experience with budgeting, forecasting, reporting, business case development, technology investment evaluation, performance measurement, and ROI. 
 Strong knowledge of AI technologies, including generative AI, machine learning, predictive analytics, intelligent automation, large language models, AI agents, and emerging AI capabilities, with an understanding of data, cybersecurity, privacy, and AI governance. 
 Strong strategic thinking, analytical, communication, stakeholder management, project management, and change management skills, with the ability to translate complex technology into practical business solutions and influence cross-functional decisions.  
 Strong technical and business judgment to evaluate AI solutions, vendors, risks, data and technology dependencies, and investment decisions. Professional certifications in AI, analytics, project management, responsible AI, or AI governance are considered an asset. 

 PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND WORKING CONDITIONS Standard office setting - hybrid arrangement (4 days in-office) 
 Fast paced office environment 
 Travel expectations between facilities in Mississauga and North York

jobs.title: CFO/VP Finance
jobs.description:
Vice President, Finance and 
Administration / Chief Financial Officer

Division: Finance and Administration

Reports To: President

Direct Reports:

• Controller

• Executive Director, Procurement and Administrative Services

• Executive Director, Public Safety

• Executive Director, Facilities Management

• Internal Auditor

 Position Summary 

Our post-secondary education client is seeking an accomplished and 
strategic financial executive to serve as its next Vice 
President, Finance and Administration / Chief Financial Officer.

As the chief financial and administrative officer and a member 
of the President’s Cabinet, the CFO provides executive 
leadership, strategic direction, and institutional stewardship 
for the school's financial operations, administrative services, 
public safety, and facilities.

This position ensures the responsible management of 
institutional resources while advancing the school's mission, 
vision, and strategic priorities. Serving as a trusted advisor 
to the President, the CFO helps shape institutional strategy, 
provides sound financial counsel, and partners with executive 
leadership to maintain the school's fiscal strength, operational 
effectiveness, and long-term sustainability.

The successful candidate will bring an institution-wide 
perspective and contribute to college-wide initiatives, 
organizational culture, governance, strategic planning, and 
executive decision-making.

 Executive Leadership Philosophy 

The school's Vice Presidents serve as institutional leaders 
first and functional leaders second. As members of the 
President’s Cabinet, they share responsibility for advancing the 
school's mission through collaborative leadership, strategic 
planning, innovation, and responsible stewardship of public 
resources.

The CFO will balance financial discipline with innovation, 
operational excellence with exceptional customer service, and 
long-term sustainability with the evolving needs of students, 
employees, and the community.

Success will be measured not only by the performance of assigned 
departments, but also by meaningful contributions to the overall 
effectiveness, reputation, and future of the college.

 Core Executive Responsibilities 

 Cabinet and Strategic Leadership 

• Serve as an active member of the President’s Cabinet and 
executive leadership team.

• Advise the President on strategic, financial, operational, and 
organizational matters.

• Participate in institutional planning, executive 
decision-making, and policy development.

• Collaborate across divisions to advance college-wide 
initiatives and strategic priorities.

• Represent the school before governmental agencies, financial 
institutions, professional organizations, and community 
partners.

• Develop long-range financial and operational strategies that 
support the school’s Strategic Plan.

• Evaluate emerging trends, risks, and opportunities affecting 
higher education and public finance.

• Champion innovation, continuous improvement, and responsible 
resource management.

 Organizational Leadership 

• Recruit, develop, mentor, and evaluate executive leaders and 
management staff.

• Build high-performing teams committed to operational 
excellence and continuous improvement.

• Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, inclusion, 
professionalism, and exceptional customer service.

• Promote employee engagement, leadership development, and 
succession planning.

• Establish measurable goals and performance expectations 
aligned with institutional priorities.

 Stewardship and Governance 

• Ensure responsible stewardship of the college’s financial, 
physical, and operational resources.

• Support the Board of Regents through executive reports, 
recommendations, and presentations.

• Develop and implement policies, administrative regulations, 
and business practices that strengthen institutional 
effectiveness.

• Ensure compliance with federal and state laws, accreditation 
standards, Board policies, and administrative regulations.

• Maintain effective systems of internal control, enterprise 
risk management, and institutional accountability.

 Division Leadership Responsibilities 

 Financial Leadership 

• Serve as the college’s chief financial officer and principal 
advisor to the President on financial strategy, fiscal 
sustainability, and institutional stewardship.

• Provide executive leadership for all financial operations, 
ensuring the integrity, transparency, and long-term health of 
the college’s financial resources.

• Deliver financial analysis and recommendations that support 
informed decision-making by the President, Cabinet, and Board of 
Regents.

• Through the Controller and Finance team, provide strategic 
oversight for:

• Budget development and administration

• Accounting and financial reporting

• Payroll administration

• Treasury, cash, investment, and debt management

• Annual financial audits and internal controls

• Financial forecasting and analysis

• Grant accounting and financial compliance

• State and federal financial reporting

• Financial systems and business process improvement

 Procurement and Administrative Services 

• Provide executive leadership for procurement and 
administrative support operations, ensuring services are 
efficient, compliant, transparent, and customer-focused.

• Promote responsible stewardship of public resources while 
supporting operational effectiveness and service to the college 
community.

• Through the Executive Director of Procurement and 
Administrative Services, oversee:

• Purchasing and procurement

• Contract administration and competitive solicitations

• Vendor relations

• Administrative services

• Auxiliary enterprises, including the campus bookstore, café, 
and merchandise store

• Shipping and receiving

 Facilities Management 

• Provide strategic leadership for the planning, maintenance, 
operation, preservation, and improvement of the college’s 
physical assets and campus environment.

• Ensure facilities remain safe, functional, attractive, and 
supportive of teaching, learning, student engagement, and 
community use.

• Through the Executive Director of Facilities Management, 
oversee:

• Facilities maintenance and operations

• Custodial services and utilities management

• Preventive and deferred maintenance

• Capital improvement, construction, and renovation projects

• Campus infrastructure

• Sustainability initiatives

• Space utilization and facilities planning

 Public Safety 

• Provide executive oversight of the school’s public safety and 
emergency preparedness functions, fostering a secure environment 
for learning and institutional operations.

• Collaborate with institutional leadership and external 
agencies to maintain a comprehensive approach to campus safety 
and emergency management.

• Through the Executive Director of Public Safety, oversee:

• Campus security

• Emergency preparedness and response

• Business continuity planning

• Safety compliance

• Threat assessment and risk mitigation

• Emergency communications and crisis response

 Minimum Qualifications 

 Required 

• Chartered Professional Accountant designation in good 
standing.

• Master’s degree in Business Administration, Finance, 
Accounting, Public Administration, Higher Education 
Administration, or a closely related field.

• At least eight years of progressively responsible executive 
leadership experience in finance and administration.

• At least three years of senior leadership experience within 
higher education, government, or another similarly complex 
organization.

• Demonstrated experience leading multiple administrative 
divisions and managing complex organizational budgets.

• Demonstrated ability to provide strategic leadership, manage 
organizational change, and build collaborative relationships 
across a complex organization.

 Preferred 

• Experience within an Ontario college or public higher 
education institution.

• Experience with public-sector budgeting, capital planning, and 
community college funding.

 Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities 

The successful candidate will demonstrate the ability to:

• Provide visionary executive leadership while maintaining 
strong fiscal stewardship.

• Develop and communicate long-term financial strategies that 
advance institutional priorities.

• Analyze complex financial and operational issues and develop 
practical, sustainable solutions.

• Build collaborative relationships across the institution and 
with external stakeholders.

• Lead organizational change with transparency, professionalism, 
and integrity.

• Interpret and apply applicable laws, regulations, accounting 
standards, and Board policies.

• Communicate effectively with the President, Board of Regents, 
executive leadership, faculty, staff, students, governmental 
officials, and community partners.

• Lead multiple complex operational areas while maintaining an 
institution-wide perspective.

• Develop high-performing leadership teams through coaching, 
mentoring, and succession planning.

• Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, collaboration, 
continuous improvement, and exceptional customer service.

• Exercise sound judgment and maintain the highest standards of 
ethics, professionalism, and confidentiality.
